worked.description_before: Charge-state-summed number density of argon ions, including Ar+ through Ar18+ and excluding neutral argon; local and averaged forms share this definition.
worked.description_after: Number density of argon ions across all charged ionization states, excluding neutral argon. It is the general argon-ion concentration shared by its local and spatially averaged forms.
worked.documentation_before:
Argon density is the number of argon ions per unit volume, summed over all ionization stages from singly charged Ar+ through fully stripped Ar18+. Neutral argon is excluded.

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ar}} = \sum_{Z=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{Z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the total argon-ion number density, $Z$ is the integer argon charge state, and $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{Z+}}$ is the number density of argon ions in that charge state.

The definition applies to a local value and to averages over a specified chord or confined plasma volume, including the [line-averaged argon density](name:line_averaged_argon_density) and [volume-averaged argon density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density). It is distinct from argon count, which represents an equivalent-electron inventory rather than particles per volume.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of argon. The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

The charge-state sum is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ar}} = \sum_{q=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the argon-ion number density, $q$ is the positive integer charge-state index, $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is the number density of argon ions in charge state $q$, and 18 is the atomic number of argon.

The quantity may be specified locally or as a spatial average, with the averaging domain set by the specific form. The [line-averaged argon density](name:line_averaged_argon_density) is the average along a specified plasma path, and the [volume-averaged argon density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density) is the average over the confined plasma volume. Both are averages of the local density, not unnormalized line or volume integrals, and both keep the same charge-state-summed ion population.

This quantity is not the argon inventory or count, which is an amount rather than a concentration per unit volume, and it is not an electron density or a density of any other species.

worked.name: beryllium_density
worked.description_before: Local number density of beryllium impurity ions per unit plasma volume, summed over all ionization states from singly ionized to fully stripped (Be1+ through Be4+), excluding neutral beryllium atoms.
worked.description_after: Number density of beryllium ions across all positive charge states, excluding neutral beryllium, expressing their concentration per physical plasma volume.
worked.documentation_before:
Beryllium (atomic number $Z = 4$) enters the plasma primarily through sputtering or evaporation from beryllium first-wall surfaces. The local beryllium ion number density $n_\mathrm{Be}$ aggregates contributions from all four charged ionization stages:

$$
n_\mathrm{Be} = \sum_{z=1}^{4} n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}$ is the number density of beryllium ions in charge state $z+$, with $z$ running from 1 (singly ionized) to 4 (fully stripped). Neutral beryllium atoms are excluded from this sum.

Beryllium impurity content is inferred from passive spectroscopy of beryllium emission lines or from active charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy, with spatially resolved profiles reconstructed by tomographic inversion of chord-integrated measurements. Spatially averaged representations include [line_averaged_beryllium_density](name:line_averaged_beryllium_density) along a diagnostic chord and [volume_averaged_beryllium_density](name:volume_averaged_beryllium_density) integrated over the confined plasma volume. The relative impurity abundance with respect to the electron population is characterized by the ratio_of_beryllium_density_to_electron_density.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of beryllium. The underlying local density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Be}} = \frac{d\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{Be}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the beryllium-ion number density, $\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the beryllium-ion count, and $V$ is physical volume.

Spatial averaging is not intrinsic to the unqualified density. The [line-averaged beryllium density](name:line_averaged_beryllium_density) is its path integral divided by the chord length, whereas the [volume-averaged beryllium density](name:volume_averaged_beryllium_density) is its volume integral divided by the confined plasma volume. In contrast, [beryllium density at the magnetic axis](name:beryllium_density_at_magnetic_axis) specifies a local evaluation rather than a spatial average.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: deuterium_density
worked.description_before: Deuterium density is the number density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion population. It is the local density of deuterons, excluding neutral atoms, molecules, and line- or volume-averaged deuterium densities.
worked.description_after: Number density of deuterium ions gives the deuteron concentration per physical volume in the plasma fuel population. The ions of the species are counted over all charge states, with neutral atoms excluded.
worked.documentation_before:
Deuterium density is the number density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion population. As a species-level density it is charge-state-summed over ionized atomic charge states; for deuterium this reduces to the singly ionized deuteron population.

The local deuterium density is defined by the charge-state sum

$$
n_D = \sum_{q>0} n_{\mathrm{D}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_D$ is the deuterium density, $q$ is the positive atomic charge state, and $n_{\mathrm{D}^{q+}}$ is the number density of deuterium ions in charge state $q$.

Neutral deuterium atoms, molecular deuterium, and non-deuterium species are excluded. This quantity is local; spatial aggregations such as [line-averaged deuterium density](name:line_averaged_deuterium_density) and [volume-averaged deuterium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density) are distinct quantities.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of deuterium. The underlying local concentration is the zeroth velocity-space moment:

$$
n_{\mathrm D} = \int f_{\mathrm D}(\mathbf v)\,\mathrm d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm D}$ is the deuterium-ion number density, $f_{\mathrm D}$ is the local deuteron velocity distribution, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity, and $\mathrm d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The integral covers the full velocity space.

No particular evaluation location or spatial averaging operation is prescribed. The [line-averaged deuterium density](name:line_averaged_deuterium_density) is the chord-length mean of this concentration, whereas the [volume-averaged deuterium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density) is its mean over the plasma volume.

Molecular deuterium and other ion species do not contribute. Unlike [deuterium–tritium density](name:deuterium_tritium_density), this quantity does not combine the two fuel isotopes. It supplies the denominator of the tritium-to-deuterium density ratio, which expresses isotope composition rather than an absolute concentration.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: deuterium_tritium_density
worked.description_before: Deuterium-tritium density is the local ion number density of the deuterium-tritium fuel-ion pseudo-species, treating deuterium and tritium as one effective species.
worked.description_after: Number density of deuterium–tritium fuel ions treated as one effective species, including all ionic charge states but excluding neutral atoms.
worked.documentation_before:
Deuterium-tritium density is the local ion number density of the deuterium-tritium fuel-ion pseudo-species, treating deuterium and tritium ions as one effective species. It is a species-level per-volume particle count summed over all ion charge states.

The defining relation is the sum of the component fuel-ion number densities:

$$
n_{DT} = n_D + n_T
$$

where $n_{DT}$ is the deuterium-tritium density, $n_D$ is the [deuterium density](name:deuterium_density), and $n_T$ is the [tritium density](name:tritium_density). Each component density is charge-state-summed over the corresponding ion charge states; the dimensionless tritium fraction, where used, is $f_T = n_T/n_{DT}$.

This quantity includes only deuterium and tritium fuel ions represented by the effective deuterium-tritium species. Neutral deuterium or tritium atoms, neutral molecules such as D$_2$, T$_2$, and DT, reaction products, and impurity ions are excluded. As a number density, its value domain is $n_{DT} \ge 0$.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of deuterium tritium. The effective-species density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{DT}} = n_{\mathrm{D}} + n_{\mathrm{T}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the combined deuterium–tritium ion number density, $n_{\mathrm{D}}$ is the [deuterium-ion number density](name:deuterium_density), and $n_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the tritium-ion number density.

This is a fuel-population density, not a fusion-reaction rate. It implies no fixed deuterium-to-tritium mixing ratio and prescribes neither a particular location nor a spatial averaging measure.

The [line-averaged form](name:line_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density) averages this concentration along a specified chord, whereas the [volume-averaged form](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density) averages it over a specified volume. Both retain the same effective fuel-species definition.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: deuterium_tritium_density_flux_surface_averaged_at_plasma_boundary
worked.description_before: Flux-surface-averaged number density of deuterium-tritium pseudo-species ions at the plasma boundary (separatrix).
worked.description_after: Flux-surface-averaged number density of deuterium-tritium pseudo-species ions at the plasma boundary (separatrix).
worked.documentation_before:
Flux-surface-averaged number density of deuterium-tritium pseudo-species ions at the plasma boundary (separatrix) is the particle density of the effective deuterium-tritium fuel species averaged over the last closed magnetic flux surface. The pseudo-species represents the deuterium-tritium fuel mixture as a single ion constituent with effective mass number 2.5; as a species-level density, it is summed over all charge states.

Using the poloidal-contour representation of a flux-surface average in an axisymmetric equilibrium, the boundary value is defined by:

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}} \rangle_b =
\frac{\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} n_{\mathrm{DT}}(l)\, dl / B_p(l)}
{\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} dl / B_p(l)}
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}} \rangle_b$ is this boundary average, $\psi_b$ labels the plasma-boundary flux surface, $l$ is poloidal arc length along that surface, and $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude. The local pseudo-species density is $n_{\mathrm{DT}} = n_{\mathrm{D}} + n_{\mathrm{T}}$, where $n_{\mathrm{D}}$ and $n_{\mathrm{T}}$ are the corresponding charge-state-summed deuterium and tritium ion densities.

This quantity is the plasma-boundary member of [flux-surface-averaged deuterium-tritium density](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary) and the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of [deuterium-tritium density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary), which retains variation around the same boundary surface. The single-isotope boundary analog [flux-surface-averaged deuterium density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary) separates one isotope contribution, while [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density) averages the same effective fuel population over the confined-plasma volume. It excludes scrape-off-layer and material-limiter densities, including [deuterium-tritium density at a limiter](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_limiter).

worked.name: difference_of_total_plasma_heating_power_and_time_derivative_of_plasma_stored_energy
worked.description_before: Instantaneous plasma power available for confinement losses after correcting total coupled heating for the rate of change of stored plasma energy.
worked.description_after: Difference of total plasma heating power and the time derivative of plasma stored energy, giving the instantaneous power available for confinement losses.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the instantaneous global power-balance residual available to account for energy leaving the plasma confinement system. It corrects the total plasma heating power for transient changes in the plasma’s stored energy.

It is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{loss}} = P_{\mathrm{heat,total}} - \frac{dW_{\mathrm{plasma}}}{dt}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{loss}}$ is the power-balance residual represented by this quantity, $P_{\mathrm{heat,total}}$ is the total plasma heating power, $W_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the total stored energy of the plasma, and $t$ is time.

The quantity is global and aggregated over all heating contributions included in total plasma heating power and over the complete stored plasma-energy reservoir. It is not the heating input itself, a single-source heating contribution, or a regional radiation measurement; [radiated power over the core region](name:radiated_power_over_core_region) is a specific loss channel rather than this balance residual. A positive value means heating exceeds the instantaneous increase in stored energy, while a negative value means stored energy is increasing faster than the heating input.

This residual is the loss-power term in the conventional energy-confinement relation $\tau_E = W_{\mathrm{plasma}}/P_{\mathrm{loss}}$, where $\tau_E$ is the energy confinement time; transient storage changes are therefore excluded from the inferred loss power rather than counted as losses.
worked.documentation_after:
Difference of total plasma heating power and the time derivative of plasma stored energy. This is the global loss-power term remaining after accounting for changes in the plasma energy inventory.

The defining power balance is

$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial t}$$

where $P_{\mathrm{loss}}$ is the instantaneous power available for confinement losses, $P_{\mathrm{heat,tot}}$ is the total heating power coupled to the plasma, $W_p$ is the plasma stored energy, and $t$ is time.

Both operands must refer to the same whole-plasma region and included energy populations. Total coupled heating is not generator power or launched power before coupling. The stored-energy inventory is not restricted to thermal energy by this definition, and the resulting loss power is not restricted to radiation alone.

No steady-state assumption is required. For constant stored energy, the loss power equals the total coupled heating power. For the same energy inventory, it supplies the denominator in the energy confinement time relation $\tau_E = W_p/P_{\mathrm{loss}}$, where $\tau_E$ is the energy confinement time and the loss power must be positive.

$$a - b$$

The difference is one quantity minus another.

The time derivative is the rate of change of a quantity with time at a fixed point or label.

It is the averaged counterpart of the local [argon ion density](name:argon_density) and differs from the [volume-averaged argon density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density), which uses a plasma-volume average instead of an inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient-weighted surface average. worked.name: flux_surface_averaged_current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive
worked.description_before: Vector average on a magnetic flux surface of conventional plasma current density generated non-inductively by electromagnetic-wave–particle interactions, excluding inductive and non-wave current drive.
worked.description_after: Vector average over a closed magnetic flux surface of conventional plasma current density driven non-inductively by electromagnetic wave–particle interactions.
worked.documentation_before:
Flux-surface-averaged wave-driven current density is the vector average, on a magnetic flux surface, of the conventional plasma current density generated non-inductively by electromagnetic-wave–particle interactions. It retains the vector character of the local current-density contribution while averaging its resolved components over the surface.

The flux-surface average is defined componentwise by

$$
\left\langle \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{wd}} \right\rangle_{\psi}
=
\frac{\displaystyle\int_{S_{\psi}} \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{wd}}\,\frac{dS}{\lvert\nabla\psi\rvert}}
{\displaystyle\int_{S_{\psi}}\frac{dS}{\lvert\nabla\psi\rvert}}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{wd}}$ is the local conventional current-density vector generated by wave–particle interactions, $\psi$ is the scalar magnetic-flux label, $S_{\psi}$ is the corresponding magnetic flux surface, $dS$ is its surface-area element, and $\nabla\psi$ is the spatial gradient of the flux label.

The quantity applies to the plasma current on one magnetic flux surface and includes the wave-driven contributions of the charged-particle populations represented in the conventional current. Its aggregation convention is a complete flux-surface average, not a local value, volume average, toroidal current integral, or Fourier-mode-resolved contribution.

It excludes inductive current density and current contributions generated by bootstrap, ohmic, or other non-wave current-drive mechanisms. No field-aligned or other directional projection is imposed at this parent level.

This quantity is obtained by applying flux-surface averaging to the local [wave-driven current density](name:current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive). The parallel flux-surface-averaged wave-driven current density is a specialization that retains only the component projected along the magnetic-field direction before or within the averaging operation.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved current-density component points in the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ basis, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, consistent with conventional positive-charge transport.
worked.documentation_after:
Flux-surface-averaged wave-driven current density represents the net vector contribution generated non-inductively by electromagnetic wave–particle interactions. It retains the vector character of conventional plasma [current density](name:current_density), rather than selecting a directional projection.

The defining relation is

$$\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$$

where $\overline{\mathbf{j}}_{\mathrm{w}}$ is the averaged wave-driven current-density vector, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{w}}$ is the local [wave-driven current-density vector](name:current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive), and angle brackets denote the [flux-surface average](concept:flux_surface_averaged).

Unlike [flux-surface-averaged parallel current density due to wave-driven current drive](name:flux_surface_averaged_parallel_current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive), this quantity averages the vector itself without applying a magnetic-field projection or dividing by a reference vacuum toroidal field.

This quantity is the flux-surface average of the ion-mixture effective charge over the plasma boundary, identified with the last closed flux surface. It summarizes the charge composition across the complete boundary surface rather than at a single location.

$$
\left\langle Z_{\mathrm{eff}} \right\rangle_{\psi_b} = \frac{\oint_{\psi_b} Z_{\mathrm{eff}}\,d\ell/B_p}{\oint_{\psi_b} d\ell/B_p}, \qquad Z_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{\sum_i n_i Z_i^2}{n_e}
$$

Here $\psi_b$ labels the plasma-boundary flux surface, $d\ell$ is poloidal arc length, $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude, $n_i$ and $Z_i$ are the number density and charge number of ion population $i$, and $n_e$ is the electron number density. The linked effective charge at the plasma boundary denotes the corresponding local boundary quantity; this entry denotes its flux-surface average.
worked.documentation_after:
Effective charge of the ion mixture, flux-surface averaged at the plasma boundary, measures the charge-squared ionic content relative to the electron population.

The local quantity being averaged is defined by

$$
Z_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{\sum_a n_a Z_a^2}{n_e}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the local [effective charge at the plasma boundary](name:effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary), $n_e$ is the local electron number density, and $a$ indexes ionic populations distinguished by species and charge state. For each population, $n_a$ is its number density and $Z_a$ is its ionic charge number. The sum includes all ion species and all positive charge states; neutral particles do not contribute.

This quantity averages the local effective charge over the entire plasma-boundary surface rather than specifying a pointwise boundary value. Its defining operator composition is

where $g(\psi)$ is this geometric equilibrium coefficient, $R$ is major radius, $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic flux labeling the surface, and angle brackets denote the flux-surface average.

It differs from [flux-surface-averaged major radius](name:flux_surface_averaged_major_radius): averaging the reciprocal is not generally equivalent to taking the reciprocal after averaging. It also differs from [flux-surface-averaged inverse squared major radius](name:flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_square_of_major_radius), whose averaged quantity is the reciprocal square rather than the reciprocal.

worked.description_before: Flux-surface average of the reciprocal square of total magnetic-field strength, a geometric coefficient in neoclassical and flux-surface-averaged transport relations.
worked.description_after: Flux-surface average of the inverse square of total equilibrium magnetic-field magnitude, a geometric coefficient in neoclassical and flux-surface-averaged transport relations.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the flux-surface average of the reciprocal square of the total magnetic-field strength on a nested magnetic surface. It captures field-strength geometry independently of the magnetic-field direction.

The defining relation is

$$
\left\langle \frac{1}{|\mathbf{B}|^2} \right\rangle_\psi
=
\frac{\displaystyle \int_{S(\psi)} |\mathbf{B}|^{-2}\,\frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}
{\displaystyle \int_{S(\psi)} \frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}$ is the total magnetic-field vector, $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, $\psi$ is the flux-surface label, $S(\psi)$ is the magnetic surface labeled by $\psi$, $dS$ is its surface-area element, and $\nabla\psi$ is the spatial gradient of the flux-surface label.

The quantity applies to the complete magnetic flux surface and uses the inverse-$|\nabla\psi|$ weighting shown in the defining relation. It is not a pointwise inverse-square field value and has no selection by magnetic-field direction, component, species, or source.

It is the flux-surface-averaged transformation of the parent [inverse square of magnetic-field magnitude](name:inverse_of_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude), with the reciprocal square formed locally before averaging. It is distinct from [flux-surface-averaged magnetic-field magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_magnetic_field_magnitude) and [flux-surface-averaged square of magnetic-field magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude), because nonlinear inversion and squaring do not commute with surface averaging.
worked.documentation_after:
Flux-surface-averaged inverse-square magnetic-field magnitude is a magnetic-geometry coefficient for equilibrium and neoclassical transport relations. It applies to the total equilibrium field on each closed nested magnetic flux surface.

The coefficient is defined by

$$
\langle B^{-2}\rangle = \oint B^{-2}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $B$ is the total equilibrium magnetic-field magnitude, $B^{-2}$ is its local inverse square, $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic-flux label, $dS$ is the surface-area element, and $\nabla\psi$ is the gradient of the flux label. Both integrals extend over the closed magnetic flux surface labeled by $\psi$, and angle brackets denote the flux-surface average on that surface.

All magnetic-field components contribute through the total magnitude; no individual component is selected. The definition requires nonzero field magnitude and finite surface integrals.

This is the surface-averaged form of the [local inverse-square magnetic-field magnitude](name:inverse_of_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude), rather than its pointwise value. Squaring and inversion precede averaging: the result is generally neither the inverse square of the [surface-averaged field magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_magnetic_field_magnitude) nor the reciprocal of the [surface-averaged squared field magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude).

This quantity is the flux-surface average of the magnitude of the total equilibrium magnetic-field vector. It represents the mean field strength on a magnetic surface, rather than a component or a vector average.

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\left\langle \lvert\mathbf{B}\rvert \right\rangle_{\psi} = \frac{\oint_{\psi} \lvert\mathbf{B}\rvert\,\mathrm{d}S/\lvert\nabla\psi\rvert}{\oint_{\psi} \mathrm{d}S/\lvert\nabla\psi\rvert}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}$ is the total equilibrium magnetic-field vector, $\psi$ is the scalar label of the magnetic flux surface, $\mathrm{d}S$ is the surface-area element, and $\nabla\psi$ is the spatial gradient of that surface label. The aggregation is the normalized surface integral with weighting $\mathrm{d}S/\lvert\nabla\psi\rvert$.

The quantity applies to all components of the equilibrium field on the selected magnetic flux surface and is non-negative. It excludes any signed field component, any species or source decomposition, and the magnitude of a vector obtained by averaging $\mathbf{B}$ before taking its modulus.

It differs from [flux-surface-averaged square of magnetic-field magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude), which averages the squared field strength rather than the field strength itself.
worked.documentation_after:

$$
\langle B\rangle = \oint B\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $B$ is the local total [magnetic-field magnitude](name:magnetic_field_magnitude), $\langle B\rangle$ is its flux-surface average, $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic-flux label, $\nabla\psi$ is the gradient of that label, and $dS$ is the area element of the closed surface over which both integrals are taken.

All equilibrium magnetic-field components contribute to the local magnitude before averaging. This quantity is not a selected field component, a pointwise field strength, or the magnitude of a surface-averaged field vector. It is positive for a nonvanishing equilibrium field.

The [flux-surface-averaged squared magnetic-field magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude) instead averages the square of the local field strength. That second moment is not the square of this mean unless the field strength is constant over the surface.

Major radius is the nonnegative perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis to a geometric point or specified location. For this flux-surface-averaged quantity, that distance is averaged over each nested magnetic flux surface in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The flux-surface average of major radius is defined by

$$
\langle R\rangle_\psi = \frac{\oint_\psi R\,dl/B_p}{\oint_\psi dl/B_p}
$$

where $\langle R\rangle_\psi$ is the averaged major-radius coordinate, $\psi$ is the magnetic-flux label identifying the surface, $l$ is poloidal arc length along that surface, and $B_p$ is the magnitude of the poloidal magnetic field. The contour integral extends around the complete poloidal intersection of the nested magnetic flux surface.

This quantity applies to a complete magnetic flux surface and aggregates the local [major radius](name:major_radius) using the flux-surface weighting defined by the inverse poloidal-field magnitude. It is therefore distinct from pointwise major radius and contains no point-specific or localized evaluation.

The quantity is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of [major radius](name:major_radius). It must not be confused with [flux-surface-averaged inverse of major radius](name:flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_major_radius), which averages the reciprocal $1/R$ rather than averaging $R$ itself; consequently, it is not generally the reciprocal of that neighboring average.

Flux-surface-averaged parallel current density at a specified constraint position is the signed plasma current density associated with the component of conventional current flowing along the local magnetic field, averaged over the corresponding closed magnetic flux surface.

The defining field-aligned flux-surface average is

$$
j_{parallel}^{\mathrm{FS}}(\psi_c)=\frac{\left\langle\mathbf{j}\cdot\mathbf{B}\right\rangle_{\psi_c}}{B_0(\psi_c)}
$$

where $j_{\parallel}^{\mathrm{FS}}(\psi_c)$ is this averaged parallel current density, $\mathbf{j}$ is the conventional plasma current-density vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector, $\psi_c$ is the flux-surface label selected by the constraint position, $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi_c}$ denotes averaging over that magnetic flux surface, and $B_0(\psi_c)$ is the reference magnetic-field magnitude used to normalize the field-aligned projection.

The quantity applies to the total plasma current-density field on the selected closed magnetic surface, with all current-carrying populations and mechanisms included unless a narrower physical qualifier is supplied. Its aggregation is over the complete flux surface, so it is not a pointwise parallel current density.

It is not restricted to a particular current-drive mechanism and is therefore distinct from the [parallel current density due to ohmic current drive](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_ohmic_current_drive) and the parallel flux-surface-averaged current density due to wave-driven current drive.

The underlying vector quantity is [current density](name:current_density); this name applies its magnetic-field-aligned projection and then performs a flux-surface average. The toroidal flux-surface-averaged current density at a constraint position instead uses the geometric toroidal projection before averaging.

Sign convention: Positive when the conventional current-density vector has a component along the local magnetic-field vector.
worked.documentation_after:
Flux-surface-averaged parallel current density at the constraint position represents net conventional plasma current along the magnetic field, with magnetic-field weighting and a signed reference-field normalization.

The defining relation is:

$$\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$$

where $j_\parallel^{\mathrm{FS}}$ is this quantity, $\mathbf{j}$ is the conventional [current density](name:current_density), $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, and $j_\parallel^{\mathrm{loc}}$ is the local [parallel current density at the constraint position](name:parallel_current_density_at_constraint_position). Angle brackets denote the flux-surface average, and $B_0$ is the nonzero signed reference toroidal magnetic field. The reference field is positive along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the symmetry axis and $Z$ is vertical height.

This is the constraint-position specialization of [flux-surface-averaged parallel current density](name:flux_surface_averaged_parallel_current_density). It includes the signed contributions of all charged-particle populations and is not restricted to inductively driven current. It is not generally the simple flux-surface average of the local parallel component: the magnetic-field magnitude enters the numerator before division by the reference field.

Sign convention: Positive when the surface-averaged conventional current–magnetic-field dot product has the same sign as the reference toroidal magnetic field $B_0$.

The flux-surface average is the average of a quantity over a closed magnetic flux surface, weighted by the inverse magnitude of the poloidal flux gradient.

worked.name: flux_surface_averaged_parallel_current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive
worked.description_before: Parallel current density driven by a coherent wave, defined by a flux-surface-averaged magnetic-field projection divided by the reference vacuum toroidal field.
worked.description_after: Parallel current density driven non-inductively by a coherent wave, defined by the flux-surface-averaged current–magnetic-field dot product divided by the reference vacuum toroidal field.
worked.documentation_before:
Parallel current density on a closed magnetic flux surface represents the signed net plasma current contribution driven non-inductively by a specified coherent electromagnetic wave. Its definition averages a magnetic-field projection rather than simply averaging the local field-aligned current component.

The defining relation is

$$\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$$

where $\overline{j}_{\parallel}$ is this averaged parallel current density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{w}}$ is the conventional plasma-current-density vector attributed to the specified wave, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, and $B_0$ is the signed reference vacuum toroidal magnetic field, which must be nonzero.

The brackets denote the flux-surface average, $\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$, where $f$ is the quantity being averaged, $S$ is the closed magnetic flux surface, $dS$ is its surface-area element, $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic flux, and $\nabla\psi$ is its spatial gradient. Here the averaged quantity is the wave-driven current-density vector dotted with the magnetic field.

This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged specialization of [parallel current density due to wave-driven current drive](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive). It includes only the net contribution attributed to the specified coherent wave, excluding inductive current, bootstrap current, and contributions attributed to other waves or non-wave mechanisms. It is therefore not the aggregate [parallel current density due to all non-inductive drive](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_non_inductive_current_drive).

Unlike the [flux-surface-averaged wave-driven current-density vector](name:flux_surface_averaged_current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive), this quantity retains a signed magnetic-field projection rather than vector direction. The projection is formed before averaging and cannot generally be recovered by projecting the averaged vector.

Sign convention: Positive when the flux-surface-averaged wave-driven current projection onto the magnetic field has the same sign as the reference vacuum toroidal field $B_0$.
worked.documentation_after:
Parallel current density due to wave-driven current drive is a signed measure of the field-aligned conventional plasma current generated non-inductively by a coherent wave through wave–particle interactions.

The defining relation is

$$\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$$

where $J_{\parallel,\mathrm{w}}$ is the quantity defined here, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{w}}$ is the coherent-wave-driven conventional current-density vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the total magnetic field, $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, and $B_0$ is the nonzero signed reference vacuum toroidal magnetic field. The local [parallel wave-driven current density](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive), $j_{\parallel,\mathrm{w}}$, is the projection of that current-density vector along the local magnetic field. Angle brackets denote the [flux-surface average](concept:flux_surface_averaged).

This is the coherent-wave contribution to the [flux-surface-averaged parallel current density](name:flux_surface_averaged_parallel_current_density). The magnetic-field factor and reference-field divisor distinguish it from the flux-surface average of the local parallel projection alone. It excludes bootstrap current, the [inductive contribution](name:flux_surface_averaged_parallel_inductive_current_density), and contributions driven by other independent sources; it is a current density, not an enclosed current.

Sign convention: Positive when the surface-averaged current–magnetic-field dot product has the same sign as $B_0$. Positive $B_0$ points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The flux-surface average is the average of a quantity over a closed magnetic flux surface, weighted by the inverse magnitude of the poloidal flux gradient.

worked.name: flux_surface_averaged_parallel_electric_field_at_plasma_boundary
worked.description_before: Flux-surface average of the signed electric-field projection along the magnetic field, taken over the separatrix rather than at a single point.
worked.description_after: Signed flux-surface average of the electric–magnetic field dot product at the plasma boundary, divided by a reference magnetic-field value.
worked.documentation_before:
The flux-surface-averaged parallel electric field is the signed average of the electric-field projection along the local magnetic-field direction over the separatrix magnetic surface.

The defining flux-surface average is

$$
\left\langle E_\parallel \right\rangle_{\rm sep} = \frac{\displaystyle\oint_{\mathcal{C}_{\rm sep}} E_\parallel\,\frac{d\ell}{B}}{\displaystyle\oint_{\mathcal{C}_{\rm sep}}\frac{d\ell}{B}}
$$

where $\langle E_\parallel \rangle_{\rm sep}$ is the averaged quantity, $E_\parallel$ is the local projection of the electric field along the local magnetic field, $\mathcal{C}_{\rm sep}$ is the poloidal contour of the separatrix, $d\ell$ is the differential poloidal arc length, and $B$ is the magnitude of the local magnetic field. The subscript $\rm sep$ identifies the separatrix surface.

The quantity applies to the complete separatrix surface and uses the inverse-magnetic-field weighting intrinsic to a flux-surface average; it is not a pointwise value. It is the averaged counterpart of the local [parallel electric field at the separatrix](name:parallel_electric_field_at_separatrix), so local variation around the separatrix is combined rather than retained as a separate spatial value.

Sign convention: Positive when the electric field points along the local magnetic-field direction.
worked.documentation_after:
The flux-surface-averaged parallel electric field at the plasma boundary represents signed field-aligned electric forcing with magnetic-field weighting. It is a surface-aggregated quantity rather than a point-local boundary value.

The defining relation is

$$\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$$

where $\overline{E}_{\parallel,b}$ is this averaged quantity, $\mathbf{E}$ is the [electric field](name:electric_field), $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector, and $B_0$ is the specified nonzero reference magnetic-field value, constant over the averaging surface. The brackets denote flux-surface averaging, and the subscript $b$ identifies evaluation at the plasma boundary.

The point-local [parallel electric field at the plasma boundary](name:parallel_electric_field_at_plasma_boundary) is $E_\parallel=\mathbf{E}\cdot\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$, where $E_\parallel$ denotes that local projection and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is the local magnetic-field magnitude. Consequently, this quantity averages $|\mathbf{B}|E_\parallel$ and divides by $B_0$; it is not generally the direct surface average of $E_\parallel$. Unlike the [flux-surface-averaged parallel wave electric-field amplitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_parallel_wave_electric_field_amplitude), it retains signed contributions, allowing cancelation rather than averaging their amplitudes.

Sign convention: Positive when the flux-surface-averaged electric–magnetic field dot product and the reference magnetic-field value $B_0$ have the same sign.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi = \psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux; $\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

The flux-surface average is the average of a quantity over a closed magnetic flux surface, weighted by the inverse magnitude of the poloidal flux gradient.

worked.name: flux_surface_averaged_parallel_inductive_current_density
worked.description_before: Flux-surface-averaged parallel current density driven by an inductive electric field.
worked.description_after: Flux-surface-averaged parallel inductive current density is the mean inductive current–magnetic-field dot product divided by a signed reference toroidal magnetic field.
worked.documentation_after:
Flux-surface-averaged parallel inductive current density is the resistively driven contribution to conventional plasma [current density](name:current_density), assigned to a closed magnetic flux surface. It represents the plasma response to the inductive electric field along the magnetic field.

The defining relation is:

$$\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$$

where $j_{\parallel,\mathrm{ind}}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ is this surface-assigned quantity, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{ind}}$ is the inductively driven conventional current-density vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector, $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, and $B_0$ is the nonzero signed reference toroidal magnetic field. Angle brackets denote the flux-surface average. The local [parallel inductive current density](name:parallel_inductive_current_density), $j_{\parallel,\mathrm{ind}}$, is the projection of $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{ind}}$ along $\mathbf{B}$.

This definition applies to closed magnetic flux surfaces. Because of the magnetic-field factor and reference-field divisor, it is not simply the flux-surface average of the local parallel projection. It excludes bootstrap and other non-inductively driven contributions. With the same averaging and reference-field convention, adding the [non-inductive contribution](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_non_inductive_current_drive) gives the [total flux-surface-averaged parallel current density](name:flux_surface_averaged_parallel_current_density).

The reference field is signed along the toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is upward vertical height.

Sign convention: Positive when the surface-averaged inductive current–magnetic-field dot product has the same sign as $B_0$, with $B_0$ positive in the direction of increasing $\phi$.

The flux-surface average is the average of a quantity over a closed magnetic flux surface, weighted by the inverse magnitude of the poloidal flux gradient.

worked.name: flux_surface_averaged_parallel_wave_electric_field_amplitude
worked.description_before: Peak strength of the wave electric field along the equilibrium magnetic field, averaged over a closed magnetic flux surface with complex phase discarded.
worked.description_after: Strength of the field-aligned coherent-wave electric field after power-deposition-weighted complex averaging over a closed magnetic flux surface.
worked.documentation_before:
The flux-surface-averaged parallel wave electric-field amplitude is a surface mean of the local peak strength of the oscillating electric field along the equilibrium magnetic field. It retains amplitude information rather than the complex phase of the wave electric-field phasor.

The geometric flux-surface average of the local amplitude is

$$
\langle A_\parallel\rangle = \oint A_\parallel\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $A_\parallel$ is the local parallel wave electric-field amplitude, $\langle A_\parallel\rangle$ is its geometric flux-surface average, $S$ is the closed magnetic flux surface, $dS$ is its differential area, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux, and $\nabla\psi$ is its spatial gradient. The integrals cover the complete surface.

The [toroidal-mode-resolved member](name:per_toroidal_mode_flux_surface_averaged_parallel_wave_electric_field_amplitude) retains each toroidal Fourier mode separately and specifies additional power-deposition weighting. Its surface mean is $\langle w A_\parallel\rangle/\langle w\rangle$, where $w$ is the local power-deposition weight and $\langle w\rangle$ is its geometric flux-surface average, which must be nonzero. Toroidal-mode resolution is not required at this parent scope.

This quantity applies surface averaging to the local parallel wave electric-field amplitude; it is neither a volume integral nor a root-mean-square field. Averaging local amplitudes is distinct from averaging complex phasors before taking their magnitude, because phase cancelation is discarded. Unlike the [flux-surface-averaged parallel electric field at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_parallel_electric_field_at_plasma_boundary), it averages a nonnegative peak wave amplitude rather than a signed electric-field projection and is not restricted to the plasma boundary.
worked.documentation_after:
This quantity is the amplitude obtained after averaging the complex, magnetic-field-parallel component of a coherent-wave electric field over a closed magnetic flux surface. Local wave-power deposition supplies an additional weighting within the surface average.

The surface-representative complex field is defined by

$$\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$$

where $\overline{E}_{\parallel}$ is the deposition-weighted complex mean, $E_{\parallel}$ is the coherent-wave electric-field phasor projected along the local equilibrium magnetic field, $P_{\mathrm{dep}}$ is the [total absorbed wave power density](name:total_absorbed_wave_power_density), and angle brackets denote the flux-surface average. The requested amplitude is the modulus of this complex mean. The definition requires a nonzero denominator and a common phase reference for the phasors being averaged.

Complex averaging precedes removal of phase, so spatial phase differences can reduce the resulting amplitude. This differs from averaging the local parallel-wave electric-field amplitude, which removes relative phase information before aggregation. It describes only the field-aligned component, not the total electric-field strength.

The [toroidal-mode-resolved member](name:per_toroidal_mode_flux_surface_averaged_parallel_wave_electric_field_amplitude) applies this definition separately to each toroidal Fourier harmonic.

The amplitude is the peak magnitude of a sinusoidally varying quantity.

The flux-surface average is the average of a quantity over a closed magnetic flux surface, weighted by the inverse magnitude of the poloidal flux gradient.

worked.name: flux_surface_averaged_perpendicular_wave_vector
worked.description_before: Power-deposition-weighted mean of the wave number perpendicular to the local background magnetic field over a closed magnetic flux surface.
worked.description_after: Power-deposition-weighted mean wave-number magnitude perpendicular to the local background magnetic field over a closed magnetic flux surface.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the power-deposition-weighted mean of the perpendicular wave-number magnitude of a coherent plasma wave over a closed magnetic flux surface. The weighting emphasizes spatial phase variation where the wave transfers energy to the plasma.

It is defined by

$$\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$$

where $k_{\perp,\mathrm{dep}}$ is the weighted mean, $k_\perp$ is the local [perpendicular wave-number magnitude](name:perpendicular_wave_vector), and $P_{\mathrm{dep}}$ is the [total absorbed wave power density](name:total_absorbed_wave_power_density), the volumetric rate of energy transfer from the coherent wave to plasma particles.

Angle brackets denote the flux-surface average $\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$, where $f$ is the quantity being averaged, $S$ is the closed magnetic flux surface, $dS$ is its area element, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux, and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator. The denominator is therefore the [flux-surface-averaged total absorbed wave power density](name:flux_surface_averaged_total_absorbed_wave_power_density).

The result is a deposition-weighted surface mean, not an unweighted surface average or a volume integral, and is undefined when the denominator vanishes. Perpendicular refers to the local background magnetic field, not specifically to the flux-surface normal; the local quantity is a magnitude rather than a signed directional projection.

The declared unit is inconsistent with a wave number.
worked.documentation_after:
This quantity is the power-deposition-weighted mean of the local perpendicular wave-vector magnitude of a coherent plasma wave on a closed magnetic flux surface. Perpendicular is relative to the local background magnetic field; the local quantity is a magnitude, not a signed component or a projection along the flux-surface normal.

The flux-surface average is the average of a quantity over a closed magnetic flux surface, weighted by the inverse magnitude of the poloidal flux gradient. For each closed flux surface and each toroidal mode number, the average of the product of the local perpendicular wave vector and the local deposition density is

$$\langle k_\perp P_{\mathrm{dep}}\rangle = \oint k_\perp P_{\mathrm{dep}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$$

and the quantity is the ratio $k_{\perp,\mathrm{dep}} = \langle k_\perp P_{\mathrm{dep}}\rangle / \langle P_{\mathrm{dep}}\rangle$. Here $k_{\perp,\mathrm{dep}}$ is this deposition-weighted mean, $k_\perp$ is the local [perpendicular wave vector](name:perpendicular_wave_vector), $P_{\mathrm{dep}}$ is the local [total absorbed wave power density](name:total_absorbed_wave_power_density), $S$ is the closed magnetic flux surface, $dS$ is its area element, $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic flux, and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator.

The denominator $\langle P_{\mathrm{dep}}\rangle$ is the [flux-surface-averaged total absorbed wave power density](name:flux_surface_averaged_total_absorbed_wave_power_density), and the mean is defined only where it is nonzero. This is a deposition-weighted surface mean, not an unweighted flux-surface average of $k_\perp$ and not a volume integral.

worked.name: flux_surface_averaged_poloidal_magnetic_field_at_pedestal_top
worked.description_before: Poloidal magnetic field at the pressure pedestal top is the mean poloidal-plane field strength, weighted over the flux surface by the inverse poloidal-flux-gradient magnitude.
worked.description_after: Flux-surface-averaged poloidal magnetic-field magnitude at the pedestal top measures the equilibrium field strength excluding its toroidal component.
worked.documentation_before:
Poloidal magnetic field at the [pressure pedestal top](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal) is the average magnitude of the equilibrium magnetic-field projection onto the poloidal plane over the corresponding closed magnetic flux surface.

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle B_\mathrm{p}\rangle = \oint B_\mathrm{p}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $B_\mathrm{p}$ is the local [poloidal magnetic-field strength at the pedestal top](name:poloidal_magnetic_field_at_pedestal_top), $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic flux, $\nabla\psi$ is its spatial gradient, $dS$ is the surface-area element, and the angle brackets denote the flux-surface average. Both integrals extend over the entire closed pedestal-top flux surface, with inverse gradient-magnitude weighting.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $B_\mathrm{p}=\sqrt{B_R^2+B_Z^2}$, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical position, and $B_R$ and $B_Z$ are the radial and vertical components of the equilibrium [magnetic field](name:magnetic_field).

The poloidal-plane magnitude is formed locally before averaging; the result is neither a vector average nor a pointwise low-field-side or high-field-side value. Unlike the [flux-surface-averaged total magnetic-field magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_magnetic_field_magnitude), this quantity excludes the toroidal component before taking the magnitude and averaging.
worked.documentation_after:
Poloidal magnetic field at the [pedestal top](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal) is the [flux-surface average](concept:flux_surface_averaged) of the magnitude of the equilibrium [magnetic field](name:magnetic_field) projected onto the poloidal plane.

The local magnitude entering the average is

$$
B_\mathrm{p} = \sqrt{B_R^2+B_Z^2}
$$

where $B_\mathrm{p}$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude, and $B_R$ and $B_Z$ are the radial and vertical magnetic-field components in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged form of [poloidal_magnetic_field_at_pedestal_top](name:poloidal_magnetic_field_at_pedestal_top), aggregated over the closed magnetic flux surface at that locus rather than evaluated at a single point on its high-field or low-field side. The local magnitude is taken before averaging; it is not the magnitude of an averaged vector.

Unlike [flux_surface_averaged_magnetic_field_magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_magnetic_field_magnitude), which includes all equilibrium field components, this quantity excludes the toroidal contribution at every point.

The flux-surface average is the average of a quantity over a closed magnetic flux surface, weighted by the inverse magnitude of the poloidal flux gradient.

worked.name: flux_surface_averaged_ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude
worked.description_before: Flux-surface average of the squared toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient magnitude divided by the squared local magnetic-field magnitude, a metric coefficient for equilibrium geometry.
worked.description_after: Ratio of the squared gradient magnitude of the toroidal-flux radial coordinate to the squared total magnetic-field magnitude, averaged over a closed magnetic flux surface as an equilibrium metric coefficient.
worked.documentation_before:
This coefficient describes the flux-surface-averaged geometric weighting of a toroidal-flux radial coordinate by the inverse square of the local magnetic-field magnitude.

The defining relation is

$$
\mathcal{G}_B = \left\langle \frac{|\nabla \rho_{\mathrm{tor}}|^2}{|\mathbf{B}|^2} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $\mathcal{G}_B$ is the averaged metric coefficient, $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal-flux radial coordinate, $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes the average over a magnetic flux surface.

The quantity applies to nested equilibrium magnetic flux surfaces and uses the average of the pointwise ratio, not the ratio of separately averaged numerator and denominator. It is nonnegative because both the gradient magnitude and magnetic-field magnitude are squared.

It is the flux-surface-averaged form of the local [ratio of squared toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient magnitude to squared magnetic-field magnitude](name:ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude). It shares the gradient-squared geometric factor with the [flux-surface-averaged squared toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude), but additionally applies the pointwise inverse-square magnetic-field weighting before averaging. It is distinct from the corresponding major-radius denominator variant, [flux-surface-averaged ratio of squared toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient magnitude to squared major radius](name:flux_surface_averaged_ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_major_radius).
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of the squared magnitude of the toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient to the squared magnitude of the total magnetic field, averaged over a closed equilibrium magnetic flux surface, defines this equilibrium metric coefficient.

The coefficient is defined by

$$\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$$

where $\mathcal{G}_B$ is the metric coefficient, $\rho_\mathrm{tor}$ is the toroidal-flux radial coordinate, a radial flux label constant on each magnetic flux surface, and $\nabla\rho_\mathrm{tor}$ is its [spatial gradient](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient). The vector $\mathbf{B}$ is the total magnetic field, $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, and the subscript $\mathrm{FS}$ identifies the flux-surface average.

The quantity applies to each closed equilibrium magnetic flux surface and aggregates over that complete surface; it is not a pointwise value or an average across distinct surfaces. It has no species or particle-population restriction. The denominator uses the total magnetic-field magnitude, not only its toroidal or poloidal component.

The averaged integrand is the [local ratio of squared toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient magnitude to squared magnetic-field magnitude](name:ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude), so division occurs before averaging. Accordingly, this quantity is generally not the ratio of the [flux-surface-averaged squared gradient magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude) to the [flux-surface-averaged squared magnetic-field magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude), nor the product of the averaged squared gradient magnitude and the [flux-surface-averaged inverse squared magnetic-field magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude). Unlike the [major-radius-denominator variant](name:flux_surface_averaged_ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_major_radius), it weights the squared gradient by the inverse squared total magnetic-field magnitude.

The flux-surface average is the average of a quantity over a closed magnetic flux surface, weighted by the inverse magnitude of the poloidal flux gradient.

The magnitude is the Euclidean norm of a vector quantity, or the modulus of a complex one.

The ratio is one quantity divided by another.

The square is a scalar quantity multiplied by itself, or a vector's dot product with itself.

worked.name: flux_surface_averaged_ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_major_radius
worked.description_before: Flux-surface-averaged magnetic-geometry coefficient measuring the squared toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient relative to the squared major radius.
worked.description_after: Ratio of the squared toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient magnitude to squared major radius, averaged over a closed magnetic flux surface as an equilibrium metric coefficient.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is a magnetic-geometry metric coefficient that characterizes how a toroidal-flux radial coordinate varies across nested magnetic surfaces, with the variation weighted by inverse squared major radius.

It is defined by

$$
g_2 = \left\langle \frac{|\nabla \rho|^2}{R^2} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $g_2$ is the flux-surface-averaged metric coefficient, $\rho$ is the toroidal-flux radial coordinate, $\nabla\rho$ is its spatial gradient, $|\nabla\rho|$ is the gradient magnitude, $R$ is the major radius, and the subscript $\mathrm{FS}$ denotes the prescribed average over a complete magnetic flux surface.

The quantity applies to an equilibrium magnetic flux surface and represents an aggregate over that surface rather than a pointwise local value. It has no species, population, or transport-channel restriction.

It is the flux-surface average of the local ratio defined by [ratio of square of toroidal flux coordinate gradient magnitude to square of major radius](name:ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_major_radius). Unlike [flux-surface-averaged square of toroidal flux coordinate gradient magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude), it retains the inverse-square-major-radius weighting; the numerator is constructed from the [toroidal flux coordinate gradient magnitude](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude).
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of the squared magnitude of the toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient to squared major radius, averaged over a closed equilibrium magnetic flux surface, defines this geometric metric coefficient.

The coefficient is defined by

$$\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$$

where $\mathcal{G}_R$ is the metric coefficient, $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal-flux radial coordinate, and $\nabla\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is its [spatial gradient](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient). The coordinate is constant on each magnetic flux surface. The quantity $R$ is the major radius, measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes the flux-surface average.

The quantity applies to each closed equilibrium magnetic flux surface and aggregates over that complete surface; it is neither a pointwise value nor an average across distinct surfaces. It describes magnetic geometry without species or particle-population weighting. The denominator is squared major radius, not squared magnetic-field magnitude.

This quantity is the surface-averaged squared strength of the total magnetic field on a nested magnetic flux surface. It is a geometric metric coefficient used in equilibrium descriptions and in bounce-averaged and neoclassical transport relations.

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\left\langle B^2 \right\rangle_\psi = \frac{\displaystyle\oint_{S(\psi)} \frac{B^2}{\lvert\nabla\psi\rvert}\,dS}{\displaystyle\oint_{S(\psi)} \frac{1}{\lvert\nabla\psi\rvert}\,dS}
$$

where $B^2$ is the [square of the magnetic-field magnitude](name:square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude), $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic-flux label of the surface, $S(\psi)$ is the closed magnetic flux surface with that label, $\nabla\psi$ is the gradient of the flux label, and $dS$ is the surface-area element.

The quantity applies to the total equilibrium magnetic field, including all of its components, and is aggregated over each closed flux surface with the inverse-$\lvert\nabla\psi\rvert$ weighting shown above. It is not the pointwise value of $B^2$, the square of a flux-surface-averaged magnetic-field magnitude, or a single magnetic-field component.

It is the flux-surface-averaged form of [square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude](name:square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude). It differs from [flux_surface_averaged_magnetic_field_magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_magnetic_field_magnitude), which averages the field magnitude before squaring, and from [flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude), which averages its reciprocal.

worked.name: flux_surface_averaged_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude
worked.description_before: Flux-surface average of the squared magnitude of the gradient of the normalized toroidal-flux radius. It is the averaged contravariant radial metric coefficient for the flux coordinate rho_tor.
worked.description_after: Mean-square toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient over a closed equilibrium magnetic surface, describing the geometric spacing of neighboring magnetic surfaces.
worked.documentation_before:
Flux-surface average of the squared magnitude of the gradient of the toroidal flux coordinate is the average, over one magnetic flux surface, of the squared norm of $\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}$. It is the flux-surface-averaged contravariant radial metric coefficient associated with the radial coordinate in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho_\mathrm{tor}, \theta, \phi)$, where $\theta$ is a poloidal angle label and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle.

The quantity is defined by the flux-surface average of the local radial metric component:

$$
G_{\rho\rho}(\rho_\mathrm{tor}) = \left\langle |\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}|^2 \right\rangle_{\rho_\mathrm{tor}} = \frac{\int_{S(\rho_\mathrm{tor})} |\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}|^2\, dA / |\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}|}{\int_{S(\rho_\mathrm{tor})} dA / |\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}|}
$$

where $G_{\rho\rho}$ denotes this flux-surface-averaged metric coefficient, $\rho_\mathrm{tor}$ is the normalized toroidal-flux radius, $S(\rho_\mathrm{tor})$ is the magnetic flux surface with that label, $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator, $dA$ is the surface-area element, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\rho_\mathrm{tor}}$ denotes averaging over that flux surface.

The coordinate $\rho_\mathrm{tor}$ is constituted by $\rho_\mathrm{tor}=\sqrt{\Phi/\Phi_b}$, where $\Phi$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the flux surface and $\Phi_b$ is its value at the plasma boundary. The scope is closed nested equilibrium flux surfaces; the aggregation convention is an average over the entire surface at fixed $\rho_\mathrm{tor}$.

This is not the pointwise quantity $|\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}|^2$, not the flux-surface average of $|\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}|$, and not a volume or time average. It belongs to the same flux-surface-averaged geometric-metric family as the [flux-surface-averaged inverse major radius](name:flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_major_radius), but it characterizes the radial metric of the normalized toroidal-flux radius rather than a major-radius factor.

worked.name: flux_surface_averaged_time_averaged_normalized_energy_flux_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
worked.description_before: Normalized electrostatic energy flux across magnetic flux surfaces in a rotating frame, averaged over time and each surface and summed over perpendicular wavenumbers in nonlinear gyrokinetic turbulence.
worked.description_after: Electrostatic energy flux across magnetic flux surfaces in a rotating frame, normalized, time- and surface-averaged, and summed over perpendicular wavenumbers in nonlinear gyrokinetic turbulence.
worked.documentation_before:
Electrostatic energy flux across magnetic flux surfaces represents transport of particle energy by the E×B drift generated by the perturbed electrostatic potential. This quantity is evaluated in the rotating frame for nonlinear gyrokinetic turbulence, normalized, averaged over time and each closed flux surface, and summed over both perpendicular wavenumber components.

Flux-surface averaging applies inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient weighting to the [time-averaged normalized energy flux due to E×B drift](name:time_averaged_normalized_energy_flux_due_to_e_cross_b_drift):

$$
\langle \overline{\widehat{\Gamma}_W}\rangle = \oint \overline{\widehat{\Gamma}_W}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

Here $\Gamma_W$ is the electrostatic energy flux summed over perpendicular wavenumbers, with $W$ denoting particle energy in the rotating frame. Its normalized value is $\widehat{\Gamma}_W=\Gamma_W/\Gamma_{W,\mathrm{ref}}$, where $\Gamma_{W,\mathrm{ref}}$ is a positive reference energy flux whose specific scaling is convention-dependent. The overbar denotes the time average, angle brackets denote the flux-surface average, $S$ is the closed magnetic flux surface, $dS$ is its area element, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux, and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator.

The result remains associated with each magnetic flux surface; it is neither a volume-integrated energy transfer nor a time-accumulated transfer. The perpendicular spectral contributions are summed rather than retained individually. Only the electrostatic contribution is included, excluding electromagnetic contributions such as the [energy flux associated with the perturbed parallel vector potential](name:energy_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential).
worked.documentation_after:
Electrostatic energy flux across magnetic flux surfaces is the energy-transport contribution carried by the E×B drift associated with the perturbed electrostatic potential. This quantity applies to nonlinear gyrokinetic turbulence in a rotating frame and combines time averaging, flux-surface averaging, and summation over both perpendicular wavenumbers.

The combined aggregation is

$$\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$$

where $\Gamma_W^{\mathrm{av}}$ is the resulting normalized rotating-frame energy flux, $\Gamma_{W,k_x,k_y}(t)$ is the unaveraged normalized electrostatic energy-flux contribution at perpendicular wavenumber components $k_x$ and $k_y$, and $t$ is time. The bounds $t_1$ and $t_2$ delimit the averaging interval, the subscript $W$ denotes particle energy, and angle brackets denote the [flux-surface average](concept:flux_surface_averaged).

This is the flux-surface-averaged, perpendicular-wavenumber-summed rotating-frame member of [time-averaged normalized energy flux due to E×B drift](name:time_averaged_normalized_energy_flux_due_to_e_cross_b_drift). It retains the normalization of the [unaveraged normalized electrostatic energy flux](name:energy_flux_normalized_due_to_e_cross_b_drift). The wavenumber contributions are summed rather than averaged, while dependence on the magnetic flux surface is retained. Contributions attributed to the perturbed parallel vector potential or perturbed parallel magnetic field are excluded; this is not the total electromagnetic energy flux.

worked.name: flux_surface_averaged_time_averaged_normalized_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field_magnitude
worked.description_before: Normalized parallel magnetic-fluctuation magnitude in nonlinear gyrokinetic turbulence, averaged over time and flux surfaces, summed over kx, and resolved in ky.
worked.description_after: Flux-surface- and time-averaged normalized perturbed parallel magnetic-field magnitude is the amplitude of magnetic fluctuations along the equilibrium field, normalized by a reference field strength, in nonlinear gyrokinetic turbulence.
worked.documentation_before:
Flux-surface- and time-averaged normalized parallel magnetic-field perturbation magnitude measures compressional fluctuations along the local equilibrium magnetic field in nonlinear gyrokinetic turbulence. It retains dependence on one perpendicular wavenumber after summation over the other.

Let $a_\parallel(k_y)$ denote the time-averaged normalized parallel perturbation magnitude, summed over the perpendicular wavenumber $k_x$ at fixed perpendicular wavenumber $k_y$. The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle a_\parallel\rangle = \oint a_\parallel\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where angle brackets denote the flux-surface average, $S$ is the closed magnetic flux surface, $dS$ is its surface-area element, $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic-flux label, and $\nabla\psi$ is its spatial gradient. The surface integrals are evaluated at fixed $k_y$.

The normalized magnitude entering the averages is $|\delta B_\parallel|/B_{\mathrm{ref}}$, where $\delta B_\parallel$ is the magnetic perturbation projected along the local equilibrium field and $B_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference magnetic-field magnitude specified by the normalization convention. Time averaging applies over the specified averaging interval. The modulus is taken before averaging; this quantity is not the modulus of the averaged signed perturbation, a squared amplitude, or a turbulent transport flux. Summation over $k_x$ does not imply summation over $k_y$.

This is the flux-surface-averaged specialization of the [time-averaged normalized parallel magnetic-perturbation magnitude](name:time_averaged_normalized_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field_magnitude), with the wavenumber aggregation stated above. Unlike the [flux-surface-averaged magnetic-field magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_magnetic_field_magnitude), it describes only the normalized parallel perturbation, not the total equilibrium field strength.
worked.documentation_after:
Flux-surface- and time-averaged normalized perturbed parallel magnetic-field magnitude is the amplitude of the perturbed magnetic-field component along the local equilibrium field, normalized by a reference field magnitude. It characterizes parallel magnetic-compression fluctuations in nonlinear gyrokinetic turbulence.

For each resolved perpendicular spectral wavevector pair, the averaged normalized amplitude is

$$\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$$

Here $A$ is the averaged normalized amplitude, $k_x$ and $k_y$ are perpendicular spectral wavevector components, $t$ is time, and $B_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference magnetic-field magnitude used for normalization. The parallel perturbation $\delta B_\parallel$ is the projection of the perturbed [magnetic field](name:magnetic_field) along the local equilibrium-field direction. The overbar denotes a time average, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_\psi$ denotes the [flux-surface average](concept:flux_surface_averaged) on the closed magnetic flux surface labeled by the [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) $\psi$.

The spectral dependence is associated with $k_x$ and $k_y$: it may be resolved in both components or summed over $k_x$ at fixed $k_y$, retaining the dependence on $k_y$. The modulus is taken before the averages, so this is an average amplitude of the parallel perturbation, not a mean-square or root-mean-square amplitude. It excludes the equilibrium field and perpendicular perturbations.

This is the flux-surface-averaged form of the [time-averaged normalized perturbed parallel magnetic-field magnitude](name:time_averaged_normalized_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field_magnitude). The [normalized perturbed parallel magnetic-field magnitude](name:normalized_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field_magnitude) is the corresponding local normalized amplitude without these time and flux-surface averages.

This quantity is the flux-surface average of the time-averaged magnitude of the normalized magnetic-vector-potential perturbation in nonlinear gyrokinetic turbulence. The parallel component is the projection along the equilibrium magnetic field, and the magnitude is the modulus of the complex perturbation.

The defining flux-surface average is

$$
\langle \overline{|\widetilde A_\parallel|}\rangle = \oint \overline{|\widetilde A_\parallel|}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\widetilde A_\parallel$ is the normalized parallel vector-potential perturbation, the overbar denotes time averaging, and angle brackets denote flux-surface averaging. The integrals extend over the closed magnetic flux surface $S$, $dS$ is its area element, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux, and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator.

The result retains wavevector dependence: the surface and time averages do not imply summation over perpendicular wavevector components. It includes only the perturbation, not the equilibrium vector potential, and averages the magnitude rather than its square or the complex perturbation itself.

Its amplitude normalization is inherited from the underlying [normalized perturbation magnitude](name:normalized_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential_magnitude), rather than defined by the averaging operations.
worked.documentation_after:
This quantity describes the electromagnetic fluctuation amplitude associated with the perturbed magnetic vector potential parallel to the equilibrium magnetic field in nonlinear gyrokinetic turbulence. It is the flux-surface average of the [time-averaged normalized parallel-vector-potential magnitude](name:time_averaged_normalized_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential_magnitude).

For a resolved perpendicular wavevector, the defining composition is

$$\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$$

where $\mathcal{A}_{\parallel}$ is the averaged normalized fluctuation amplitude, $\delta\widehat{A}_{\parallel}$ is the normalized perturbation of the magnetic vector potential projected along the equilibrium magnetic field, $\mathbf{k}$ is the perpendicular wavevector, and $t$ is time. Vertical bars denote the perturbation magnitude, the overbar denotes averaging over the specified time interval, and angle brackets denote the flux-surface-average operator.

The wavevector-resolved form retains both perpendicular wavenumbers. The reduced form additionally sums these nonnegative amplitudes over $k_x$, the first perpendicular wavenumber, while retaining dependence on the other perpendicular wavenumber; this sum is not a wavenumber average.

The magnitude is taken before either average, so phase cancelation does not reduce the amplitude as it would for an averaged signed or complex perturbation. This is not a mean-square amplitude or magnetic energy. Only the perturbed vector potential is included, excluding the equilibrium contribution. The normalization is inherited from the underlying [normalized perturbation magnitude](name:normalized_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential_magnitude); neither average introduces an additional normalization.
