worked.description_before: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal bulk-flow velocity of elemental argon ions at the plasma boundary, combining charge states through a density-weighted mean.
worked.description_after: Toroidal bulk-flow velocity of argon ions, density-weighted over all ionic charge states and flux-surface averaged at the plasma boundary.
worked.documentation_before:
Flux-surface-averaged toroidal bulk-flow velocity of elemental argon ions describes the toroidal component of their collective motion over the plasma-boundary flux surface. It includes the argon ion population rather than a single charge state.

The boundary flux-surface average is defined by:

$$
\left\langle v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}}\right\rangle_{\psi_b}
= \frac{\displaystyle\int_{S_{\psi_b}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi|}{\displaystyle\int_{S_{\psi_b}} dS/|\nabla\psi|}
$$

where $\psi$ is a scalar magnetic-flux label, $\psi_b$ is its value on the plasma boundary, $S_{\psi_b}$ is the complete boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface-area element, and $\nabla\psi$ is the spatial gradient of the flux label. The component $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}}$ is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$; $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For charge-state index $z$, with density $n_{\mathrm{Ar},z}$ and bulk velocity $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ar},z}$, the local elemental-argon velocity is the density-weighted mean $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ar}}=\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Ar},z}\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ar},z}/\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Ar},z}$. Thus, this quantity differs from the local, unaveraged [toroidal argon velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) and parallels the charge-state aggregation used for toroidal flux-surface-averaged deuterium velocity at the plasma boundary.

Sign convention: Positive when the argon bulk-flow component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.
worked.documentation_after:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the argon-ion bulk-flow velocity, flux-surface averaged at the plasma boundary. The projection is onto the toroidal unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The local density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states is averaged as follows:

$$\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$$

where $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the local charge-state-aggregated toroidal argon-ion velocity, $q$ is the positive ion charge number, $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is the number density of that charge state, and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is its toroidal bulk-flow velocity. The brackets with subscript $b$ denote flux-surface averaging at the plasma boundary.

Neutral argon is excluded. Charge-state velocities are combined through a local density-weighted mean, not summed; the subsequent spatial operation is the flux-surface average of the [pointwise toroidal argon velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), rather than a value at one boundary point. The [beryllium counterpart](name:flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) uses the same projection, averaging operation, and locus for beryllium ions.

Sign convention: Positive when the flux-surface-averaged toroidal argon-ion velocity is directed toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

worked.description_before: Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of an effective deuterium–tritium fuel species, averaged over the last closed flux surface at the plasma boundary.
worked.description_after: Toroidal bulk-flow velocity of an effective single-species deuterium–tritium ion fuel, density-weighted over all ionic charge states and flux-surface averaged at the plasma boundary.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of deuterium and tritium treated as one effective fuel species, averaged over the last closed magnetic flux surface at the plasma boundary.

$$
\left\langle v_{\phi,\mathrm{DT}} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{\left\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{DT}} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}}{\left\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

Here, $v_{\phi,\mathrm{DT}}$ is the local toroidal bulk-flow velocity of the effective deuterium–tritium species, $n_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is its number density, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes a flux-surface average over the plasma-boundary surface. This averaged quantity is distinct from the local value represented by [toroidal deuterium–tritium velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
worked.documentation_after:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the effective deuterium–tritium ion bulk-flow velocity, flux-surface averaged at the plasma boundary. The projection is onto the toroidal unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The local velocity entering the average is

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{DT}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{DT}}\cdot\hat{\phi}
$$

where $v_{\phi,\mathrm{DT}}$ is the local toroidal bulk-flow velocity and $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the effective fuel-ion bulk-velocity vector, defined as the density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states.

The fuel mixture is represented by one fictitious species with mass $m_{\mathrm{DT}}=2.5m_u$, where $m_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the effective species mass and $m_u$ is the atomic mass constant. This denotes an effective fuel species, not the deuterium–tritium fusion reaction channel. Neutral particles are excluded.

This quantity applies flux-surface averaging to the [toroidal deuterium–tritium velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), rather than selecting its value at one boundary point. Charge-state velocities are combined through a local density-weighted mean, not summed, before the spatial averaging. The [tritium-ion counterpart](name:flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) uses the same projection, spatial averaging, and locus but describes tritium ions alone rather than the effective combined fuel species.

Sign convention: Positive when the flux-surface-averaged toroidal velocity is directed toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi = \psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux; $\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

The flux-surface average is the average of a quantity over a closed magnetic flux surface, weighted by the inverse magnitude of the poloidal flux gradient.

worked.name: flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
worked.description_before: Flux-surface-averaged deuterium-ion bulk-flow velocity along increasing toroidal angle on the last closed magnetic surface in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, with ionization states density-weighted.
worked.description_after: Toroidal bulk-flow velocity of deuterium ions, density-weighted over all ionic charge states and flux-surface averaged at the plasma boundary.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the flux-surface average of the toroidal component of the deuterium-ion bulk velocity on the plasma boundary, defined as the last closed magnetic flux surface. The deuterium velocity is the density-weighted mean over all deuterium ionization states.

$$
\left\langle V_{\phi,D} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{\displaystyle \oint_{\mathcal{S}_b} V_{\phi,D}\,\frac{dS}{|\mathbf{B}|}}{\displaystyle \oint_{\mathcal{S}_b} \frac{dS}{|\mathbf{B}|}}
$$

Here, $V_{\phi,D}=\mathbf{V}_D\cdot\hat{\phi}$ is the deuterium bulk-velocity projection onto the toroidal unit vector, $\mathcal{S}_b$ is the boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface-area element, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is the magnetic-field magnitude. The projection is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Unlike [toroidal deuterium velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), this quantity is averaged over the entire boundary surface rather than evaluated at a local point.

Sign convention: Positive when the deuterium bulk velocity has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

worked.name: flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude
worked.description_before: Geometric metric coefficient formed by averaging the local magnitude of the toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient over each nested magnetic flux surface.
worked.description_after: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient magnitude measures how rapidly the flux coordinate changes with distance across neighboring equilibrium magnetic surfaces.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the flux-surface average of the local geometric rate at which the toroidal flux coordinate changes through physical space. It is a scalar metric coefficient associated with nested magnetic surfaces.

The defining relation is

$$
\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{S}) = \left\langle \left|\nabla \rho_{\mathrm{tor}}\right| \right\rangle_{\mathcal{S}}
$$

where $\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{S})$ is the averaged metric coefficient, $\mathcal{S}$ is a magnetic flux surface, $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal flux coordinate labeling nested magnetic surfaces, $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient, and the angle brackets with subscript $\mathcal{S}$ denote averaging over that surface.

The quantity applies to the complete nested magnetic flux surface and is aggregated over the surface rather than evaluated at a point, along a line, or over a volume. It represents the average of the gradient magnitude, not a directional component and not the local unaveraged value.

It is obtained by applying flux-surface averaging to the local [toroidal flux coordinate gradient magnitude](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude). Unlike [flux-surface-averaged square of toroidal flux coordinate gradient magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude), it averages the magnitude itself rather than its square.
worked.documentation_after:
Flux-surface-averaged toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient magnitude is a geometric metric coefficient describing the spatial spacing of neighboring equilibrium magnetic surfaces for a specified flux-coordinate scale.

The coefficient is defined by

$$\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$$

where $\mathcal{G}$ is this metric coefficient, $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal-flux radial coordinate, and $\nabla\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is its [spatial gradient](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient). The coordinate is constant on each magnetic flux surface, vertical bars denote magnitude, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes the flux-surface average.

The quantity applies separately to each closed equilibrium magnetic flux surface and aggregates over that complete surface, without species or particle-population weighting. It is neither a pointwise value nor an average across distinct surfaces.

The averaged quantity is the [local toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient magnitude](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude), so the magnitude is taken before averaging. This differs from taking the magnitude of an averaged gradient vector. It also differs from the root-mean-square gradient magnitude, which is the square root of the [flux-surface-averaged squared gradient magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude).

The flux-surface average is the average of a quantity over a closed magnetic flux surface, weighted by the inverse magnitude of the poloidal flux gradient.

The magnitude is the Euclidean norm of a vector quantity, or the modulus of a complex one.

worked.name: flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
worked.description_before: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal velocity of helium-3 ions at the plasma boundary (separatrix).
worked.description_after: Toroidal bulk-flow velocity of helium-3 ions, density-weighted over all ionic charge states and flux-surface averaged at the plasma boundary.
worked.documentation_before:
The flux-surface-averaged toroidal velocity of helium-3 ($^3$He) ions quantifies the bulk toroidal flow of this light helium isotope (2 protons, 1 neutron) evaluated on the last closed flux surface that separates the confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. This boundary value characterizes net toroidal rotation of $^3$He ions at the separatrix, relevant to impurity transport, momentum balance, and plasma–wall interaction studies.

The flux-surface average of the toroidal velocity component is defined as:

$$
\langle v_\phi \rangle = \frac{\oint v_\phi \, dl / B_p}{\oint dl / B_p}
$$

where $v_\phi = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{He_3}} \cdot \hat{\phi}$ is the ion fluid velocity projected onto $\hat{\phi}$ — the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame — $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic field magnitude, and $dl$ is the arc-length element along the separatrix contour.

Toroidal rotation at the boundary is driven by external momentum sources such as neutral beam injection, intrinsic rotation arising from turbulent and neoclassical stresses, and the edge radial electric field. The quantity is inferred from charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS) using injected neutral beams that stimulate helium-3 charge-exchange emission lines whose Doppler shift encodes the local toroidal velocity.

Boundary toroidal flow speeds for light ions in tokamak edge plasmas are of order $10^3$–$10^4$ m s$^{-1}$, depending on heating power, plasma current, and confinement regime. The analogous quantities for tritium and hydrogen are [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) and [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary); the generic multi-species form is toroidal_ion_velocity_at_plasma_boundary.
worked.documentation_after:

$$

where $v_{\phi,{}^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the local toroidal helium-3 ion bulk-flow velocity and $\mathbf{v}_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-3 ion bulk-velocity vector, defined as the density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states.

Singly and doubly ionized helium-3 are included; neutral helium-3, other helium isotopes, and other ion species are excluded. Charge-state velocities are combined through a local density-weighted mean, not summed, before spatial averaging.

worked.name: flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_plasma_boundary

worked.description_after: Toroidal bulk-flow velocity of helium-4 ions, density-weighted over all ionic charge states and flux-surface averaged at the plasma boundary.
worked.documentation_before:
The quantity is the flux-surface average over the separatrix of the toroidal component of the helium-4 ion bulk-flow velocity. The helium-4 value includes all helium-4 charge states through a density-weighted mean, rather than a sum of their velocities.

For charge-state-resolved density $n_{4,q}$ and toroidal velocity $v_{\phi,4,q}$, the species velocity is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{FS}} = \left\langle \frac{\sum_q n_{4,q}v_{\phi,4,q}}{\sum_q n_{4,q}} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{sep}}
$$

where $q$ indexes helium-4 charge state, $n_{4,q}$ is its number density in m$^{-3}$, $v_{\phi,4,q}$ is its toroidal velocity in m s$^{-1}$, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{sep}}$ denotes the flux-surface average over the separatrix. The toroidal component is taken along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This averaged quantity is distinct from the local toroidal helium-4 velocity at the plasma boundary; the corresponding isotope-specific construction for helium-3 is toroidal flux-surface-averaged helium-3 velocity at the plasma boundary.

worked.name: flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
worked.description_before: Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of hydrogen ions, averaged over the last closed magnetic flux surface and combining all ionization states.
worked.description_after: Toroidal bulk-flow velocity of hydrogen ions, density-weighted over all ionic charge states and flux-surface averaged at the plasma boundary.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the density-weighted mean toroidal bulk-flow velocity of hydrogen ions at the plasma boundary, combining all hydrogen ionization states. The average is taken over the last closed magnetic flux surface in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

$$
\bar v_{\phi,\mathrm{H}}^{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{\sum_q \left\langle n_{\mathrm{H},q}v_{\phi,\mathrm{H},q}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}}{\sum_q \left\langle n_{\mathrm{H},q}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

Here $q$ indexes the hydrogen ionization states, $n_{\mathrm{H},q}$ is the number density of state $q$, $v_{\phi,\mathrm{H},q}$ is its toroidal velocity component, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes the flux-surface average over the plasma boundary.

The charge-state aggregation is a density-weighted mean, not a sum of velocities. It differs from the local quantity [toroidal hydrogen velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) because that quantity is not flux-surface averaged, and from [toroidal flux-surface-averaged ion velocity at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_ion_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), which represents the total ion fluid.

worked.name: flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_ion_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
worked.description_before: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal bulk-flow velocity of the total ion fluid at the plasma boundary, representing the density-weighted mean over all ion species and charge states.
worked.description_after: Toroidal bulk-flow velocity of a selected ion species, density-weighted over all ionic charge states and flux-surface averaged at the plasma boundary.
worked.documentation_before:
The toroidal component of the ion bulk-flow velocity, flux-surface averaged over the plasma boundary — the last closed flux surface forming the core–scrape-off-layer interface. For a plasma containing multiple ion species and charge states, the ion velocity is the density-weighted mean

$$
v_\phi = \frac{\sum_s n_s \, v_{\phi,s}}{\sum_s n_s}
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density and $v_{\phi,s}$ is the toroidal velocity of species $s$, with the sum running over all ion species and charge states present.

The flux-surface average is evaluated as $\langle A \rangle = \oint A \, dl/B_p \,/\, \oint dl/B_p$, where $dl$ is the poloidal arc-length element and $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic field magnitude, integrated along the plasma boundary flux surface. Species-resolved counterparts such as [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_nitrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) and [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) give contributions from individual ion species.

Sign convention: Positive when $v_\phi$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.
worked.documentation_after:

The projection is onto the toroidal unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The local velocity entering the average is

$$
v_{\phi,i} = \mathbf{v}_i\cdot\hat{\phi}
$$

where $i$ identifies the selected ion species, $v_{\phi,i}$ is its local toroidal bulk-flow velocity, and $\mathbf{v}_i$ is its bulk-velocity vector, defined as the density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states.

Only ions of the selected species are included; neutral particles and other ion species are excluded. The quantity describes directed collective motion, not random thermal motion or a transport-model convection velocity. It is not an aggregate velocity of the combined ion fluid.

worked.name: flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_iron_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
worked.description_before: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal component of the iron impurity ion bulk flow velocity at the plasma boundary (last closed flux surface).
worked.description_after: Toroidal bulk-flow velocity of iron ions, density-weighted over all ionic charge states and flux-surface averaged at the plasma boundary.
worked.documentation_before:
The toroidal component of the iron impurity bulk flow velocity, averaged over the magnetic flux surface coinciding with the plasma boundary, characterizes the net toroidal rotation of iron ions at the last closed flux surface. The flux-surface average eliminates poloidal asymmetries in the local velocity distribution, providing a single scalar representative of the toroidal impurity flow at the edge.

The flux-surface average of a quantity $f$ on a given flux surface is defined as:

$$
\langle f \rangle = \frac{\oint f \, dl_p / B_p}{\oint dl_p / B_p}
$$

where $l_p$ is the poloidal arc length along the flux-surface contour and $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic field magnitude. Iron ($Z = 26$) is a high-$Z$ metallic impurity that enters the confined plasma through sputtering of plasma-facing components; its toroidal rotation at the boundary reflects edge momentum transport and neoclassical impurity flow physics.

This quantity is measured via charge exchange recombination spectroscopy, exploiting Doppler shifts of iron charge-state emission lines recorded along multiple poloidal viewing chords; the flux-surface-averaged value is then reconstructed from multi-chord data. This name is directly analogous to boundary velocity names for lighter impurities such as [carbon](name:flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), [argon](name:flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), and [neon](name:flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary). Where poloidally resolved measurements are available, the local counterpart [toroidal iron velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) provides additional information on poloidal asymmetries not captured by the flux-surface average.

Sign convention: Positive when the iron ion velocity is directed in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

worked.description_before: Density-weighted toroidal bulk velocity of krypton ions, averaged over all ionization states and the last closed magnetic flux surface in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.

worked.documentation_before:
Flux-surface-averaged toroidal krypton velocity is the density-weighted mean over all krypton ionization states on the plasma boundary, identified with the last closed magnetic flux surface. The toroidal direction is the direction of increasing angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

$$
\left\langle v_{\phi,\mathrm{Kr}}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS},b} = \frac{\displaystyle\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} \left(\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}\right)\frac{dl}{B_p}}{\displaystyle\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} \left(\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}\right)\frac{dl}{B_p}}
$$

Here $q$ indexes krypton ionization states, $n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$ is the number density of state $q$ in m$^{-3}$, $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$ is its toroidal bulk velocity, $dl$ is poloidal arc length, $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude, and $\psi_b$ labels the boundary surface. This species-resolved quantity differs from the total-ion quantity toroidal flux-surface-averaged ion velocity at the plasma boundary; its locus differs from [toroidal krypton velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).

worked.description_before: Flux-surface-averaged total plasma momentum in the toroidal direction at the plasma boundary is the signed flux-surface average, on the last closed magnetic flux surface, of the cumulative toroidal linear momentum enclosed by that surface, summed over electrons and all ion species. worked.documentation_before:
Flux-surface-averaged total plasma momentum in the toroidal direction at the plasma boundary is the flux-surface average, on the last closed magnetic flux surface, of the cumulative toroidal component of plasma linear momentum enclosed by that surface. The cumulative momentum includes electrons and all ion species and is treated as a flux-surface scalar before averaging.

The cumulative boundary value is defined by the enclosed-volume integral; writing the flux-surface average explicitly gives:

$$
P_{\phi,\mathrm{FSA}}^{\mathrm{b}}
=
\frac{\oint_{\psi=\psi_\mathrm{b}} P_\phi(\psi_\mathrm{b})\, dA/|\nabla\psi|}
     {\oint_{\psi=\psi_\mathrm{b}} dA/|\nabla\psi|}
=
\int_{V_\mathrm{b}} \sum_s m_s n_s(\mathbf{x})\, v_{\phi,s}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $P_{\phi,\mathrm{FSA}}^\mathrm{b}$ is this quantity, $P_\phi(\psi_\mathrm{b})$ is the [toroidal total plasma momentum](name:toroidal_total_plasma_momentum) associated with the boundary flux label, $\psi_\mathrm{b}$ is the boundary value of the [poloidal magnetic-flux label](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface), $dA/|\nabla\psi|$ is the flux-surface averaging measure normalized by the denominator, $V_\mathrm{b}$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface, $dV$ is the volume element, $s$ runs over electrons and all ion species, $m_s$ is species mass, $n_s$ is species number density, and $v_{\phi,s}=\mathbf{v}_s\cdot\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal velocity component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The product $m_s n_s v_{\phi,s}$ is the toroidal momentum density contribution of species $s$, so the flux-surface average is applied to the enclosed total $P_\phi(\psi_\mathrm{b})$, not directly to this local density.

This quantity is not a boundary-surface integral of local toroidal momentum density, not the flux-surface average of the local density $g_\phi=\sum_s m_s n_s v_{\phi,s}$ alone, and not a major-radius-weighted angular-momentum measure. It is the flux-surface-averaged representation of toroidal total plasma momentum at the plasma boundary; the analogous cumulative value at the pedestal top is [toroidal plasma momentum at the pedestal top](name:toroidal_plasma_momentum_at_pedestal_top).

Sign convention: Positive when the enclosed total toroidal momentum is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The species contributions combine according to

$$\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$$

where $p_\phi$ is total toroidal linear momentum, $p_{\phi,e}$ is the electron contribution, $p_{\phi,i}$ is the contribution from ion species $i$, and $\phi$ is toroidal angle. The brackets with subscript $\mathrm b$ denote flux-surface averaging at the plasma boundary.

The density-weighted flux-surface average is defined by:

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{tungsten},b}^{\mathrm{FS}} =
\frac{\displaystyle \int_{S_b} \left(\sum_q n_{\mathrm{tungsten},q} v_{\phi,\mathrm{tungsten},q}\right) \frac{dS}{|\nabla \rho|}}
{\displaystyle \int_{S_b} \left(\sum_q n_{\mathrm{tungsten},q}\right) \frac{dS}{|\nabla \rho|}}
$$

where $V_{\phi,\mathrm{tungsten},b}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ is this quantity, $S_b$ is the last closed magnetic flux surface, $q$ indexes tungsten ionization states, $n_{\mathrm{tungsten},q}$ is the local number density of ionization state $q$, $v_{\phi,\mathrm{tungsten},q}$ is its local toroidal bulk-flow component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $dS$ is the surface area element on $S_b$, and $\rho$ is the radial flux coordinate in a flux coordinate set $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$ labeling the nested magnetic flux surfaces. The factor $dS/|\nabla\rho|$ gives the volume-derivative flux-surface-average measure, and any monotonic relabeling of $\rho$ gives the same ratio on a given surface.

This quantity represents the boundary value only; for a diverted boundary it is understood as the limit approaching the last closed magnetic flux surface from inside the confined plasma. The flux-surface-averaged toroidal xenon velocity at the plasma boundary quantifies the mean azimuthal flow of xenon impurity ions around the torus, averaged along the last closed flux surface (separatrix). Xenon ($Z=54$) is a heavy noble-gas impurity used in radiative-mantle experiments to spread divertor heat loads, and its toroidal rotation reflects momentum balance between collisional coupling to the bulk plasma, neoclassical forces, and external toroidal momentum input.

The flux-surface average of the toroidal velocity component $v_\phi^\mathrm{Xe}$ is defined as:

$$
\langle v_\phi^\mathrm{Xe} \rangle = \frac{\oint v_\phi^\mathrm{Xe} \, B_p^{-1} \, dl}{\oint B_p^{-1} \, dl}
$$

where $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic field magnitude and the line integrals are taken along the plasma boundary contour.

Toroidal impurity velocities at the separatrix are measured primarily by charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS), resolving Doppler shifts from charge exchange between injected neutral beam atoms and Xe ions; a poloidally distributed array of sightlines is necessary to reconstruct the flux-surface average. The non-averaged counterpart is given by [toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), while analogous averaged quantities for lighter seeding species include [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) and [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).

worked.description_after: Number density of helium-3 ions, counting all positive charge states but no neutral atoms, expressed as their local concentration per physical plasma volume.

Helium-3 ion number density is the local count of charged helium-3 ions per unit plasma volume at a specified plasma location. It is summed over the singly ionized and fully stripped charge states and excludes neutral helium-3 atoms.

$$
n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{Z=1}^{2} n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He},Z}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is the plasma location, $Z$ is the ionic charge state, and $n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He},Z}$ is the number density of helium-3 ions in charge state $Z$, expressed in m$^{-3}$. The [volume-averaged helium-3 density](name:volume_averaged_helium_3_density) and [line-averaged helium-3 density](name:line_averaged_helium_3_density) are spatial averages of this local quantity over their respective domains.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of helium 3. The local number density is defined by

$$
n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}} = \frac{d\mathcal{N}_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-3 ion number density, $\mathcal{N}_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the number of helium-3 ions in physical volume $V$, and the derivative defines their local concentration in the continuum description.

No particular plasma location or spatial averaging domain is prescribed. The [line-averaged helium-3 density](name:line_averaged_helium_3_density) is the chord-length mean of this local density along a specified path, whereas the [volume-averaged helium-3 density](name:volume_averaged_helium_3_density) is its volume-weighted mean over the confined plasma.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: helium_4_density
worked.description_before: Local number density of helium-4 ions per unit plasma volume, the principal measure of fusion ash concentration in deuterium-tritium burning plasmas.
worked.description_after: Number density of helium-4 ions, counting all positive charge states but no neutral atoms, expressed as their concentration per physical plasma volume.
worked.documentation_before:
The helium-4 ion number density $n_{{}^4\text{He}}$ quantifies the local concentration of ${}^4\text{He}$ nuclei at a given point in the plasma. At fusion-relevant temperatures (several keV), helium-4 is fully stripped to He$^{2+}$, and in deuterium-tritium burning plasmas it accumulates as the primary fusion ash product of the reaction ${}^2\text{H} + {}^3\text{H} \rightarrow {}^4\text{He} + n$; its buildup dilutes the fuel and reduces the fusion reaction rate if not exhausted by the divertor system.

The time evolution of $n_{{}^4\text{He}}$ is governed by the particle continuity equation

$$
\frac{\partial n_{{}^4\text{He}}}{\partial t} + \nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{{}^4\text{He}} = S_{{}^4\text{He}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{{}^4\text{He}}$ is the helium-4 particle flux and $S_{{}^4\text{He}}$ is the volumetric source rate from fusion reactions and ionization of recycled helium neutrals at the plasma edge.

The helium-4 density is measured primarily via charge exchange recombination spectroscopy, where injected neutral beam atoms undergo charge exchange with He$^{2+}$ ions to produce line emission from excited helium atoms; passive spectroscopy of edge recycling emission provides a complementary approach. Chord-averaged and volume-averaged forms are provided by [line_averaged_helium_4_density](name:line_averaged_helium_4_density) and [volume_averaged_helium_4_density](name:volume_averaged_helium_4_density) respectively, while [helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary) gives the boundary value.

In D-T burning plasmas, central He-4 densities are in the range $10^{18}$-$10^{19}$ m$^{-3}$, with the helium-to-electron density ratio — captured by [fraction](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density) — kept below approximately 5-10% in steady state to avoid excessive fuel dilution.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of helium 4. The underlying local density is the zeroth velocity-space moment:

$$
n_{\mathrm{He4}} = \int f_{\mathrm{He4}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the helium-4 ion number density, $f_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the local velocity distribution of the counted ion population, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The integral extends over all particle velocities.

This quantity is isotope-specific and distinct from [helium-3 density](name:helium_3_density). It selects no particular plasma region or spatial averaging operation.

The [line-averaged helium-4 density](name:line_averaged_helium_4_density) is the chord-length mean of this local density, whereas the [volume-averaged helium-4 density](name:volume_averaged_helium_4_density) is its volume mean over the confined plasma. Both averages retain the same counted population.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: hydrogen_density
worked.description_before: Local number density of hydrogen (protium) ions in the plasma, giving the count of H+ particles per unit volume at a specified spatial position.
worked.description_after: Number density of hydrogen (protium) ions in the plasma, providing the concentration underlying local values and spatially averaged forms. The ions of the species are counted over all charge states, with neutral atoms excluded.
worked.documentation_before:
The hydrogen density quantifies the local concentration of protium ions ($^1$H$^+$, the lightest hydrogen isotope with mass number $A = 1$) at a point in the plasma. It is distinct from the neutral atomic hydrogen density and from the number densities of heavier hydrogenic isotopes such as deuterium ($^2$H) and tritium ($^3$H).

The number density $n_H$ at position $\mathbf{r}$ is defined as

$$
n_H(\mathbf{r}) = \frac{dN_H}{dV}
$$

where $N_H$ is the number of hydrogen ions within the infinitesimal volume element $dV$ centered at $\mathbf{r}$.

Spatially averaged forms provide experimentally accessible measures of the same quantity: [line_averaged_hydrogen_density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density) gives the path-length-normalized ion count along a spectroscopic or interferometric chord, while [volume_averaged_hydrogen_density](name:volume_averaged_hydrogen_density) integrates the ion content over the full plasma volume. The isotopic composition of the hydrogenic fuel is tracked by [ratio_of_hydrogen_density_to_total_hydrogenic_density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density), which expresses $n_H$ relative to the combined protium, deuterium, and tritium ion density. The aggregate over all three hydrogen isotopes is given by hydrogenic_density, and the full multi-species ion sum by [total_ion_density](name:total_ion_number_density).
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of hydrogen. Its local value is the zeroth velocity-space moment:

$$
n_{\mathrm{H}} = \int f_{\mathrm{H}^{+}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the hydrogen-ion number density, $f_{\mathrm{H}^{+}}$ is the protium-ion velocity distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The integral covers the full velocity distribution without selecting a thermal or fast-particle subset.

Hydrogen here denotes protium, not deuterium or tritium. Like [argon density](name:argon_density), this is a species-specific concentration rather than the combined density of all ion species; no particular spatial average or plasma region is prescribed.

The [line-averaged hydrogen density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density) is its path-length-normalized integral along a specified chord, whereas the [volume-averaged hydrogen density](name:volume_averaged_hydrogen_density) is its volume-normalized integral over the specified plasma volume. The [hydrogen-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_hydrogen_density_to_electron_density) divides this hydrogen-ion concentration by the free-electron concentration and is a relative abundance rather than a number density.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: hydrogenic_density
worked.description_before: Charge-state- and isotope-summed number density of hydrogenic particles in the plasma.
worked.description_after: Number density of a selected species' ions, combining its charged states while excluding neutral atoms, expressed as a concentration per physical volume.
worked.documentation_before:
Hydrogenic particle density is the local abundance of hydrogen isotopes, including every included ionization state, expressed per unit volume.

$$
n_{\mathrm{H}} = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{H}} \sum_q n_{s,q}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the total hydrogenic number density, $\mathcal{H}$ is the set of included hydrogenic isotopes, $q$ indexes their charge states, and $n_{s,q}$ is the number density of isotope $s$ in state $q$.

The quantity includes all charge states and isotopic variants and is not restricted to a particular isotope, ionization state, or neutral population. The concrete catalog instance is [total hydrogenic density](name:total_hydrogenic_density).
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of hydrogenic. The local density is defined by

$$
n_s(\mathbf{x}) = \int f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_s$ is the ion number density, $s$ labels the selected population, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_s$ is that population's velocity distribution per physical volume, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The integral covers all particle velocities.

This general quantity selects no particular isotope, location, or spatial averaging convention. Line-averaged and volume-averaged densities are spatial averages of the concentration, rather than integrated particle inventories. Number density counts ions without electric-charge weighting and is therefore distinct from charge density.

[Hydrogen density](name:hydrogen_density) and [deuterium density](name:deuterium_density) specialize this definition to individual hydrogen isotopes; a grouped population includes the explicitly selected species.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: iron_density
worked.description_before: Total number density of iron impurity ions in the plasma, summed over all ionization states from singly to fully ionized iron (atomic number Z = 26).
worked.description_after: Number density of iron ions summed over positive charge states, with each ion counted once and neutral iron excluded.
worked.documentation_before:
Iron density is the total number density of iron ions present in the plasma, aggregated over all charge states from Fe$^{1+}$ through Fe$^{26+}$ (atomic number $Z = 26$). It characterizes the iron impurity content without resolving the per-charge-state distribution, and may refer to a local point value or a spatially averaged quantity depending on the sampling convention.

The total iron ion number density $n_\mathrm{Fe}$ is defined as:

$$
n_\mathrm{Fe} = \sum_{z=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}$ is the number density of iron in charge state $z$.

Iron enters confined plasmas primarily through physical sputtering of high-$Z$ plasma-facing components. Spectroscopic measurements in the vacuum-ultraviolet and soft X-ray ranges resolve individual charge-state emission lines; the total iron density is reconstructed by summing ionization-state-resolved densities derived from ionization balance calculations.

This general quantity is concretized by spatial-sampling variants: flux_surface_averaged_iron_density averages the local density over a magnetic flux surface, [line_averaged_iron_density](name:line_averaged_iron_density) represents a chord-integrated value divided by path length, and [volume_averaged_iron_density](name:volume_averaged_iron_density) integrates over the full plasma volume. Position-specific forms are available at key radial locations such as [iron_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:iron_density_at_magnetic_axis), iron_density_at_pedestal, and [iron_density_at_limiter](name:iron_density_at_limiter).
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of iron. The density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \sum_{q=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the iron-ion number density, $q$ is the positive ionic charge number, and $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}$ is the number density of iron ions in charge state $q$; 26 is the atomic number of iron. The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

No particular plasma location or spatial averaging operation is implied. Each ion contributes one particle rather than a contribution weighted by its charge. Evaluation on the last closed magnetic flux surface gives [iron density at the plasma boundary](name:iron_density_at_plasma_boundary).

The [line-averaged iron density](name:line_averaged_iron_density) is the path-length mean of this density, whereas [volume-averaged iron density](name:volume_averaged_iron_density) is its volume mean over the confined plasma. This density is also the numerator of the [ratio of iron density to electron density](name:ratio_of_iron_density_to_electron_density), which expresses iron-ion abundance relative to free electrons rather than an absolute concentration.

worked.name: krypton_density
worked.description_before: Number density of krypton ions at a point in the plasma, summed over all ionized charge states from Kr1+ through fully stripped Kr36+ and excluding neutral krypton atoms.
worked.description_after: Number density of krypton ions across all positive charge states, excluding neutral krypton, expressed as their concentration per physical plasma volume.
worked.documentation_before:
Number density of krypton ions at a point in the plasma, summed over all ionized charge states from Kr$^{1+}$ through fully stripped Kr$^{36+}$; neutral krypton atoms are excluded.

With krypton atomic number $Z_\mathrm{Kr}=36$, the ion density is the charge-state sum:

$$
n_\mathrm{Kr} = \sum_{q=1}^{36} n_\mathrm{Kr}^{(q)}
$$

where $n_\mathrm{Kr}^{(q)}$ is the number density of krypton ions in charge state $q$ and the neutral state $q=0$ is omitted from the sum.

This is an extensive, charge-state-summed species density, not a density-weighted mean over charge states and not the charge-state-resolved [ion charge-state density](name:ion_charge_state_density), which retains the individual $n_\mathrm{Kr}^{(q)}$ terms. It is an absolute density, distinct from the relative [krypton fraction](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_krypton_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density) normalized to the electron density. The locus-specific values [krypton_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:krypton_density_at_magnetic_axis), krypton_density_at_pedestal, and [krypton_density_at_divertor_target](name:krypton_density_at_divertor_target) share this ions-only charge-state scope. In contrast, [volume_averaged_krypton_density](name:volume_averaged_krypton_density) includes all krypton charge states from neutral through fully stripped, so its charge-state scope differs from this ions-only local quantity; the [line_averaged_krypton_density](name:line_averaged_krypton_density) likewise carries its own averaging definition.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of krypton. The local number density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Kr}} = \frac{d\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the local krypton-ion number density, $\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the krypton-ion count, and $V$ is physical plasma volume.

This is the krypton-ion specialization of [particle number density](name:particle_density), distinct from mass density and charge density.

The [line-averaged krypton density](name:line_averaged_krypton_density) is its chord-length mean, whereas the [volume-averaged krypton density](name:volume_averaged_krypton_density) is its volume mean over the confined plasma inside the last closed flux surface. Neither spatial averaging operation is implicit in the local density.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: line_averaged_argon_density
worked.description_before: Chord-averaged number density of argon ions along a specified plasma path, with contributions from all ionization stages summed together.
worked.description_after: Number density of argon ions averaged along a specified plasma chord, including all positive charge states and excluding neutral argon atoms.
worked.documentation_before:
Line-averaged argon ion number density is the argon ion concentration averaged along a specified chord through the plasma, including all ionization stages.

The line average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_\mathrm{Ar} = \frac{1}{L} \int_0^L \sum_{q=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar},q}(\mathbf{r}(l))\,dl
$$

where $L$ is the chord length, $l$ is distance along the chord, $\mathbf{r}(l)$ is the position on the chord, and $n_{\mathrm{Ar},q}$ is the local number density of argon ions in charge state $q$.

This path average is distinct from the local [argon ion density](name:argon_density) and from the plasma-volume average [volume-averaged argon density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density).
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of argon. The argon-specific chord average is

$$
\bar{n}_{\mathrm{Ar}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\,dl
$$

where $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the line-averaged argon ion number density, $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the local argon ion number density evaluated along the chord, $L$ is the chord length, and $l$ is distance along the chord.

This chord-specific average is not a local value at an individual point; it equals the local density throughout the chord when that density is uniform. It differs from [volume-averaged argon density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density), which averages the same population over the confined plasma volume. The [line-averaged xenon density](name:line_averaged_xenon_density) applies the same chord-averaging convention to xenon instead of argon.

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: line_averaged_beryllium_density
worked.description_before: Chord-average of the beryllium ion number density along a diagnostic line of sight, equal to the path integral of the local beryllium density divided by the chord length.
worked.description_after: Number density of beryllium ions averaged along a specified plasma chord, including all positive charge states and excluding neutral beryllium atoms.
worked.documentation_before:
The line-averaged beryllium ion number density quantifies the mean beryllium ion content along a plasma diagnostic chord, normalized by chord length. It is the chord-integrated analog of the local [beryllium_density](name:beryllium_density) and is the most directly accessible measure of beryllium impurity concentration from line-of-sight diagnostics.

The quantity is defined as:

$$
\bar{n}_{Be} = \frac{1}{L} \int_0^L n_{Be}(l) \, dl
$$

where $n_{Be}(l)$ is the local beryllium ion number density at path coordinate $l$ along the chord and $L$ is the total chord length.

Inferred from passive spectroscopy of beryllium emission lines by inverting chord-integrated emission intensities using atomic emissivity coefficients; the result aggregates contributions from all beryllium ionization states present along the chord. The [volume_averaged_beryllium_density](name:volume_averaged_beryllium_density) provides a complementary global volume average, while [beryllium_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:beryllium_density_at_magnetic_axis) gives the local on-axis value.

Sign convention: Positive when beryllium ions populate the measurement chord.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of beryllium. The beryllium-specific chord average is

$$
\bar{n}_{\mathrm{Be}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_{\mathrm{Be}}\,dl
$$

where $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the line-averaged beryllium ion number density, $n_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the local [beryllium density](name:beryllium_density) evaluated along the chord, $L$ is the stated chord length, and $l$ is distance along that chord.

This quantity averages the local beryllium density over the stated chord rather than evaluating it at a prescribed point, as [beryllium density at the plasma boundary](name:beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary) does. It is the beryllium counterpart of [line-averaged helium-4 density](name:line_averaged_helium_4_density) under the same chord-averaging convention.

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: line_averaged_deuterium_density
worked.description_before: Deuterium ion density averaged along a plasma chord is the mean local number density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion population. It is charge-state-summed over ionized deuterium and excludes neutral or molecular deuterium and non-deuterium species.
worked.description_after: Number density of deuterium ions averaged along a specified plasma chord, including all positive charge states and excluding neutral deuterium atoms.
worked.documentation_before:
Deuterium ion density averaged along a plasma chord is the mean local number density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion population. It represents the path-length mean of the local deuterium density along the specified chord, with deuterium treated as a species-level ion density.

The line average is defined by the path-length average of the local [deuterium density](name:deuterium_density):

$$
\langle n_D \rangle_\ell = \frac{1}{L} \int_{\ell_0}^{\ell_1} n_D(\ell) \, d\ell
$$

where $\langle n_D \rangle_\ell$ is the line-averaged deuterium density, $\ell$ is arclength along the chord, $\ell_0$ and $\ell_1$ are the endpoints of the averaging interval, $L = \ell_1 - \ell_0$ is the chord path length, and $n_D(\ell)$ is the local [deuterium density](name:deuterium_density) at position $\ell$.

The local deuterium density entering the integral is charge-state-summed over ionized atomic charge states; for deuterium this reduces to the singly ionized deuteron population. Neutral deuterium atoms, molecular deuterium, and non-deuterium species are excluded. This quantity is a path average; local [deuterium density](name:deuterium_density) and [deuterium ion density averaged over the total plasma volume](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density) are distinct quantities.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of deuterium. Deuterium has only one positive atomic charge state, giving the species-specific identity

$$
\bar{n}_{\mathrm D} = \bar{n}_{\mathrm D^{+}}
$$

where $\bar{n}_{\mathrm D}$ is the line-averaged deuterium ion number density and $\bar{n}_{\mathrm D^{+}}$ is the line-averaged number density of singly ionized deuterium, whose ions are deuterons.

This chord-specific quantity is not a local density at a single point; it equals the local density throughout the chord only when that density is uniform. It differs from [volume-averaged deuterium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density), which averages the same ion population over the plasma volume. It is the deuterium counterpart of [line-averaged hydrogen density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density), with the isotope population changed from protium to deuterium.

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: line_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density
worked.description_before: Chord-averaged ion number density of the combined deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species along a specified line of sight.
worked.description_after: Number density of deuterium–tritium fuel ions treated as one effective species and averaged along a plasma chord, including all ionic charge states and excluding neutral atoms.
worked.documentation_before:
The deuterium-tritium density is the chord-averaged ion count per unit volume of the fictitious combined fuel pseudo-species formed by merging deuterium and tritium ions. It is derived from the local [deuterium-tritium density](name:deuterium_tritium_density) along a specified chord.

The chord average is defined by

$$
\bar{n}_{DT} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_{DT}(l)\,dl
$$

where $\bar{n}_{DT}$ is the chord-averaged density, $L$ is the chord length, $l$ is distance along the chord, and $n_{DT}(l)$ is the local deuterium-tritium pseudo-species density. The quantity is a line average and must not be interpreted as the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density); both retain the deuterium-plus-tritium aggregation convention.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of deuterium tritium. Line averaging preserves the effective-species density relation:

$$
\bar{n}_{\mathrm{DT}} = \bar{n}_{\mathrm{D}} + \bar{n}_{\mathrm{T}}
$$

where $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the line-averaged effective deuterium–tritium ion number density, $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{D}}$ is the [line-averaged deuterium ion number density](name:line_averaged_deuterium_density), and $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the line-averaged tritium ion number density. All three averages refer to the same chord segment.

The local quantity being averaged is [deuterium–tritium density](name:deuterium_tritium_density). This chord-specific mean is distinct from a plasma-volume average and does not generally equal the local density at any specified point. Deuterium–tritium denotes the effective fuel species here, not the fusion reaction channel.

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: line_averaged_effective_charge
worked.description_before: Effective charge of a plasma ion mixture averaged uniformly along a specified line of sight, expressing its chord-mean composition factor for electron–ion Coulomb scattering.
worked.description_after: Effective charge of a plasma ion mixture averaged along a specified viewing chord, expressing its mean composition factor for electron–ion Coulomb scattering.
worked.documentation_before:
Effective charge averaged along a specified plasma line of sight describes the chord-mean charge-state composition of the ion mixture relevant to electron–ion Coulomb scattering.

The line average is defined by:

$$
\bar{Z}_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L Z_{\mathrm{eff}}\,dl
$$

where $\bar{Z}_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the line-averaged effective charge, $Z_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the local [effective charge](name:effective_charge), $L$ is the length of the specified plasma chord, and $l$ is distance along that chord.

The local composition factor is $Z_{\mathrm{eff}} = \sum_a n_a Z_a^2/n_e$, where $a$ indexes all ion species and their ionized charge states, $n_a$ is the number density of each ionic population, $Z_a$ is its charge number, and $n_e$ is the free-electron number density. The mixture includes both fuel and impurity ions; it is not the mean charge number of a selected species.

The averaging uses uniform length weighting of the local effective charge. It is distinct from an unnormalized chord integral, an emissivity-weighted average, or a ratio formed from separately chord-integrated charge moments.
worked.documentation_after:
Effective charge averaged along a specified viewing chord expresses the chord-mean composition factor for electron–ion Coulomb scattering.

The local [effective charge](name:effective_charge) being averaged obeys $Z_{\mathrm{eff}} = \sum_a n_a Z_a^2/n_e$, where $Z_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the local mixture effective charge, $a$ labels an ion species and charge-state combination, $n_a$ is its number density, $Z_a$ is its ionic charge number, and $n_e$ is the free-electron number density. The sum includes all ion species and positive ionic charge states, not only impurities; neutral particles do not contribute.

The chord-averaged quantity is distinct from a local value at a beam-crossing point, an unnormalized line integral, and an emissivity-weighted average.

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

worked.name: line_averaged_effective_hydrogenic_mass
worked.description_before: Line-averaged effective hydrogenic mass is the chord-length average of the local density-weighted mean atomic mass of bulk hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium.
worked.description_after: Line-averaged effective hydrogenic mass describes bulk hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium composition using the local isotope-density-weighted mean atomic mass along a specified chord.
worked.documentation_before:
Line-averaged effective hydrogenic mass is the chord-length average of the local [effective hydrogenic mass](name:effective_hydrogenic_mass) of the bulk hydrogenic ion mixture. The local mean atomic mass is weighted by the isotope number densities.

The line average is defined by:

$$
\bar{m}_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L m_{\mathrm{eff}}\,dl
$$

where $\bar{m}_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the line-averaged effective hydrogenic mass, $m_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the local effective hydrogenic mass, $L$ is the chord length, and $l$ is distance along the chord. The local mean satisfies $m_{\mathrm{eff}} = (\sum_s n_s m_s)/(\sum_s n_s)$, where $s$ labels hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium, $n_s$ is the local bulk-ion number density of isotope $s$ summed over its ionic charge states, and $m_s$ is that isotope's atomic mass.

Electrons and non-hydrogenic species do not enter the isotope weighting. The chord average weights the local effective mass uniformly by length; it is not a ratio of chord-integrated mass density to chord-integrated number density. It differs from [volume-averaged effective hydrogenic mass](name:volume_averaged_effective_hydrogenic_mass) by averaging along a chord rather than over a plasma volume.
worked.documentation_after:
Line-averaged effective hydrogenic mass describes the isotopic composition of the bulk hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium ion mixture along a specified chord. It applies the line-average operator to the local [effective hydrogenic mass](name:effective_hydrogenic_mass), rather than describing the mass of one specified isotope.

The local mixture mass entering the average is

$$
m_{\mathrm{eff}}(l) = \frac{\sum_i n_i(l)m_i}{\sum_i n_i(l)}
$$

where $m_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the local effective hydrogenic mass, $l$ is distance along the chord, $i$ labels hydrogen, deuterium, or tritium, $n_i$ is the local number density of bulk ions of isotope $i$ summed over ionic charge states, and $m_i$ is that isotope's atomic mass.

Spatial averaging is applied after forming this local isotope-density-weighted mean; the quantity is not defined by substituting line-averaged isotope densities into the local mass formula. Nonhydrogenic species and fast-ion populations are excluded. Unlike [volume-averaged effective hydrogenic mass](name:volume_averaged_effective_hydrogenic_mass), this quantity averages along the specified chord rather than over the plasma volume.

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

worked.name: line_averaged_electron_density
worked.description_before: Number density of free electrons averaged along a specified plasma chord with equal path-length weighting, excluding electrons bound in atoms, molecules, or ions.
worked.description_after: Number density of free electrons averaged along a specified plasma chord, including thermal and nonthermal populations and excluding bound electrons.
worked.documentation_before:
Number density of electron

The line average is defined by

$$\bar{f} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L f\,dl$$

where $\bar{n}_e$ is the line-averaged electron density, $n_e$ is the local free-electron number density evaluated along the chord, $L$ is the positive length of the specified chord, and $l$ is distance along it. The integration interval and length denominator refer to the same chord segment.

The electron population includes thermal and nonthermal free electrons over the full velocity distribution; electrons bound in atoms, molecules, or ions are excluded. The average uses equal path-length weighting, without additional density or volume weighting.

Unlike [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), this quantity averages along a chord rather than over the plasma volume. It equals the local density everywhere on the chord only when that density is uniform. The [line-integrated electron number density](name:line_integrated_electron_number_density) is instead a column abundance; dividing that abundance by its corresponding path length yields this mean when both quantities refer to the same path.

The [line-averaged xenon density](name:line_averaged_xenon_density) applies the same chord-mean operation to xenon ions rather than electrons. The [ratio of line-averaged electron density to Greenwald density](name:ratio_of_line_averaged_electron_density_to_greenwald_density) uses this electron chord mean as its numerator and is a separate normalized quantity.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of electron. The electron-specific chord average is

$$\bar{f} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L f\,dl$$

where $\bar{n}_e$ is the line-averaged electron number density, $n_e$ is the local [electron density](name:electron_density) evaluated along the chord, $L$ is the chord length, and $l$ is distance along the chord. The integration interval and chord length refer to the same complete path.

For that same path, the [line-integrated electron number density](name:line_integrated_electron_number_density) is the corresponding column abundance before division by the chord length. The result characterizes the selected chord rather than a local point; a uniform local density equals its chord average. It differs from [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), which averages the free-electron population over the plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface.

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

worked.name: line_averaged_electron_temperature
worked.description_before: Thermal energy of the bulk electron population expressed as an energy-equivalent temperature, averaged along a plasma chord.
worked.description_after: Temperature of bulk electrons averaged along a specified plasma chord, expressing their random translational energy rather than directed-flow energy.
worked.documentation_before:
Line-averaged electron temperature is the energy-equivalent measure of the mean random kinetic energy of the bulk electron population, averaged along a plasma chord.

The defining path-length average is:

$$
T_{e,\mathrm{line}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L T_e(l)\,dl
$$

where $T_{e,\mathrm{line}}$ is the line-averaged electron temperature, $T_e(l)$ is the local [electron temperature](name:electron_temperature) at path coordinate $l$, and $L$ is the total chord length. The coordinate $l$ measures distance along the specified plasma chord, and the averaging is uniform with respect to path length.

This is an intensive quantity for the bulk electron population, aggregated along the chord rather than summed over electron energies or particle populations. It excludes ion temperatures and differs from the local electron temperature because it combines values along the entire chord.

The line average is a chord-integrated representation of the parent [electron_temperature](name:electron_temperature), whereas [volume_averaged_electron_temperature](name:volume_averaged_electron_temperature) applies a volume average over the confined plasma and is therefore a distinct spatial aggregation.
worked.documentation_after:
Temperature of electrons averaged along a specified plasma chord characterizes the random translational motion of the bulk electron population relative to its local mean flow. It excludes directed bulk-flow energy and is distinct from a radiation temperature.

The local quantity being averaged is the [electron temperature](name:electron_temperature). The spatial scope is the specified plasma chord, with no additional electron-density or emissivity weighting.

Unlike the [volume-averaged electron temperature](name:volume_averaged_electron_temperature), this quantity uses chord-length rather than plasma-volume weighting. The [line-averaged total ion temperature](name:line_averaged_total_ion_temperature) applies the same spatial averaging to the combined thermal ion population instead of electrons.

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

worked.name: line_averaged_helium_3_density
worked.description_before: Line-averaged helium-3 density is the chord-length average of local ionized helium-3 density along a specified viewing path, excluding neutral atoms.
worked.description_after: Number density of helium-3 ions averaged along a specified plasma chord, including all positive charge states and excluding neutral helium-3 atoms.
worked.documentation_before:
Line-averaged helium-3 density is the chord-length average of the local helium-3 ion number density along a specified path. It includes singly ionized $^3\mathrm{He}^{+}$ and fully stripped $^3\mathrm{He}^{2+}$ ions, while excluding neutral helium-3 atoms.

The line average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_{^3\mathrm{He}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_{0}^{L} n_{^3\mathrm{He}}(s)\,\mathrm{d}s
$$

where $\overline{n}_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the line-averaged density, $n_{^3\mathrm{He}}(s)$ is the local charge-state-summed density at path coordinate $s$, and $L$ is the chord length. Unlike the volume average in [volume-averaged helium-3 density](name:volume_averaged_helium_3_density), this quantity weights each position uniformly by distance along the path. It is a path-integrated representation of [helium-3 density](name:helium_3_density), not a separate charge-state population.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of helium 3. The helium-3-specific chord average is

$$
\bar{n}_{{}^3\mathrm{He}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}\,dl
$$

where $\bar{n}_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the line-averaged helium-3 ion number density, $n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the local [helium-3 density](name:helium_3_density) evaluated along the chord, $L$ is the stated chord length, and $l$ is distance along that chord.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

This quantity describes the specified chord rather than a local value at a single point. It differs from [volume-averaged helium-3 density](name:volume_averaged_helium_3_density), which averages the same species population over the plasma volume. Its isotope-specific counterpart, [line-averaged helium-4 density](name:line_averaged_helium_4_density), applies the same chord-average operation to helium-4 rather than helium-3.

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

worked.name: line_averaged_helium_4_density
worked.description_before: Chord-averaged helium-4 ion number density along a specified line of sight through the plasma, representing the path mean of local fusion-ash concentration.
worked.description_after: Number density of helium-4 ions averaged along a specified plasma chord, including all positive charge states and excluding neutral helium-4 atoms.
worked.documentation_before:
The line-averaged helium-4 ion number density is the path average of the local helium-4 ion density along a specified chord through the plasma. It represents an effective density for that chord, not the local value at a point or a volume-wide mean.

The line average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_{{}^4\mathrm{He}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_{0}^{L} n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}(l)\,dl
$$

where $n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}(l)$ is the local helium-4 ion number density from [helium_4_density](name:helium_4_density), $l$ is distance along the chord, and $L$ is the chord length; $l$ and $L$ are measured in m.

The average includes the local helium-4 ion density along the specified path and uses uniform path-length weighting. Unlike [volume_averaged_helium_4_density](name:volume_averaged_helium_4_density), it is not averaged over the confined plasma volume.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of helium 4. Line averaging preserves the helium-4-specific charge-state relation:

$$
\bar{n}_{\mathrm{He4}} = \bar{n}_{\mathrm{He4}^{+}} + \bar{n}_{\mathrm{He4}^{2+}}
$$

where $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the line-averaged helium-4 ion number density, $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{He4}^{+}}$ is the line-averaged singly ionized helium-4 number density, and $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{He4}^{2+}}$ is the line-averaged doubly ionized helium-4 number density. All three averages refer to the same chord.

The underlying local quantity is [helium-4 density](name:helium_4_density); the chord average is neither a neutral-helium density nor a single-charge-state density. It does not specify the local density at an individual point.

Unlike [volume-averaged helium-4 density](name:volume_averaged_helium_4_density), which averages over the confined plasma volume, this quantity characterizes the specified chord. It uses the same chord-averaging convention as [line-averaged hydrogen density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density).

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: line_averaged_hydrogen_density
worked.description_before: Line-averaged number density of hydrogen (protium) ions in the plasma, giving the path-length-normalized H+ concentration along a specified chord.
worked.description_after: Number density of hydrogen (protium) ions averaged along a specified plasma chord, including its sole positive charge state and excluding neutral atoms.
worked.documentation_before:
The line-averaged hydrogen density quantifies the mean concentration of protium ions along a specified chord through the plasma. It represents the path-integrated hydrogen ion content normalized by the chord length.

The line average is defined as

$$
\overline{n}_H = \frac{1}{L}\int_{\mathcal{C}} n_H(\mathbf{r}(l))\,dl
$$

where $\overline{n}_H$ is the line-averaged hydrogen density, $n_H(\mathbf{r}(l))$ is the local protium-ion number density at position $\mathbf{r}(l)$ along the chord, $l$ is the path-length coordinate, $\mathcal{C}$ is the specified chord, and $L$ is its total length.

The quantity applies to charged protium ions, with any included protium ion charge states summed before the line average; neutral atomic hydrogen and heavier hydrogenic isotopes are excluded. It is a chord average rather than the local [hydrogen density](name:hydrogen_density) at a point or the volume average represented by [volume_averaged_hydrogen_density](name:volume_averaged_hydrogen_density).

Unlike [line_averaged_total_ion_density](name:line_averaged_total_ion_density), it does not include other ion species or hydrogen isotopes. The path-length normalization preserves the same density meaning as the parent local quantity while replacing its pointwise value with an average along the chord.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of hydrogen. Protium has only one positive atomic charge state, giving the species-specific identity

$$
\bar{n}_{\mathrm{H}} = \bar{n}_{\mathrm{H}^{+}}
$$

where $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the line-averaged hydrogen ion number density and $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{H}^{+}}$ is the line-averaged singly ionized protium number density, both referring to the same chord.

The species is protium alone, not the combined hydrogen-isotope population; [line-averaged deuterium density](name:line_averaged_deuterium_density) describes the corresponding quantity for a separate isotope.

This quantity is a chord average rather than a local evaluation or an unnormalized line integral. It differs from [volume-averaged hydrogen density](name:volume_averaged_hydrogen_density), which averages the same local species density over the plasma volume instead of along the specified chord.

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: line_averaged_iron_density
worked.description_before: Line-averaged iron density is the path-length mean of total iron impurity-ion number density, summed over Fe1+ through Fe26+.
worked.description_after: Number density of iron ions averaged along a specified plasma chord, including all positive charge states and excluding neutral iron atoms.
worked.documentation_before:
Line-averaged iron density is the chord-length mean of the total iron ion number density along a specified line of sight. It includes all ionization states from Fe$^{1+}$ through Fe$^{26+}$ and does not resolve their individual contributions.

The line average is defined as

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe,line}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_{\mathrm{Fe}}(l)\,dl
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe,line}}$ is the line-averaged density, $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}(l)$ is the local iron ion number density at path coordinate $l$, and $L$ is the total chord length.

The local quantity being averaged is the charge-state-summed [iron density](name:iron_density). This chord average is distinct from [line_averaged_argon_density](name:line_averaged_argon_density), which applies the same path averaging to argon ions, and from a volume-averaged iron density, which averages over a plasma volume rather than a line of sight.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of iron. Line averaging preserves the iron-specific charge-state decomposition:

$$
\bar{n}_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \sum_{q=1}^{26} \bar{n}_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}
$$

where $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the line-averaged iron-ion number density, $q$ is the positive ionic charge number, and $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}$ is the line-averaged number density of iron ions in charge state $q$. Every partial density is averaged over the same chord; 26 is the atomic number of iron.

Unlike [volume-averaged iron density](name:volume_averaged_iron_density), this quantity averages along the specified chord rather than over the plasma volume. It is the iron counterpart of [line-averaged argon density](name:line_averaged_argon_density), with the same chord-average convention.

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: line_averaged_lithium_density
worked.description_before: Path-length-averaged total number density of lithium ions along a specified plasma chord, summed over Li+ through fully stripped Li3+ and excluding neutral lithium.
worked.description_after: Number density of lithium ions averaged along a specified plasma chord, including all positive charge states and excluding neutral lithium atoms.
worked.documentation_before:
This is the path-length average of lithium ion number density, summed over all ionization stages from Li$^+$ through fully stripped Li$^{3+}$, along a specified chord through the plasma.

The chord average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{Li} \rangle_L = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_{Li}(s)\,ds
$$

where $n_{Li}(s)$ is the local lithium ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $s$ is path length in meters along the chord, and $L$ is the total chord length in meters.

This quantity weights each path-length element equally and excludes neutral lithium. It differs from the flux-surface-averaged lithium density at the plasma boundary, which averages over a separatrix, and from [volume-averaged lithium density](name:volume_averaged_lithium_density), which averages over confined plasma volume.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of lithium. The lithium-specific chord average is

$$
\bar{n}_{\mathrm{Li}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_{\mathrm{Li}}\,dl
$$

where $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the line-averaged lithium ion number density, $n_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the local lithium ion number density evaluated along the chord, $L$ is the chord length, and $l$ is distance along the chord.

The result represents the selected chord rather than a local value at a single point; a uniform local density equals its chord average. It differs from [volume-averaged lithium density](name:volume_averaged_lithium_density), which averages the same ion population over the plasma volume. For the same chord, lithium contributes one species component to the [line-averaged total ion density](name:line_averaged_total_ion_density).

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.
