The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: line_averaged_time_derivative_of_electron_density
worked.description_before: Rate of change of free-electron number density averaged along a specified plasma chord, positive for density buildup and negative for depletion.
worked.description_after: Rate of change of free-electron number density averaged along a specified plasma chord, including thermal and nonthermal electrons and excluding bound electrons.
worked.documentation_before:
Number density of electron

The temporal rate is defined by

$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial t}$$

where $\dot{\bar{n}}_e$ is the rate of change, $\bar{n}_e$ is the [line-averaged electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density), and $t$ is time. The chord mean is $\bar{n}_e = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_e\,dl$, where $n_e$ is the local free-electron number density evaluated along the chord, $L$ is the chord length, and $l$ is distance along it.

The population comprises free electrons and excludes electrons bound in atoms, ions, or molecules. This quantity is a net density-evolution rate, not an isolated electron source term: particle transport and electron production or loss can all contribute. Unlike the derivative of electron column density, it includes division by chord length.

For a fixed chord and chord length, temporal differentiation commutes with chord averaging, so this quantity equals the chord average of the local [time derivative of electron density](name:time_derivative_of_electron_density). It differs from the [volume-averaged time derivative of electron density](name:volume_averaged_time_derivative_of_electron_density), which averages over a plasma volume rather than along a chord.

Sign convention: Positive when the free-electron number density averaged along the specified chord increases with time.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of electron. The electron-specific defining expression is

$$
\frac{\partial \bar{n}_e}{\partial t}
$$

where $\bar{n}_e$ is the [line-averaged electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density) and $t$ is time.

For a fixed chord, line averaging and time differentiation commute, making this the chord-averaged specialization of the [electron-density time derivative](name:time_derivative_of_electron_density). It represents the selected chord rather than a local value or the [volume-averaged electron-density time derivative](name:volume_averaged_time_derivative_of_electron_density). It describes net density evolution, not an isolated electron production or loss term.

Sign convention: Positive when the line-averaged free-electron number density increases with time.

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

The time derivative is the rate of change of a quantity with time at a fixed point or label.

worked.name: line_averaged_toroidal_plasma_velocity
worked.description_before: Line-of-sight average of the plasma bulk velocity projected onto the toroidal direction, representing Doppler-sensitive motion around the machine axis.
worked.description_after: Signed toroidal plasma flow averaged along a viewing chord, describing directed motion about the symmetry axis rather than random thermal motion.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the effective toroidal bulk-flow velocity of plasma averaged along a diagnostic line of sight. It represents motion around the machine axis rather than a local velocity at one point or an accumulated line signal.

For a line of sight with path length $L$, the line-averaged toroidal velocity is defined by

$$
\overline{v}_{\phi} = \frac{1}{L}\int_{0}^{L} v_{\phi}(\ell)\,d\ell
$$

where $\ell$ is distance along the line of sight, $L$ is its total path length, and $v_{\phi}(\ell)=\mathbf{v}(\ell)\cdot\hat{\phi}$ is the local toroidal component of the plasma bulk velocity. The normalization by $L$ distinguishes this velocity from a line-integrated quantity. The generic plasma designation does not select a particular ion species or charge state, unlike species-resolved quantities such as [toroidal deuterium velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).

Sign convention: Positive when the toroidal bulk velocity points in the direction of increasing $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.
worked.documentation_after:
This quantity characterizes directed plasma motion around the symmetry axis at the level of a specified viewing chord, rather than at a single plasma position.

The local toroidal component entering the line average is

$$
v_\phi = \mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\phi}
$$

where $v_\phi$ is the toroidal plasma velocity, $\mathbf{v}$ is the plasma bulk velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle. The right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The chord-level aggregation distinguishes this quantity from a local, species-resolved [toroidal ion velocity](name:toroidal_ion_velocity). It is not an unnormalized velocity path integral, a projection of the full velocity onto the viewing direction, or a thermal velocity spread.

Sign convention: Positive when the chord-averaged toroidal plasma motion is toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

worked.name: line_averaged_total_ion_density
worked.description_before: Total ion number density averaged along a specified plasma chord, summing all ion species and charge states, including thermal and non-thermal ions.
worked.description_after: Number density of ions averaged along a specified plasma chord, summed over all ion species and positive charge states, excluding electrons and neutral particles.
worked.documentation_before:
The line-averaged total ion density is the chord average of the local [total ion density](name:total_ion_number_density), including all ion species, resolved charge states, and thermal and non-thermal ion populations. It excludes electron density.

$$
n_{\mathrm{i,line}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_{\mathrm{i,total}}(l)\,dl
$$

where $l$ is distance along the chord, $L$ is chord length, $n_{\mathrm{i,total}}(l)$ is local total ion density, and $n_{\mathrm{i,line}}$ is the resulting line average. Unlike the [volume-averaged total ion density](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_density), it averages along a chord rather than throughout a volume.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of ion. Line averaging preserves the species sum:

$$
\bar{n}_{i,\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_s \bar{n}_s
$$

where $\bar{n}_{i,\mathrm{tot}}$ is the line-averaged total ion number density, $s$ labels ion species, and $\bar{n}_s$ is the line-averaged number density of species $s$, summed over all positive charge states. Every species contribution uses the same chord.

Thermal and nonthermal ions are included; electrons and neutral particles are excluded. Each ion is counted once regardless of its charge, so this is a particle number density rather than a charge-weighted density.

The result characterizes the selected chord rather than a local point or a plasma-volume average. For the same chord, [line-averaged lithium density](name:line_averaged_lithium_density) supplies the lithium contribution to this total.

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

worked.name: line_averaged_total_ion_temperature
worked.description_before: Density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion population, with all species and charge states contributing by number density and averaged along a specified plasma chord.
worked.description_after: Temperature of thermal ions averaged along a specified plasma chord, with local number-density weighting over all ion species and charge states.
worked.documentation_before:
The line-averaged total ion temperature is the line average of the local density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion population, including all included thermal ion species and charge states. It represents random thermal motion and excludes directed bulk-flow energy.

The chord average is defined by

$$
T_{i,\mathrm{line}} = \frac{\int_{\mathcal{C}} T_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\ell)\,d\ell}{\int_{\mathcal{C}}d\ell}
$$

where $T_{i,\mathrm{line}}$ is the line-averaged quantity, $T_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\ell)$ is the local [total ion temperature](name:total_ion_temperature), $\ell$ is path length along the chord, and $\mathcal{C}$ is the specified chord. Species and charge states are combined by number density before the line average is taken. Unlike the [volume-averaged total ion temperature](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature), this quantity weights positions by chord length rather than plasma volume.
worked.documentation_after:
Temperature of ions averaged along a specified plasma chord characterizes the random translational motion of the combined thermal ion population relative to each population's local mean flow. It excludes directed bulk-flow energy and nonthermal ion energy.

The local quantity being averaged is the [total ion temperature](name:total_ion_temperature), defined as the number-density-weighted mean over all thermal ion species and all their charge states, not a sum of their temperatures. The spatial operation is the [line average](concept:line_averaged) along the specified plasma chord, with no additional ion-density or emissivity weighting along that chord.

Unlike the [volume-averaged total ion temperature](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature), this quantity uses chord-length rather than plasma-volume weighting. The [line-averaged electron temperature](name:line_averaged_electron_temperature) applies the same spatial averaging to bulk electrons instead of the combined thermal ion population.

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

worked.name: line_averaged_tritium_density
worked.description_before: Chord-averaged number density of tritium ions, obtained by averaging local tritium ion density along a specified chord.
worked.description_after: Number density of tritium ions averaged along a specified plasma chord, including its sole positive charge state and excluding neutral tritium atoms.
worked.documentation_before:
Chord-averaged tritium ion density is the path-length mean of the local tritium ion number density along a specified chord. It is derived from the local [tritium_density](name:tritium_density) and represents the chord-integrated fuel content normalized by chord length.

$$
\overline{n}_T = \frac{1}{L} \int_0^L n_T(\ell)\,d\ell
$$

where $\overline{n}_T$ is the chord-averaged density, $n_T(\ell)$ is the local tritium ion density at path coordinate $\ell$, and $L$ is the chord length. The average includes the specified chord segment and is distinct from the confined-volume mean [volume_averaged_tritium_density](name:volume_averaged_tritium_density) and from the corresponding helium-4 quantity [line_averaged_helium_4_density](name:line_averaged_helium_4_density).
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of tritium. Line averaging preserves the tritium-specific charge-state identity:

$$
\bar{n}_{\mathrm{T}} = \bar{n}_{\mathrm{T}^{+}}
$$

where $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the line-averaged tritium ion number density and $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{T}^{+}}$ is the line-averaged number density of singly ionized tritium on the same chord.

The underlying local quantity is [tritium density](name:tritium_density). The chord average is distinct from a local point value and from a plasma-volume average.

For the same chord, adding the [line-averaged deuterium density](name:line_averaged_deuterium_density) gives the [line-averaged deuterium–tritium density](name:line_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density), which treats both fuel isotopes as one effective species.

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: line_averaged_tungsten_density
worked.description_before: Line-of-sight average of the number density of positively charged tungsten ions, summed over all ionization states and excluding neutral tungsten.
worked.description_after: Number density of tungsten ions averaged along a specified plasma chord, summed over all charge states and excluding neutral tungsten atoms.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the line-of-sight average of the charge-state-summed number density of positively charged tungsten ions.

$$
\bar n_{\mathrm{W}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_{\mathcal{L}} \left[\sum_{Z=1}^{74} n_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}}(l)\right] \, dl
$$

Here, $\bar n_{\mathrm{W}}$ is the line-averaged tungsten-ion number density, $\mathcal{L}$ is the specified averaging line, $L$ is its total length, $l$ is distance along that line, $Z$ is the positive tungsten charge-state index, and $n_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}}(l)$ is the local number density of tungsten ions in charge state $Z$. The sum includes all positive tungsten ionization states and excludes neutral tungsten.

The quantity applies to the aggregate tungsten-ion population along the specified line and is averaged over that line rather than evaluated locally or averaged over volume. It therefore differs from the local or otherwise spatially averaged [tungsten-ion density](name:tungsten_density) by its line-of-sight aggregation, and from [volume-averaged tungsten density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density) by using a line rather than the enclosed plasma volume.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of tungsten. For tungsten, the defining chord average is

$$
\bar{n}_{\mathrm{W}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_{\mathrm{W}}\,dl
$$

where $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{W}}$ is the line-averaged tungsten ion number density, $n_{\mathrm{W}}$ is the local tungsten ion number density evaluated along the specified chord, $L$ is the chord length, and $l$ is distance along that chord.

This quantity is not an unnormalized line integral or a local density at a particular point; it equals the local density throughout the chord when that density is uniform. Unlike [volume-averaged tungsten density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density), it averages over a chord rather than the plasma volume. It is the tungsten counterpart of [line-averaged xenon density](name:line_averaged_xenon_density), with the species changed but the averaging convention unchanged.

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: line_averaged_xenon_density
worked.description_before: Number density of xenon ions averaged along a chord through the plasma, summed over all ionization states from singly ionized through fully stripped xenon and excluding neutral xenon atoms.
worked.description_after: Number density of xenon ions averaged along a specified plasma chord, including all positive charge states and excluding neutral xenon atoms.
worked.documentation_before:
The line-averaged xenon ion number density is the chord-length mean of the local [xenon density](name:xenon_density), which sums xenon ions from singly ionized through fully stripped xenon and excludes neutral xenon atoms. It represents the xenon ion content sampled by a specified chord, not the local value at any single point unless the local density is uniform along that chord.

The chord average is defined by

$$
\bar{n}_{\mathrm{Xe},L} = \frac{1}{L}\int_{\mathcal{C}} n_\mathrm{Xe}(\ell)\, d\ell
$$

where $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{Xe},L}$ is the line-averaged xenon ion number density, $\mathcal{C}$ is the chord segment over which the average is defined, $L = \int_{\mathcal{C}} d\ell$ is its path length, $\ell$ is distance along the chord, and $n_\mathrm{Xe}(\ell)$ is the local [xenon density](name:xenon_density) evaluated on the chord.

The species aggregation is performed over charge states before the line average: $n_\mathrm{Xe}(\ell)=\sum_{z=1}^{54} n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{z+}}(\ell)$, where $z$ is the xenon ionic charge-state index, $n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{z+}}$ is the partial density of xenon ions carrying charge $ze$, and $e$ is the elementary charge. The physical population is charged xenon ions located on the chord segment through the plasma; neutral xenon atoms and charge-state-resolved xenon densities are excluded.

This quantity differs from [volume-averaged xenon density](name:volume_averaged_xenon_density), which averages the same local xenon density over the plasma volume, and from [xenon density at magnetic axis](name:xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis), which evaluates it at the magnetic-axis locus. It is the xenon counterpart of [line-averaged argon density](name:line_averaged_argon_density) under the same chord-mean convention.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of xenon. The xenon-specific chord average is

$$
\bar{n}_{\mathrm{Xe}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_{\mathrm{Xe}}\,dl
$$

where $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the line-averaged xenon ion number density, $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the [local xenon ion number density](name:xenon_density) evaluated along the chord, $L$ is the chord length, and $l$ is distance along the chord.

The result represents the selected chord rather than a local value at a single point; a uniform local density equals its chord average. It differs from [volume-averaged xenon density](name:volume_averaged_xenon_density), which averages the same ion population over the plasma volume. For the same chord, xenon contributes one species component to the [line-averaged total ion density](name:line_averaged_total_ion_density).

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: line_integrated_electron_number_density
worked.description_before: Line-integrated electron number density is the free-electron column abundance along the complete propagation path, including forward and return segments when present.
worked.description_after: Line-integrated electron number density is the free-electron column content along the complete propagation path, including forward and return segments when present.
worked.documentation_before:
Line-integrated electron number density counts free electrons accumulated along the complete electromagnetic-wave propagation path. It is the complete-path specialization of [electron number density](name:electron_number_density).

The defining line integral is

$$\int_0^L f\,dl$$

where $N_e$ is the free-electron column abundance, $n_e$ is the local free-electron number density, $l$ is distance along the propagation path, and $L$ is the total path length.

For reflected paths, forward and return segments both contribute, without a factor-of-two correction. Electrons bound in atoms, molecules, or ions are excluded.

This quantity is neither a local volume density nor the [line-averaged electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density), which divides the corresponding line integral by the length of its averaging path.
worked.documentation_after:
Line-integrated electron number density represents the free-electron column content associated with the complete propagation path. It includes thermal and nonthermal free electrons and excludes electrons bound in atoms or ions.

The electron column content is defined by

$$\int_0^L f\,dl$$

where $N_e$ is the electron column content, $n_e$ is the local [electron density](name:electron_density), $l$ is distance along the propagation path, and $L$ is its total length.

For reflected propagation, both forward and return segments contribute, without a factor-of-two correction. This is the column quantity described by [electron number density](name:electron_number_density), not a local volume density. It is not divided by path length: the corresponding [line-averaged electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density) equals $N_e/L$ when evaluated over the same path.

The line integral is the integral of a quantity along a stated path.

worked.name: line_integrated_neutral_beam_radiance_at_spectral_line
worked.description_before: Photon radiance of one of nine motional-Stark components of fast neutral-beam emission, integrated along a sightline crossing the beam.
worked.description_after: Photon radiance of an individual motional-Stark component of fast neutral-beam emission at the specified spectral line, integrated along a sightline crossing the beam.
worked.documentation_before:
Photon radiance at the spectral line quantifies emission from an individual Stark-split component of fast neutral-beam atoms along a viewing sightline. The splitting arises from the Lorentz electric field experienced by the moving atoms.

In the optically thin limit, the defining line integral is

$$\int_0^L f\,dl$$

where $L_i$ is the photon radiance of component $i$, $i$ identifies one of the nine Stark-split components, $j_i$ is the local directional photon emissivity integrated over that component's wavelength interval, $l$ is distance along the sightline crossing the neutral beam, and $l_{\max}$ is the total path length.

Each value applies to one component, not the sum over the nine-component multiplet. It is integrated over the selected component's wavelength interval rather than resolved per wavelength, and it counts photons rather than their energy. Unlike local emissivity, it includes emission accumulated along the sightline.

This quantity is the neutral-beam-specific case of [motional-Stark spectral-line radiance](name:motional_stark_radiance_of_spectral_line) and a component-resolved instance of [photon radiance at a spectral line](name:photon_radiance_at_spectral_line).
worked.documentation_after:
The photon radiance at the specified spectral line resolves one of the nine motional-Stark components emitted by fast neutral-beam atoms. The splitting arises from the Lorentz electric field experienced by the moving atoms.

For optically thin emission, the component radiance is

$$\int_0^L f\,dl$$

where $L_k$ is the photon radiance of component $k$, $k$ labels one of the nine components, $j_k$ is its directional photon emissivity integrated over that component, $l$ is distance along the sightline, and $\ell_b$ is the total path length through the emitting beam.

Each value includes the selected component's spectral extent but excludes the other eight components; it is not a radiance density per wavelength interval or a local emissivity. Summing the nine component radiances gives the motional-Stark contribution to the [neutral-beam radiance at the spectral line](name:neutral_beam_radiance_at_spectral_line).

The line integral is the integral of a quantity along a stated path.

worked.name: line_integrated_neutron_emissivity
worked.description_before: Neutron emissivity integrated along a detector line of sight gives the neutron brightness associated with that viewing path.
worked.description_after: Neutron emissivity accumulated along a detector line of sight defines the neutron-source brightness associated with that viewing path.
worked.documentation_before:
neutron emissivity

The defining line integral is

$$\int_0^L f\,dl$$

where $\mathcal{B}_n$ is the neutron brightness, $\varepsilon_n$ is the local [neutron emissivity](name:neutron_emissivity), $l$ is distance along the line of sight, and $L$ is the total integration-path length.

This quantity integrates neutron-number emission along the specified path, not over the source volume. It is distinct from the detector count rate, neutron energy flux, and the [total neutron emission rate](name:total_neutron_rate), which aggregates neutron production throughout the plasma.
worked.documentation_after:
neutron emissivity. The quantity is the [line integral](concept:line_integrated)

$$
\int_0^L \varepsilon_n\,dl
$$

where $\varepsilon_n$ is the local [neutron emissivity](name:neutron_emissivity), evaluated along the viewing path, $l$ is distance along that path, and $L$ is its total integration length.

The accumulation includes neutron production along the stated path without selecting a particular production mechanism. It is not an integral over the source volume and includes no detector-response or solid-angle weighting. It is therefore distinct from the [neutron flux incident on the detector](name:neutron_flux_of_neutron_detector) and the [accepted detection-event rate](name:rate_of_neutron_detector).

The line integral is the integral of a quantity along a stated path.

worked.name: linear_thermal_electron_decay_time_volume_averaged_due_to_disruption
worked.description_before: Linear 20–80% decay time of the volume-averaged thermal electron temperature during a disruption, based on its pre-disruptive value.
worked.description_after: Linear-extrapolated decay time of the volume-averaged thermal electron temperature during a disruption, defined from custom fractional thresholds or the fixed 20–80% interval.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the characteristic disruption decay time of the volume-averaged thermal electron temperature, determined by a linear 20–80% construction. It describes the reduction of the bulk electron thermal state over the plasma volume, rather than a local temperature or an exponential e-folding time.

The defining relation is

$$
\tau_{e,V}^{20\text{--}80} = \frac{t(0.2)-t(0.8)}{0.6}
$$

where $\tau_{e,V}^{20\text{--}80}$ is the decay time, $t(f)$ is the time at which the volume-averaged temperature $T_{e,V}(t)$ reaches the fraction $f$ of its pre-disruptive value, and $f$ is a dimensionless temperature fraction. The reference $T_{e,V,0}$ is the pre-disruptive volume-averaged thermal electron temperature, so $t(0.8)$ marks the 80% level and $t(0.2)$ marks the 20% level. For a decreasing temperature, $t(0.2)>t(0.8)$.

The quantity applies to the thermal electron population and uses a volume average over the plasma rather than a pointwise or magnetic-axis value. It is specific to the temperature loss occurring during a disruption and excludes decay times obtained from an exponential e-folding fit or from another electron-temperature reduction interval.

The same linear 20–80% construction applied at the magnetic axis is [linear electron decay time at the magnetic axis due to disruption](name:linear_electron_decay_time_at_magnetic_axis_due_to_disruption); [electron decay time at the magnetic axis due to disruption](name:electron_decay_time_at_magnetic_axis_due_to_disruption) instead represents an exponential e-folding timescale for a local temperature decrease.
worked.documentation_after:
This quantity is the linear-extrapolated decay time of the volume-averaged thermal electron temperature during a disruption. It characterizes the temperature decrease between two specified fractions of its pre-disruption value without requiring the entire decrease to follow a linear law.

The linear decay time is defined by:

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{L}}=\frac{t(X_2)-t(X_1)}{X_1-X_2}
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{L}}$ is the linear decay time, $X_1$ and $X_2$ are the upper and lower fractional temperature thresholds with $0<X_2<X_1\leq1$, and $t(X)$ is the time when the volume-averaged thermal electron temperature reaches the fraction $X$ of its pre-disruption value during the specified decrease. The denominator extrapolates the temperature decline between the thresholds to a decrease equal to the full pre-disruption value; the result is not merely the elapsed time between threshold crossings.

Custom linear definitions use their specified threshold fractions. The fixed 20–80% definition uses $X_1=0.8$ and $X_2=0.2$, giving $\tau_{\mathrm{L}}=[t(0.2)-t(0.8)]/0.6$.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume. Here, the thermal [electron temperature](name:electron_temperature) is averaged over the stated plasma volume before applying the decay-time definition. This is not an average of local decay times or a density-weighted temperature average.

The [on-axis linear electron decay time](name:linear_electron_decay_time_at_magnetic_axis_due_to_disruption) instead characterizes the local temperature decrease at the magnetic axis. The [volume-averaged exponential electron decay time](name:volume_averaged_electron_decay_time_due_to_disruption) is an e-folding time rather than a linear-threshold extrapolation, and the two conventions are not interchangeable. This temperature-decay quantity is distinct from the [plasma-current decay time](name:plasma_decay_time_due_to_disruption) and the [thermal-energy decay time](name:thermal_energy_decay_time_due_to_disruption).

worked.name: neon_density
worked.description_before: Number density of neon impurity ions, summed over the included ionization states; line-averaged and volume-averaged forms express the same elemental content.
worked.description_after: Number density of neon ions across all positive charge states, excluding neutral neon, evaluated locally or with a specified spatial average.
worked.documentation_before:
Neon density is the number of neon impurity ions per unit volume, summed over all included charged ionization states. It represents elemental neon content rather than the density of one selected charge state; neutral neon atoms are excluded.

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ne}} = \sum_{z \in \mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{Ne}}} n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the charge-state-summed neon ion density, $n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{z+}}$ is the density of neon ions in charge state $z+$, and $\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the set of included charged ionization states.

This species-specific quantity is a member of density. The same charge-state-summed field may be spatially averaged; [volume_averaged_neon_density](name:volume_averaged_neon_density) represents its volume average, while a charge-state-resolved quantity such as [ion_charge_state_density](name:ion_charge_state_density) selects one ionization state and is not equivalent.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of neon. The local number density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ne}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Ne}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the number density of neon ions, $N_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the number of neon ions, and $V$ is physical volume.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded. The quantity may be evaluated locally or spatially averaged; it does not select a particular location or averaging domain.

[Line-averaged neon density](name:line_averaged_neon_density) is the line-averaged form, while [volume-averaged neon density](name:volume_averaged_neon_density) is averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface. These are spatial averages of the density, not integrated particle inventories. In contrast, [ion charge state density](name:ion_charge_state_density) selects a single ionization state rather than the charge-state-summed density.

worked.name: parallel_current_density_flux_surface_averaged_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive
worked.description_before: Flux-surface-averaged field-aligned conventional plasma current density generated non-inductively by electromagnetic-wave–particle interactions.
worked.description_after: Flux-surface-averaged field-aligned conventional plasma current density generated non-inductively by electromagnetic-wave–particle interactions.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the scalar field-aligned component of the conventional plasma current generated by electromagnetic-wave–particle interactions. It represents the wave-driven contribution to current flowing along the magnetic field on a magnetic flux surface.

For a magnetic flux surface labeled by the poloidal flux coordinate $\psi$, the flux-surface-averaged parallel current density is defined by

$$
j_{\parallel,\mathrm{FSA}}(\psi) = \frac{\left\langle \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{wave}} \cdot \mathbf{B} \right\rangle_{\psi}}{B_0(\psi)}
$$

where $j_{\parallel,\mathrm{FSA}}$ is this scalar current-density quantity, $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{wave}}$ is the conventional current-density contribution generated by wave–particle interactions, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes averaging over the flux surface labeled by $\psi$, and $B_0(\psi)$ is the reference magnetic-field magnitude used for the parallel-current normalization.

The quantity applies to the wave-driven current contribution from the plasma populations participating in the electromagnetic-wave interaction and uses a flux-surface average rather than a local value. It excludes inductive current and current contributions from non-wave mechanisms, and it is distinct from the full vector flux-surface-averaged wave-driven current density.

It is the magnetic-field-aligned scalar projection of that vector parent, retaining only the component parallel to the local magnetic field; [parallel current density due to ohmic current drive](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_ohmic_current_drive) instead represents the inductive resistive contribution.

Sign convention: Positive when the wave-driven conventional current flows in the direction of the magnetic field, so that $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{wave}} \cdot \mathbf{B} > 0$.

worked.name: per_toroidal_mode_flux_surface_averaged_parallel_wave_electric_field_amplitude
worked.description_before: Peak strength of the magnetic-field-parallel coherent-wave electric field for each toroidal mode after power-deposition-weighted complex averaging over a closed magnetic flux surface.
worked.description_after: Peak strength of the magnetic-field-parallel coherent-wave electric field for one toroidal Fourier mode, obtained after power-deposition-weighted complex averaging over a closed magnetic flux surface.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the nonnegative amplitude of the component of a coherent-wave [electric-field](name:electric_field) phasor parallel to the equilibrium magnetic field. It represents the toroidal-mode-resolved field strength after power-deposition-density-weighted averaging over a closed magnetic flux surface.

The real oscillation associated with the weighted modal phasor has the form

$$f(t) = A\cos(\omega t + \varphi)$$

where $E_{\parallel,n}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the real parallel field associated with the weighted modal phasor, $t$ is time, $A_{\parallel,n}$ is its peak amplitude, $\omega$ is the wave angular frequency, $\varphi_{\parallel,n}$ is its temporal phase, and $n$ is the integer toroidal Fourier mode number.

The amplitude is $A_{\parallel,n}=|\langle p_{\mathrm{dep}}\widetilde E_{\parallel,n}\rangle/\langle p_{\mathrm{dep}}\rangle|$, where $\widetilde E_{\parallel,n}$ is the local complex parallel modal field and $p_{\mathrm{dep}}$ is the coherent-wave power-deposition density used as the weight. The flux-surface average is $\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$, where $f$ is the quantity being averaged, $S$ is the closed magnetic flux surface, $dS$ is its surface-area element, $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic flux labeling the surface, and $\nabla$ denotes the spatial gradient. The weighted amplitude is defined only when the surface-averaged weight is nonzero.

The quantity resolves one toroidal mode; no summation over modes or division by the mode number is implied. It excludes perpendicular field components and complex phase information, and it is a peak amplitude rather than a root-mean-square field. The modulus is taken after complex averaging, so phase cancelation is retained; averaging pointwise amplitudes defines a different quantity.

It is the toroidal-mode-resolved specialization of the [flux-surface-averaged parallel wave electric-field amplitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_parallel_wave_electric_field_amplitude). Like the [right-hand circularly polarized amplitude per toroidal mode](name:per_toroidal_mode_right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_amplitude), it uses power-deposition-weighted complex averaging, but it selects the magnetic-field-parallel component rather than a circularly polarized perpendicular component.
worked.documentation_after:
This quantity is the nonnegative amplitude of the magnetic-field-parallel component of a coherent-wave electric-field phasor for one toroidal Fourier mode. It represents the surface-representative field strength after power-deposition-weighted complex averaging.

Its defining relation is

$$\langle f\rangle = \oint f\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|$$

where $\mathcal{E}_{\parallel,n}^{\mathrm{amp}}$ is the amplitude defined here, $\widetilde{E}_{\parallel,n}$ is the local complex electric-field component parallel to the background magnetic field, $n$ is the integer toroidal Fourier mode number, and $p_{\mathrm{dep}}$ is the local wave-power-deposition density supplying the additional weighting. Angle brackets denote the flux-surface-average operator, and vertical bars denote the complex modulus. The normalization requires nonzero surface-averaged deposition.

The quantity resolves one toroidal mode on each closed magnetic flux surface; no summation over modes or division by mode number is implied. Complex averaging precedes taking the modulus, so phase cancelation contributes to the result. This is neither an average of pointwise amplitudes nor a root-mean-square field. It excludes perpendicular field components and does not retain the phase of the averaged phasor.

It is the toroidal-mode-resolved specialization of the [flux-surface-averaged parallel wave electric-field amplitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_parallel_wave_electric_field_amplitude); amplitudes of separate modes are not additive. The [right-hand circularly polarized amplitude per toroidal mode](name:per_toroidal_mode_right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_amplitude) applies the corresponding surface-representative construction to the E-minus polarization rather than the magnetic-field-parallel component.

The amplitude is the peak magnitude of a sinusoidally varying quantity.

The flux-surface average is the average of a quantity over a closed magnetic flux surface, weighted by the inverse magnitude of the poloidal flux gradient.

worked.name: poloidal_electron_beta_flux_surface_averaged_at_pedestal_top
worked.description_before: Poloidal flux-surface-averaged electron beta at the pedestal top is the dimensionless ratio of flux-surface-averaged electron kinetic pressure to the magnetic pressure associated with the flux-surface-averaged poloidal magnetic field, evaluated at the fitted core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier.
worked.description_after: Poloidal flux-surface-averaged electron beta at the pedestal top is the dimensionless ratio of flux-surface-averaged electron kinetic pressure to the magnetic pressure associated with the flux-surface-averaged poloidal magnetic field, evaluated at the fitted core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier.
worked.documentation_before:
Poloidal flux-surface-averaged electron beta at the pedestal top is the electron contribution to poloidal beta on the flux surface at the fitted core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It compares the flux-surface-averaged electron kinetic pressure with the magnetic pressure formed from the flux-surface-averaged magnitude of the poloidal magnetic field on the same surface.

The defining relation is:

$$
\beta_{p,e}^{\mathrm{fs}}(\psi_{\mathrm{top}}) = \frac{2\mu_0\,\langle p_e\rangle_{\psi_{\mathrm{top}}}}{\left(\langle |B_p|\rangle_{\psi_{\mathrm{top}}}\right)^2}
$$

where $\psi_{\mathrm{top}}$ is the poloidal magnetic flux coordinate labeling the pedestal-top flux surface, $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi_{\mathrm{top}}}$ denotes a flux-surface average on that surface using the normalized measure $dS/|\nabla\psi|$, $p_e$ is the electron kinetic pressure in pascals, $|B_p|$ is the magnitude of the poloidal magnetic field in tesla, and $\mu_0$ is the magnetic permeability of free space in henries per meter. The denominator uses the square of the averaged field magnitude, not the flux-surface average of $B_p^2$.

The pressure term is the pedestal-top electron kinetic pressure represented by [electron_pressure_at_pedestal_top](name:electron_pressure_at_pedestal_top), with averaging over the same pedestal-top flux surface. Ion pressure and total thermal pressure contributions are excluded. The flux-surface-averaged denominator distinguishes this quantity from [poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top_low_field_side](name:poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top_low_field_side) and [poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top_high_field_side](name:poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top_high_field_side), which use local poloidal-field values at specified poloidal locations, and from [poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top](name:poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top_high_field_side), which does not specify flux-surface averaging of the poloidal field.

worked.name: radial_width_time_derivative_of_neoclassical_tearing_mode
worked.description_before: Instantaneous growth or shrinkage rate of a single neoclassical tearing mode's full magnetic-island width along the major-radius direction.
worked.description_after: Radial width change rate of an individual neoclassical tearing mode expresses growth or shrinkage of its full magnetic-island span along major radius.
worked.documentation_before:
Width of neoclassical tearing mode

The defining time derivative follows the same individual mode:

$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial t}$$

where $\dot{w}$ is the full-width change rate, $w$ is the [full radial island width](name:radial_width_of_neoclassical_tearing_mode), and $t$ is time.

The rate applies to one mode and is not summed over modes. It differentiates the full width rather than the half-width and is distinct from motion of the island center. Negative values denote island shrinkage.

Sign convention: Positive when the full island width increases with time.
worked.documentation_after:
Width of neoclassical tearing mode. The defining expression is

$$
\frac{\partial w}{\partial t}
$$

where $w$ is the [radial full width of the individual mode](name:radial_width_of_neoclassical_tearing_mode), $t$ is time, and the mode identity is held fixed. The major-radius direction is the direction of increasing $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical position.

The differentiated quantity is the full island width, not its half-width, and the rate applies to one mode rather than a sum over modes. It describes island-size evolution, not translation of the island center or rotation of the island pattern. This width-evolution rate enters the generalized Rutherford equation.

Sign convention: Positive when the full major-radius island width increases with time; negative when it decreases.

The time derivative is the rate of change of a quantity with time at a fixed point or label.

worked.name: ratio_of_electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_electron_temperature
worked.description_before: Ratio of electron temperature at the magnetic axis to its volume average inside the last closed magnetic flux surface, expressing central electron-temperature peaking.
worked.description_after: Ratio of magnetic-axis electron temperature to its volume average within the last closed magnetic flux surface, expressing central electron-temperature peaking.
worked.documentation_before:
Ratio of electron temperature at the magnetic axis to its volume average inside the last closed magnetic flux surface. It expresses central electron-temperature peaking relative to the enclosed plasma's mean thermal state.

It is defined by

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $P_{T_e}$ is the electron-temperature peaking ratio, $T_{e,\mathrm{axis}}$ is the [electron temperature at the magnetic axis](name:electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis), and $\langle T_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron temperature](name:volume_averaged_electron_temperature). The volume average is $\langle T_e\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V T_e\,dV$, where $T_e$ is the local electron kinetic temperature, $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface, and $dV$ is a physical volume element.

The denominator is weighted by physical volume, not by electron density, and is not a flux-surface average. The numerator is evaluated at the magnetic axis rather than at an independently located temperature maximum. The ratio requires a positive denominator and is not an absolute temperature; unity means that the axis temperature equals the volume average, while values greater than unity indicate central peaking relative to that average.

The [corresponding ion-temperature ratio](name:ratio_of_ion_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_ion_temperature) applies the same axis-to-volume-average comparison to ion temperature.

$$a/b$$
worked.documentation_after:

It is defined by

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $F_{T_e}$ is the electron-temperature peaking ratio, $T_e$ is the local electron kinetic temperature, $T_{e,\mathrm{axis}}$ is its [value at the magnetic axis](name:electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis), and $\langle T_e\rangle_V$ is its [volume average](name:volume_averaged_electron_temperature). The averaging volume $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface.

The denominator must be positive. The numerator is the magnetic-axis value, not a maximum selected elsewhere in the plasma. The ratio is not an absolute temperature: values above unity indicate an axis temperature exceeding the volume mean, while a spatially uniform temperature gives unity.

The [ion-temperature counterpart](name:ratio_of_ion_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_ion_temperature) applies the same axis-to-volume-average comparison to ions rather than electrons.

$$a/b$$

The ratio is one quantity divided by another.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: ratio_of_hydrogen_density_to_electron_density
worked.description_before: Ratio of hydrogen-ion number density to free-electron number density, expressing the abundance of ionized protium relative to electrons in the plasma.
worked.description_after: Ratio of hydrogen (protium) ion number density to free-electron number density, expressing the abundance of ionized protium relative to plasma electrons.
worked.documentation_before:
Ratio of hydrogen-ion number density to free-electron number density at the same plasma location and time. It expresses particle abundance rather than mass-density or charge-density composition.

The local ratio is defined by

$$
R_{\mathrm{H}/e} = \frac{n_{\mathrm{H}}}{n_e}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{H}/e}$ is the hydrogen-to-electron abundance ratio, $n_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the local [hydrogen-ion number density](name:hydrogen_density), and $n_e$ is the local [free-electron number density](name:electron_density).

The hydrogen population is protium summed over all ionic charge states, consisting only of H+; neutral hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium are excluded. The electron denominator has no imposed thermal or fast-population selection. The ratio is defined where $n_e$ is nonzero and is not the protium fraction of the total hydrogenic population.

No spatial averaging or peak-density time selection is imposed on the underlying ratio. The [volume-averaged hydrogen-to-electron density ratio](name:volume_averaged_ratio_of_hydrogen_density_to_electron_density) averages this local ratio over volume and evaluates it when electron density peaks. That average is distinct from dividing separately volume-averaged hydrogen and electron densities.

The [lithium-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_lithium_density_to_electron_density) is the corresponding species-abundance quantity with lithium ions in the numerator.
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of hydrogen (protium) ion number density to free-electron number density. It compares particle populations rather than electric charge or mass.

The underlying local abundance ratio is

$$
R_{\mathrm{H}/e} = \frac{n_{\mathrm{H}}}{n_e}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{H}/e}$ is the protium-to-electron abundance ratio, $n_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the [hydrogen-ion number density](name:hydrogen_density), and $n_e$ is the [free-electron number density](name:electron_density), with both densities evaluated at the same position and time.

The numerator includes all positive charge states of protium, consisting only of singly charged protium ions. Neutral protium, deuterium, and tritium are excluded from the numerator. The denominator must be nonzero. This ratio is not the protium fraction among hydrogenic ions, because its reference population is free electrons rather than hydrogenic ions.

The [volume-averaged member](name:volume_averaged_ratio_of_hydrogen_density_to_electron_density) averages this local ratio over the plasma volume at the time of peak electron density. Averaging the local ratio is not generally equivalent to dividing separately volume-averaged densities; that averaging operation and time selection belong to the child quantity, not the underlying ratio.

The [lithium-to-electron abundance ratio](name:ratio_of_lithium_density_to_electron_density) is the analogous species ratio with lithium-ion density replacing protium-ion density.

The ratio is one quantity divided by another.

worked.name: ratio_of_ion_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_ion_temperature
worked.description_before: Ratio of ion temperature at the magnetic axis to its volume average inside the last closed magnetic flux surface, expressing central ion-temperature peaking.
worked.description_after: Ratio of magnetic-axis ion temperature to its volume average within the last closed magnetic flux surface, expressing central ion-temperature peaking.
worked.documentation_before:
Ratio of ion temperature at the magnetic axis to its volume average inside the last closed magnetic flux surface. It expresses central ion-temperature peaking relative to the enclosed plasma's mean thermal state.

It is defined by

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $P_i$ is the ion-temperature peaking factor, $T_{i,0}$ is the magnetic-axis ion temperature, $T_i$ is the local ion temperature, and $\langle T_i\rangle_V$ is its average over the enclosed plasma volume $V$.

The denominator is the [volume-averaged ion temperature](name:volume_averaged_ion_temperature): the integral of ion temperature over the enclosed plasma volume divided by that volume, without density weighting of the spatial average. Both temperatures must refer to the same ion population and describe random translational kinetic motion, excluding directed flow and internal excitation. The numerator is the magnetic-axis value, not a maximum selected at an arbitrary location.

The ratio requires a positive denominator and is not an absolute temperature. A value above unity means that the magnetic-axis temperature exceeds the volume average. The [electron-temperature peaking ratio](name:ratio_of_electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_electron_temperature) applies the same axis-to-volume-average comparison to electrons.

$$a/b$$
worked.documentation_after:

Here $T_i$ denotes the local ion kinetic temperature and $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface.

Both operands refer to the same specified ion species. Its local temperature is the density-weighted mean over all charge states and describes the isotropic part of random translational motion, excluding directed bulk-flow energy.
