worked.name: ratio_of_iron_density_to_electron_density
worked.description_before: Dimensionless abundance ratio of charge-state-summed iron-ion number density to local free-electron number density.
worked.description_after: Ratio of charge-state-summed iron-ion number density to free-electron number density, expressing the local abundance of ionized iron relative to plasma electrons.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the local iron-to-electron abundance ratio in a plasma, comparing the population of iron ions with unbound free electrons.

$$
R_{\mathrm{Fe}/e} = \frac{n_{\mathrm{Fe}}}{n_e}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{Fe}/e}$ is the iron-to-electron abundance ratio, $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the total [iron-ion number density](name:iron_density), and $n_e$ is the local [free-electron number density](name:electron_density).

The numerator is summed over all positive iron ionization states, while the denominator counts free electrons and excludes electrons bound in atoms, molecules, or ions. This is a local ratio with no volume averaging, maximum operation, or specified spatial locus.

The ratio is the iron-specific counterpart of the general [ion-density-to-electron-density ratio](name:ratio_of_ion_density_to_electron_density); its numerator is the charge-state-summed iron density and its denominator is the electron-density parent quantity.
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of iron-ion number density to free-electron number density at the same plasma location and time. It compares particle populations rather than electric charge or mass.

The local iron abundance is defined by

$$
R_{\mathrm{Fe}/e} = \frac{n_{\mathrm{Fe}}}{n_e} = \frac{\sum_{z=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}}{n_e}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{Fe}/e}$ is the iron-to-electron abundance ratio, $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the iron-ion number density summed over all positive charge states, $n_e$ is the [free-electron number density](name:electron_density), $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}$ is the number density of iron ions with charge number $z$, and $z$ indexes the positive iron charge states from 1 through 26.

Each iron ion contributes once to the numerator, regardless of charge state; neutral iron is excluded. Both densities are local quantities, with no spatial averaging implied. The ratio is defined only when the electron density is nonzero.

Like the [lithium-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_lithium_density_to_electron_density), this quantity expresses unweighted ion-particle abundance relative to free electrons. It is neither a charge-weighted contribution to electron density nor an effective-charge measure.

The ratio is one quantity divided by another.

worked.name: ratio_of_line_averaged_electron_density_to_greenwald_density
worked.description_before: Dimensionless Greenwald fraction comparing the electron number density averaged along a plasma chord with the empirical density limit set by plasma current and effective minor radius.
worked.description_after: Ratio of line-averaged free-electron number density to the empirical Greenwald density limit, expressing proximity to a plasma-current-dependent density reference.
worked.documentation_before:
The Greenwald fraction measures the proximity of a confined plasma's line-averaged electron density to its empirical Greenwald density limit.

It is defined by:

$$
f_G = \frac{\bar{n}_e}{n_G}
$$

where $f_G$ is the Greenwald fraction, $\bar{n}_e$ is the [line-averaged electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density), and $n_G$ is the [Greenwald density](name:greenwald_density) determined from the plasma-current magnitude and effective minor radius.

The numerator represents the electron population averaged along a plasma chord; the denominator is the empirical density reference for the confined plasma. This quantity is a global normalized ratio, not a local electron density, a density limit itself, or an average over charge states or spatial regions.

The fraction is the direct normalization of line-averaged electron density by Greenwald density: values near unity indicate proximity to the empirical reference limit, while values above or below unity indicate a line-averaged density respectively above or below that reference.
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of line-averaged free-electron number density to the empirical Greenwald density reference. It expresses the line-averaged density relative to this plasma-current-dependent reference.

The ratio is defined as

$$
f_{\mathrm{G}} = \frac{\bar{n}_e}{n_{\mathrm{G}}}
$$

where $f_{\mathrm{G}}$ is this ratio, $\bar{n}_e$ is the [line-averaged electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density), and $n_{\mathrm{G}}$ is the [Greenwald density](name:greenwald_density).

The numerator is formed by the [line average](concept:line_averaged) along a stated chord; it is not a local or [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density). The denominator is the Greenwald density reference, not another chord-averaged density. This is the ratio of the line-averaged density to the reference, not the line average of a local density-to-reference ratio.

This is the explicitly line-averaged form of the [electron-density-to-Greenwald-density ratio](name:ratio_of_electron_density_to_greenwald_density). A value of one means the line-averaged density equals the Greenwald reference; values above one are possible because the empirical reference is not a strict mathematical bound.

$$a/b$$

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

The ratio is one quantity divided by another.

worked.name: ratio_of_line_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_line_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density
worked.description_before: Dimensionless line-averaged protium fraction among hydrogenic ions, obtained by dividing the protium density by the total hydrogenic density along the same chord.
worked.description_after: Ratio of line-averaged protium-ion density to line-averaged total hydrogenic-ion density, giving the protium fraction among hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium ions.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the fraction of hydrogenic ion content carried by protium along a specified chord through the plasma. It is a ratio of consistently line-averaged densities, rather than a local fraction or a volume-averaged fraction.

$$
f_{\rm H}^{\rm line} = \frac{\bar{n}_{\rm H}^{\rm line}}{\bar{n}_{\rm H}^{\rm line}+\bar{n}_{\rm D}^{\rm line}+\bar{n}_{\rm T}^{\rm line}}
$$

where $f_{\rm H}^{\rm line}$ is the line-averaged protium fraction, $\bar{n}_{\rm H}^{\rm line}$ is the line-averaged protium-ion number density, $\bar{n}_{\rm D}^{\rm line}$ is the corresponding deuterium-ion number density, and $\bar{n}_{\rm T}^{\rm line}$ is the corresponding tritium-ion number density. The symbols H, D, and T denote protium, deuterium, and tritium, respectively.

The quantity applies to the hydrogenic ion population along one common chord and aggregates the isotope densities through the total hydrogenic denominator. Neutral atomic hydrogen and non-hydrogenic species are excluded. The numerator is the [line-averaged hydrogen density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density), while the denominator is the [total hydrogenic density](name:total_hydrogenic_density) under the same line-averaging convention.

This ratio differs from the [ratio of volume-averaged hydrogen density to volume-averaged total hydrogenic density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density), because the latter uses volume-averaged rather than chord-averaged isotope densities.
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of line-averaged hydrogen (protium) ion number density to line-averaged total hydrogenic-ion number density. It expresses the protium particle fraction among hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium ions along a specified plasma chord.

The isotope fraction is defined by

$$
f_{\mathrm{H}} = \frac{\bar{n}_{\mathrm{H}}}{\bar{n}_{\mathrm{hyd}}} = \frac{\bar{n}_{\mathrm{H}}}{\bar{n}_{\mathrm{H}}+\bar{n}_{\mathrm{D}}+\bar{n}_{\mathrm{T}}}
$$

where $f_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the protium fraction, $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the [line-averaged hydrogen density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density), $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{D}}$ and $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{T}}$ are the line-averaged deuterium-ion and tritium-ion number densities, respectively, and $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{hyd}}$ is their total hydrogenic-ion number density averaged along the same chord.

All averages refer to the same chord and time. Each isotope density is summed over all positive ionic charge states; for these isotopes, the sole positive atomic charge state is singly charged. Neutral particles, electrons, and nonhydrogenic species are excluded. The denominator counts ions without mass or charge weighting.

The aggregation is the ratio of line-averaged densities, not the line average of the local isotope fraction. The fraction is defined only for a nonzero denominator and lies between zero and one for nonnegative isotope densities.

This quantity is the chord-based counterpart of the [volume-averaged hydrogen isotope fraction](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density), which instead forms the ratio from densities averaged over a common plasma volume.

$$a/b$$

The line average is the integral of a quantity along a stated chord divided by the chord length.

The ratio is one quantity divided by another.

worked.name: ratio_of_lithium_density_to_electron_density
worked.description_before: Ratio of charge-state-summed lithium-ion number density to free-electron number density, expressing the abundance of ionized lithium relative to electrons.
worked.description_after: Ratio of an ion species’ charge-state-summed number density to free-electron number density, expressing particle abundance rather than charge contribution.
worked.documentation_before:
Ratio of lithium-ion number density to free-electron number density, expressing lithium abundance relative to electrons in the plasma. It compares particle populations rather than electric charge or mass.

The local abundance ratio is defined by

$$
R_{\mathrm{Li}/e} = \frac{n_{\mathrm{Li}}}{n_e}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{Li}/e}$ is the lithium-to-electron abundance ratio, $n_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium-ion number density summed over all positive lithium charge states, and $n_e$ is the [free-electron number density](name:electron_density).

Both densities refer to the same location and instant, and the ratio is defined only where the electron density is nonzero. The lithium population includes singly, doubly, and triply ionized lithium and excludes neutral lithium. Each lithium ion contributes equally to the numerator regardless of charge state; this is not a charge-weighted contribution to electron density or an effective-charge measure.

Volume averaging this local ratio gives the [volume-averaged lithium-to-electron density ratio](name:volume_averaged_ratio_of_lithium_density_to_electron_density), whose stated evaluation time is the electron-density peak. Averaging the local ratio is distinct from dividing two separately volume-averaged densities. The [hydrogen-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_hydrogen_density_to_electron_density) uses the same particle-abundance definition with hydrogen replacing lithium.
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of a specified ion species’ number density to free-electron number density. It compares ion and electron particle populations without weighting ions by their electric charge.

The underlying local abundance ratio is

$$
R_{i/e} = \frac{n_i}{n_e}
$$

where $R_{i/e}$ is the ion-species abundance relative to free electrons, $n_i$ is the specified species’ ion number density summed over all positive charge states, and $n_e$ is the [free-electron number density](name:electron_density).

The two densities refer to the same plasma location and time, and the local ratio is defined only where the electron density is nonzero. Neutral atoms are excluded from the ion population, and each ion counts once regardless of charge state. This abundance is neither a charge-weighted contribution to electron density nor an effective-charge measure.

Species-specific members include the [iron-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_iron_density_to_electron_density). The [volume-averaged lithium-to-electron density ratio](name:volume_averaged_ratio_of_lithium_density_to_electron_density) averages the corresponding local lithium ratio over the plasma volume at the time of peak electron density. That aggregation is an average of local ratios, not a ratio of separately volume-averaged densities; neither its species selection nor its averaging and timing restrictions apply to the general quantity.

The ratio is one quantity divided by another.

worked.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_argon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
worked.description_before: Elemental abundance ratio of argon nuclei to free electrons inside the last closed flux surface, formed from the corresponding volume-averaged densities. The argon population is summed over all argon ion charge states and excludes neutral argon.
worked.description_after: Ratio of volume-averaged argon-ion number density to volume-averaged free-electron number density, expressing charge-state-summed argon abundance in the confined plasma.
worked.documentation_before:
Elemental abundance ratio of argon nuclei to free electrons inside the last closed flux surface is the confined-plasma composition fraction obtained by normalizing the volume-averaged argon density to the volume-averaged electron density. The argon population is the species-level ion population summed over all argon ion charge states.

The ratio is defined as the quotient of the corresponding volume-averaged densities:

$$
C_{\mathrm{Ar}} = \frac{\langle n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\rangle_V}{\langle n_e\rangle_V}
$$

where $C_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is this argon-to-electron abundance ratio, $\langle n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged argon-ion number density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density), $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron number density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), and $V$ denotes the confined plasma volume bounded by the last closed flux surface.

The scope is the confined plasma population inside the last closed flux surface, with the same volume-averaging operation applied to the argon and electron densities before forming the quotient. It excludes neutral argon, is not charge-state-resolved, and is a ratio of volume averages rather than the volume average of a local argon-to-electron density ratio.

This quantity is related to [argon_density](name:argon_density) as its volume-averaged, electron-normalized elemental abundance; [argon_density](name:argon_density) denotes the argon density before normalization to the electron population.
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of volume-averaged argon-ion number density to volume-averaged free-electron number density. It compares particle populations rather than electric charge or mass.

The argon abundance ratio is defined by

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $a_{\mathrm{Ar},V}$ is this argon abundance ratio, $\langle n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged argon density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density), $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged free-electron number density, and $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface. The underlying quantities $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ and $n_e$ are the local [argon-ion number density](name:argon_density) and free-electron number density, respectively.

Both averages use the same confined plasma volume and evaluation time; the supplied composition context specifies the time of peak electron density. The argon population is summed over all positive charge states, from singly ionized to fully stripped argon; neutral argon is excluded.

The aggregation is the ratio of two volume averages, not the volume average of the local argon-to-electron density ratio. It is defined only when the volume-averaged electron density is nonzero. It is an unweighted argon-particle abundance, not a charge-weighted contribution to electron density or an effective-charge measure.

It is the argon member of the same composition-ratio family as the [corresponding neon abundance ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_neon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), with the numerator population changed from neon ions to argon ions.

$$a/b$$

The ratio is one quantity divided by another.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_beryllium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
worked.description_before: Dimensionless beryllium abundance formed by dividing the volume-averaged beryllium density by the volume-averaged electron density.
worked.description_after: Ratio of volume-averaged beryllium-ion number density to volume-averaged free-electron number density, expressing confined-plasma beryllium abundance summed over positive charge states.
worked.documentation_before:
Dimensionless beryllium abundance formed by dividing the volume-averaged beryllium density by the volume-averaged electron density. It represents the abundance of ionized beryllium relative to free electrons in the confined plasma volume.

The abundance is defined by the ratio of the two volume averages:

$$
a_{\mathrm{Be}} =
\frac{\langle n_{\mathrm{Be}} \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
=
\frac{\left\langle \sum_{q=1}^{4} n_{\mathrm{Be}^{q+}} \right\rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $a_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the beryllium abundance ratio, $\langle \cdot \rangle_V$ denotes averaging over the confined plasma volume, $n_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the charge-state-summed beryllium ion number density, $n_{\mathrm{Be}^{q+}}$ is the number density of beryllium ions in charge state $q$, and $n_e$ is the [electron density](name:electron_density).

The numerator is the [volume-averaged beryllium density](name:volume_averaged_beryllium_density), summed over all ionized beryllium charge states and excluding neutral beryllium atoms. The denominator is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density) over the same confined plasma volume.

This quantity is a ratio of two global volume averages, not a pointwise impurity fraction and not the volume average of $n_{\mathrm{Be}}/n_e$. It is not charge-weighted; a charge-weighted beryllium contribution to quasineutrality would use terms proportional to $q n_{\mathrm{Be}^{q+}}$ rather than the unweighted ion sum. The local pre-averaged counterpart of the numerator is [beryllium density](name:beryllium_density).
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of volume-averaged beryllium-ion number density to volume-averaged free-electron number density. It compares particle populations rather than electric charge or mass.

The beryllium abundance ratio is

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $R_{\mathrm{Be}/e,V}$ denotes this abundance ratio, $\langle n_{\mathrm{Be}}\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged beryllium density](name:volume_averaged_beryllium_density), $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged free-electron number density, and $V$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface. The local densities $n_{\mathrm{Be}}$ and $n_e$ denote beryllium-ion and free-electron number density, respectively.

Both averages use the same plasma volume and are evaluated at the time of peak electron density. The [local beryllium density](name:beryllium_density) includes all positive charge states: $n_{\mathrm{Be}}=\sum_{z=1}^{4}n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}$, where $z$ is the positive charge number and $n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}$ is the number density of beryllium ions in that charge state. Neutral beryllium is excluded.

The aggregation is the ratio of two volume averages, not the volume average of the local ratio $n_{\mathrm{Be}}/n_e$. The quantity is defined only when the volume-averaged electron density is nonzero.

Like the [corresponding tungsten abundance ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_tungsten_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), this quantity counts each included ion once; it is not a charge-weighted contribution to electron density or an effective-charge measure.

$$a/b$$

The ratio is one quantity divided by another.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
worked.description_before: Dimensionless volume-averaged deuterium abundance ratio is the quotient of the volume-averaged deuterium ion number density and the volume-averaged electron number density over the same plasma volume. The deuterium numerator is charge-state-summed over positive atomic ion charge states and excludes neutral or molecular deuterium.
worked.description_after: Ratio of volume-averaged deuterium-ion number density to volume-averaged free-electron number density in the confined plasma, evaluated at the time of peak electron density.
worked.documentation_before:
Dimensionless volume-averaged deuterium abundance ratio is the electron-density-normalized abundance of deuterium ions in a specified plasma volume. It is the quotient of the [volume-averaged deuterium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density) and the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density) evaluated over that same volume.

The ratio is defined by the quotient of volume averages:

$$
f_{D,V} = \frac{\langle n_D \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $f_{D,V}$ is this abundance ratio, $n_D$ is the [deuterium density](name:deuterium_density), $n_e$ is the electron density, $\langle n_D \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged deuterium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density), $\langle n_e \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), and the subscript $V$ denotes averaging over the common plasma volume.

The numerator is the volume average of deuterium ion number density summed over all positive atomic ion charge states. It excludes neutral deuterium atoms, molecular deuterium, and deuterium bound in non-ion populations. The aggregation convention is a quotient of two volume-averaged densities, not the volume average of the pointwise ratio $n_D/n_e$.

For non-negative number densities and positive $\langle n_e \rangle_V$, $f_{D,V}$ is non-negative. It is not the fraction of deuterium among all fuel nuclei and does not represent the absolute deuterium particle inventory. It differs from the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium abundance ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), which uses the combined deuterium-tritium numerator, while this quantity uses deuterium alone.
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of volume-averaged deuterium-ion number density to volume-averaged free-electron number density. It expresses confined-plasma deuterium abundance relative to free electrons at the time of peak electron density.

The deuterium abundance ratio is

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $a_{\mathrm D,V}$ denotes this ratio, $\langle n_{\mathrm D}\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged deuterium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density), $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged free-electron number density, and $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface. The local quantities $n_{\mathrm D}$ and $n_e$ denote the [deuterium-ion number density](name:deuterium_density) and free-electron number density, respectively.

Both averages use the same confined plasma volume and evaluation time. The deuterium numerator is summed over all positive atomic charge states; for deuterium, this consists solely of singly ionized deuterons. Neutral deuterium and molecular species are excluded. The aggregation is the ratio of two volume averages, not the volume average of the local density ratio, and the denominator must be nonzero.

Normalizing the volume-averaged deuterium density by the electron density gives abundance relative to free electrons, not the deuterium fraction among hydrogen-isotope ions or an effective-charge measure. Unlike the [combined deuterium–tritium abundance ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), its numerator includes deuterium ions only, not tritium ions.

$$a/b$$

The ratio is one quantity divided by another.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
worked.description_before: Volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density divided by volume-averaged electron density for the combined deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species, treating deuterium and tritium as one effective species.
worked.description_after: Ratio of volume-averaged effective deuterium–tritium fuel-ion number density, summed over ionic charge states, to volume-averaged free-electron number density.
worked.documentation_before:
Volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density divided by volume-averaged electron density for the combined deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species, treating deuterium and tritium as one effective species, is the electron-density-normalized abundance of that fuel species. It compares the fuel-ion population with the electron population after each density is averaged over the same plasma volume.

The ratio is defined by:

$$
\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{DT}/e} = \frac{\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}} \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{DT}/e}$ is this ratio, $\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}} \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density), $\langle n_e \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the local number density of the combined deuterium-tritium effective species, $n_e$ is the local electron number density, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_V$ denotes averaging over the common plasma volume $V$.

The scope is the plasma volume common to numerator and denominator; the value is a ratio of two volume averages, not the volume average of a pointwise density ratio. The numerator is a species-level extensive density for the effective deuterium-tritium fuel species and is summed over all charge states before averaging. It includes only that fuel species and excludes helium ash, impurity ions, and separate isotope-composition ratios such as the [tritium-to-deuterium density ratio](name:ratio_of_tritium_density_to_deuterium_density).

Equivalently, this quantity is the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density) normalized by the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density); it is a normalized ratio, not a derivative of either density. When the combined deuterium-tritium density is resolved into deuterium and tritium contributions over the same volume and denominator, it equals the sum of the [volume-averaged deuterium-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density) and the [volume-averaged tritium-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of volume-averaged effective deuterium-tritium fuel-ion number density to volume-averaged free-electron number density. It expresses the abundance of the combined effective fuel-ion population relative to free electrons, comparing particle populations rather than electric charge or mass.

For the common plasma volume $V$, the ratio is

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{DT}/e}$ is this abundance ratio, $\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}}\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density), $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the local number density of the effective deuterium-tritium fuel-ion species, and $n_e$ is the local free-electron number density.

Both averages apply to the same confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface. The numerator population is summed over all ionic charge states, and the ratio is defined only when the volume-averaged free-electron density is nonzero. The aggregation is the ratio of the two volume averages, not the volume average of the local density ratio.

This is an unweighted particle-abundance ratio, not a charge-weighted contribution to electron density, a mass fraction, or a fusion reaction rate. It compares the combined effective fuel-ion population with free electrons, rather than comparing deuterium and tritium with each other.

When the effective deuterium-tritium population is resolved into deuterium and tritium contributions over the same volume and normalized by the same electron average, this ratio equals the sum of the [volume-averaged deuterium-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density) and the [volume-averaged tritium-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

$$a/b$$

The ratio is one quantity divided by another.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.description_before: Dimensionless composition ratio comparing the charge-state-summed helium-3 ion density averaged over the confined plasma volume with the electron density averaged over the same volume. It is the helium-3 average divided by the electron average.
worked.description_after: Ratio of volume-averaged helium-3 ion density to volume-averaged free-electron density in the confined plasma, counting helium-3 ions across all positive charge states.
worked.documentation_before:
Dimensionless composition ratio comparing the charge-state-summed helium-3 ion density averaged over the confined plasma volume with the electron density averaged over the same volume. It is the helium-3 average divided by the electron average and represents the global helium-3 ion composition relative to electrons.

The ratio is defined by applying the volume average separately to each density over the same confined plasma volume before division:

$$
r_{{}^3\mathrm{He}/e} =
\frac{\frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV}{\frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_e(\mathbf{x})\,dV}
$$

where $r_{{}^3\mathrm{He}/e}$ is this composition ratio, $n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local helium-3 ion number density summed over all charged ionization states, $n_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local electron number density, $\mathbf{x}$ denotes position, $dV$ is the volume element, and $V_c$ is the confined plasma volume, with the same symbol denoting its volume measure in the normalization factors.

The scope is a species-level, volume-averaged, confined-plasma composition ratio. The helium-3 population includes charged helium-3 ions summed over charge states and excludes neutral helium-3 atoms; the electron population is the corresponding electron population in the same confined volume. No particular time within an evolution is part of the quantity definition.

This quantity is not the confined-volume average of the local ratio $n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}/n_e$; it equals that average only for special spatial distributions. Its numerator is the [volume-averaged helium-3 density](name:volume_averaged_helium_3_density), and its denominator is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density). The [ratio of volume-averaged helium-4 density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density) is the analogous isotope composition ratio for helium-4.
worked.documentation_after:

where $a_{3,V}$ denotes this abundance ratio, $\langle n_3\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged helium-3 density](name:volume_averaged_helium_3_density), $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), and $V$ is the common plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface. The brackets denote volume averaging; $n_3$ and $n_e$ denote the corresponding local helium-3 ion and free-electron number densities.

Both averages are evaluated at the time of peak electron density. The helium-3 population is summed over all positive charge states, including singly and doubly ionized helium-3; neutral helium-3 and other helium isotopes are excluded. Neither density is restricted to thermal particles.

The aggregation is the ratio of two volume averages, not the volume average of the local ratio $n_3/n_e$. The quantity is defined only when the volume-averaged electron density is nonzero. The [corresponding tritium abundance ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density) uses the same averaging-before-division convention for the tritium-ion population.

$$a/b$$

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.description_after: Ratio of volume-averaged helium-4 ion number density to volume-averaged free-electron number density, expressing confined-plasma helium-4 abundance summed over positive charge states.
worked.documentation_before:
Helium-4 abundance ratio formed from mean densities inside the last closed flux surface is the quotient of the volume-averaged helium-4 ion number density and the volume-averaged electron number density. It is a global isotope-abundance measure for ionized helium-4 relative to electrons in the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface.

The ratio is defined from independent volume averages over the same enclosed plasma volume:

$$
f_{{}^4\mathrm{He},e}^{V} = \frac{\langle n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}\rangle_V}{\langle n_e\rangle_V}, \qquad \langle n_s\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{LCFS}}\int_{V_\mathrm{LCFS}} n_s(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $f_{{}^4\mathrm{He},e}^{V}$ is this helium-4 abundance ratio, the superscript $V$ denotes formation from volume averages, $\langle n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged helium-4 density](name:volume_averaged_helium_4_density), $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_s(\mathbf{x})$ is the local number density of species $s$ at position $\mathbf{x}$, $V_\mathrm{LCFS}$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is an element of that volume. For $s={}^4\mathrm{He}$, $n_s$ is the local helium-4 ion number density summed over all ion charge states; for $s=e$, $n_s$ is the local electron number density.

The semantic scope is species-level helium-4 ion density inside the last closed flux surface. The helium-4 numerator is summed over all ion charge states before averaging, while neutral helium-4 atoms and helium isotopes other than helium-4 are excluded. Because the numerator and denominator are averaged separately, this quantity is not the volume average of the local ratio $n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}/n_e$.

For fully stripped helium-4 ions in a quasi-neutral plasma, $2 f_{{}^4\mathrm{He},e}^{V}$ represents the helium-4 ion contribution to the electron charge balance, apart from contributions of other ions and departures from full stripping. The isotope analog is [ratio of volume-averaged helium-3 density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_3_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), and the analogous elemental abundance quantity is [ratio of volume-averaged neon density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_neon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density). worked.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density
worked.description_before: Dimensionless hydrogen-isotope fraction equal to the volume-averaged protium-ion density divided by the volume-averaged density of all hydrogenic ions.
worked.description_after: Ratio of volume-averaged protium-ion density to volume-averaged total hydrogenic-ion density, giving the protium fraction among hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium ions.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the fraction of the hydrogenic ion population attributable to protium, evaluated from volume-averaged densities over the same plasma volume. The numerator is the [volume-averaged hydrogen density](name:volume_averaged_hydrogen_density), while the denominator includes the corresponding hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium ion populations.

$$
f_H = \frac{\overline{n}_H}{\overline{n}_H + \overline{n}_D + \overline{n}_T}
$$

Here $f_H$ is the hydrogen-isotope fraction; $\overline{n}_H$, $\overline{n}_D$, and $\overline{n}_T$ are the volume-averaged densities of protium, deuterium, and tritium ions, respectively. The quantity is a ratio of separately volume-averaged densities, not a local isotope fraction or a fraction restricted to a single charge state.
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of volume-averaged hydrogen (protium) ion number density to volume-averaged total hydrogenic-ion number density. It expresses the protium particle fraction among hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium ions in the confined plasma.

The protium fraction is

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $f_{\mathrm{H},V}$ is this protium fraction; $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface; $n_{\mathrm{H}}$, $n_{\mathrm{D}}$, and $n_{\mathrm{T}}$ are the local protium-, deuterium-, and tritium-ion number densities; and $n_{\mathrm{hyd}}$ is their sum, the [total hydrogenic density](name:total_hydrogenic_density). Angle brackets with subscript $V$ denote volume averages. The numerator is the [volume-averaged hydrogen density](name:volume_averaged_hydrogen_density).

Both averages refer to the same confined plasma volume and time. Each isotope density is summed over all positive ionic charge states; neutral particles are excluded. The denominator includes only hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium ions, not electrons or non-hydrogenic ions. This is a particle-number fraction, not a mass fraction. It lies between zero and one when the denominator is positive and is undefined when the denominator vanishes.

The aggregation is a ratio of volume averages, not the volume average of the local fraction $n_{\mathrm{H}}/n_{\mathrm{hyd}}$. Because both averages use the same volume, it also equals the fraction of the confined hydrogenic-ion inventory carried by protium. Unlike the [line-averaged protium fraction](name:ratio_of_line_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_line_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density), it describes composition over the confined plasma volume rather than along a specified chord.

worked.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_neon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
worked.description_before: Dimensionless elemental abundance ratio of charge-state-summed neon nuclei to free electrons, formed from their respective mean number densities inside the last closed flux surface.
worked.description_after: Ratio of volume-averaged neon-ion number density, summed over positive charge states, to volume-averaged free-electron number density in the confined plasma.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the abundance of neon nuclei relative to free electrons, with both species represented by number densities averaged over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface. Neon is summed over all charge states, so the quantity is an elemental composition ratio rather than a charge-state-specific abundance or a local density ratio.

The ratio of volume-averaged densities is defined by

$$
\frac{\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Ne}}}{\overline{n}_e} = \frac{\displaystyle \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV}{\displaystyle \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_e(\mathbf{x})\,dV}
$$

where $\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the [volume-averaged neon density](name:volume_averaged_neon_density), $\overline{n}_e$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local neon nuclear number density summed over charge states, $n_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local free-electron number density, $V_p$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $dV$ is the volume element.

Both operands use the same plasma volume and the same volume-averaging convention. This quantity is the ratio of the two global means, not the volume average of the local ratio $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{x})/n_e(\mathbf{x})$; its denominator is specifically the parent [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), while its numerator is the corresponding [volume-averaged neon density](name:volume_averaged_neon_density).
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of volume-averaged neon-ion number density to volume-averaged free-electron number density. It expresses elemental neon abundance relative to free electrons in the confined plasma.

The neon abundance ratio is

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $a_{\mathrm{Ne},V}$ denotes this abundance ratio, $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ and $n_e$ are the local neon-ion and free-electron number densities, respectively, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_V$ denotes volume averaging over the plasma volume $V$ enclosed by the last closed flux surface.

The numerator is the [volume-averaged neon density](name:volume_averaged_neon_density), summed over all positive neon charge states; neutral neon is excluded. Each neon ion counts once, irrespective of its charge state. Both operands use the same volume and averaging operation, and the ratio is defined only when the electron-density average is nonzero.

This quantity is a ratio of volume averages, not the volume average of the local ratio $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}/n_e$. It is not a charge-weighted neon contribution to electron density or an effective-charge measure. The [corresponding nitrogen abundance ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_nitrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density) uses the same definition with nitrogen replacing neon.

worked.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_oxygen_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
worked.description_before: Volume-averaged oxygen ion density relative to volume-averaged electron density for the plasma, with oxygen summed over ionized charge states and neutral oxygen excluded.
worked.description_after: Ratio of plasma-volume-averaged oxygen-ion number density, summed over positive charge states, to plasma-volume-averaged free-electron number density. It expresses oxygen-ion abundance relative to free electrons in the plasma volume.
worked.documentation_before:
Volume-averaged oxygen ion density relative to volume-averaged electron density is a scalar oxygen impurity fraction for the plasma. It compares the charge-state-summed volume average of ionized oxygen number density with the corresponding volume average of electron number density over the same averaging volume.

The ratio is defined by

$$
f_O = \frac{\left\langle \sum_{q=1}^{8} n_{O^{q+}} \right\rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $f_O$ is this oxygen-to-electron density ratio, $\langle\cdot\rangle_V$ denotes a volume average over the averaging volume $V$, $q$ is the oxygen charge-state index, $n_{O^{q+}}$ is the local number density of oxygen ions in charge state $q+$, and $n_e$ is the local electron number density. The denominator $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density).

The numerator is summed over ionized oxygen charge states $O^{1+}$ through $O^{8+}$ and excludes neutral oxygen. This quantity is a single scalar composition fraction formed from volume-averaged populations; it is distinct from a local [oxygen density](name:oxygen_density), from a [line-averaged oxygen density](name:line_averaged_oxygen_density), and from a neutral-inclusive [volume-averaged oxygen density](name:volume_averaged_oxygen_density) when that quantity includes neutral oxygen.

The essential relationship is normalization: the charge-state-summed volume-averaged oxygen ion density is divided by the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), so the result represents oxygen ion abundance relative to the electron population rather than an absolute density.
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of the plasma-volume-averaged oxygen-ion number density to the plasma-volume-averaged free-electron number density. It compares particle populations, so each oxygen ion counts once regardless of its charge state. It is not a charge-weighted or mass-weighted measure.

The ratio is formed from the two volume averages over the same plasma volume:

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $a_{\mathrm{O}}$ is this oxygen-to-electron abundance ratio, $\langle n_{\mathrm{O}}\rangle_V$ is the volume average of the oxygen-ion number density summed over all positive charge states of oxygen, and $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density). The averaging volume $V$ is the plasma volume, and both averages use the same $V$.

The oxygen population is elemental oxygen in positive ionization states, summed over all charge states. Neutral oxygen is excluded. The [volume-averaged oxygen density](name:volume_averaged_oxygen_density) is the corresponding absolute oxygen density, and this ratio is that density normalized by the volume-averaged electron density. The quantity is the ratio of the two volume averages, not the volume average of the local ratio of oxygen density to electron density. It is distinct from a local [oxygen density](name:oxygen_density) and from any line-averaged density. It is defined only when $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is nonzero.

This is the oxygen member of the family of volume-averaged abundance ratios that includes the [tungsten ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_tungsten_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

worked.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
worked.description_before: Ratio of volume-averaged tritium density to volume-averaged electron density is the volume-averaged tritium number density, summed over all charge states, divided by the volume-averaged electron number density.
worked.description_after: Ratio of plasma-volume-averaged tritium-ion number density to plasma-volume-averaged free-electron number density, comparing the tritium-ion and free-electron particle populations in the same plasma volume.
worked.documentation_before:
Ratio of volume-averaged tritium density to volume-averaged electron density is the volume-averaged tritium number density divided by the volume-averaged electron number density. It expresses the tritium contribution to plasma composition relative to the electron population after both densities have been averaged over the same plasma volume.

The ratio is defined as:

$$
f_{T/e}^{V} = \frac{\langle n_T \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $f_{T/e}^{V}$ is this ratio, $\langle n_T \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged tritium density](name:volume_averaged_tritium_density), $\langle n_e \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_T$ is the local [tritium density](name:tritium_density), $n_e$ is the local [electron density](name:electron_density), and $\langle q\rangle_V$ denotes $V^{-1}\int_V q\,dV$ for scalar field $q$ over the common plasma volume $V$.

The scope is the specified plasma volume and the particle populations contained in that volume. The tritium density is a species-level per-volume amount and is therefore summed over all tritium charge states before volume averaging. The definition contains no selection by the time of peak electron density or by any other operating condition.

This quantity is the ratio of volume averages, not the volume average of the local ratio $n_T/n_e$, and it is not normalized to the total hydrogenic-fuel density. It is the tritium-only counterpart of the [ratio of volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), which uses the combined deuterium-plus-tritium numerator; it also differs from the local ratio of tritium density to electron density.
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of the plasma-volume-averaged tritium-ion number density to the plasma-volume-averaged free-electron number density. It compares particle populations rather than electric charge or mass.

The ratio is formed from the two volume averages over a common plasma volume:

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $a_{\mathrm{T}/e,V}$ denotes this ratio, $\langle n_{\mathrm{T}}\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged tritium density](name:volume_averaged_tritium_density), and $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density). Each average has the form $\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$, with $f$ replaced by the local tritium-ion number density $n_{\mathrm{T}}$ (the local [tritium density](name:tritium_density)) or by the local free-electron number density $n_e$ (the local [electron density](name:electron_density)). $V$ is the plasma volume over which both averages are taken, and it is the same for numerator and denominator.

The tritium population is ionized tritium summed over all charge states; neutral tritium is excluded. The aggregation is the ratio of the two volume averages, not the volume average of the local ratio $n_{\mathrm{T}}/n_e$. The ratio is defined only when $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is nonzero.

This is an unweighted tritium-ion abundance relative to free electrons. It is not the tritium fraction among fuel ions, not a charge-weighted contribution to electron density, and not an effective-charge measure. Its local counterpart is [ratio of tritium density to electron density](name:ratio_of_tritium_density_to_electron_density), which is not volume averaged.

worked.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_tungsten_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
worked.description_before: Dimensionless tungsten abundance ratio equal to the plasma-volume-averaged elemental tungsten density divided by the plasma-volume-averaged electron density.
worked.description_after: Ratio of volume-averaged tungsten-ion number density to volume-averaged free-electron number density, expressing confined-plasma tungsten abundance summed over all positive charge states.
worked.documentation_before:
Dimensionless tungsten abundance ratio equal to the plasma-volume-averaged elemental tungsten density divided by the plasma-volume-averaged electron density. It compares the charge-state-summed tungsten-ion population with the free-electron population in the same plasma volume.

The ratio is defined from the two volume averages over the plasma volume $V$ as

$$
a_{\mathrm{W},V}
=
\frac{\langle n_{\mathrm{W}}\rangle_V}{\langle n_e\rangle_V}
=
\frac{V^{-1}\int_V \sum_{z=1}^{74} n_{\mathrm{W}^{z+}}(\mathbf{x})\, dV}{V^{-1}\int_V n_e(\mathbf{x})\, dV}
$$

where $a_{\mathrm{W},V}$ denotes this tungsten abundance ratio, $V$ denotes the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface over which both averages are formed, $\langle n_{\mathrm{W}}\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged tungsten density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density), $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_{\mathrm{W}^{z+}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local number density of tungsten ions in charge state $z$ at position $\mathbf{x}$, $n_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local free-electron number density, $z=1,\ldots,74$ indexes the positive tungsten ionization states, and $dV$ is the volume element.

The scope is the confined plasma volume: both numerator and denominator use the same volume and the same volume-averaging operation. The tungsten population is elemental tungsten in positive ionization states, summed over charge state; neutral tungsten is excluded. The aggregation is the ratio of the two volume averages, not the volume average of the local ratio $n_{\mathrm{W}}/n_e$, and the quantity is defined only when $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is nonzero.

This ratio is an unweighted tungsten-nucleus abundance relative to free electrons; it is not a charge-weighted tungsten contribution to electron density and is not an effective-charge measure. It is the tungsten member of the same volume-averaged composition-ratio family as the [deuterium-tritium abundance ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density) and the [carbon abundance ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_carbon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), which replace the tungsten numerator with the corresponding species volume average while retaining the same electron-density denominator.
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of volume-averaged tungsten-ion number density to volume-averaged free-electron number density. It compares particle populations rather than electric charge or mass.

The tungsten abundance ratio is defined by

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{W}/e}$ is the tungsten abundance ratio, $n_{\mathrm{W}}$ is the local tungsten-ion number density, $n_e$ is the local free-electron number density, and $V$ is the common averaging volume. The numerator $\langle n_{\mathrm{W}}\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged tungsten density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density), and the denominator $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density).

Both averages apply to the plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface and are evaluated at the time of peak electron density. Tungsten density is summed over all positive charge states, counting each ion once and excluding neutral tungsten. The electron density includes thermal and nonthermal free electrons.

This quantity is a ratio of volume averages, not a volume average of the local density ratio. Because the averaging volume is common to both operands, it also equals the total number of tungsten ions divided by the total number of free electrons within that volume. The electron-density denominator must be nonzero.

The [analogous tritium abundance ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density) replaces the tungsten-ion numerator with the volume-averaged tritium-ion density.

worked.name: rotation_frequency_time_derivative_of_neoclassical_tearing_mode
worked.description_before: Instantaneous angular acceleration of a neoclassical tearing-mode magnetic island, indicating whether its helical rotation is accelerating or decelerating.
worked.description_after: Instantaneous angular acceleration of a neoclassical tearing-mode magnetic island, indicating whether its helical rotation is accelerating or decelerating.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the instantaneous angular acceleration of a single neoclassical tearing-mode magnetic island on its resonant flux surface.

The defining relation is

$$
\alpha_{\mathrm{NTM}}(t) = \frac{d\omega_{\mathrm{NTM}}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $\alpha_{\mathrm{NTM}}$ is the island's angular acceleration, $\omega_{\mathrm{NTM}}$ is its [angular rotation frequency](name:rotation_frequency_of_neoclassical_tearing_mode), $t$ is time, and the subscript $\mathrm{NTM}$ identifies the neoclassical tearing mode.

The quantity applies to one identified magnetic island at a specified instant; it is not a time average, a sum over multiple modes, or an aggregate over multiple islands. It is distinct from the island's angular rotation frequency itself and from its [helical phase](name:neoclassical_tearing_mode_phase), whose second time derivative it represents. It also differs from the [cyclic frequency](name:frequency_of_neoclassical_tearing_mode), which describes cycles per unit time rather than angular rotation.

The orientation is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Sign convention: Positive when the signed angular rotation frequency increases with time, with positive rotation defined by helical-phase advance in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

worked.name: runaway_electron_critical_momentum_volume_averaged_due_to_avalanche
worked.description_before: Volume-averaged momentum threshold for runaway-electron avalanche multiplication, separating collisional drag-dominated electrons from those capable of net acceleration and secondary runaway production.
worked.description_after: Volume-averaged momentum threshold for runaway-electron avalanche multiplication, separating collisional drag-dominated electrons from those capable of net acceleration and secondary runaway production.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the plasma-volume average of the local critical momentum threshold for avalanche-driven runaway-electron generation. It characterizes the boundary between collisional drag-dominated and net-accelerated electron dynamics.

The volume average is defined by

$$
p_{c,\mathrm{av}} = \frac{1}{V}\int_V p_c(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $p_{c,\mathrm{av}}$ is the averaged threshold, $V$ is the plasma volume, $dV$ is a differential volume element, and $p_c(\mathbf{r})$ is the local critical momentum due to avalanche at position $\mathbf{r}$.

This quantity is an unweighted volume average, not the momentum carried by the runaway-electron population and not a volume average of electron momentum. It is the spatially aggregated form of the local avalanche threshold and is distinct from the broader momentum due to avalanche, which need not denote a critical threshold.

worked.name: time_derivative_of_derivative_of_volume_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate
worked.description_before: Temporal change of the geometric volume derivative with respect to the dimensionful toroidal flux coordinate for each nested magnetic flux surface.
worked.description_after: Temporal change of the geometric volume derivative with respect to the dimensionful toroidal flux coordinate for each nested magnetic flux surface.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the temporal rate of change of the volume change associated with an increment of dimensionful toroidal flux coordinate on a nested magnetic flux surface.

It is defined by

$$
\left.\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\left(\frac{\partial V}{\partial \rho_{\mathrm{tor}}}\right)\right|_{\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}}
$$

where $V$ is the cumulative volume enclosed by the flux surface, $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the dimensionful toroidal flux coordinate labeling that surface, and $t$ is time. The outer derivative is taken at fixed $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$, following the corresponding moving flux surface as the equilibrium evolves.

The quantity applies to an individual nested magnetic flux surface and has no species, population, or source-process weighting. It is a temporal derivative of a geometric metric coefficient, not the enclosed volume itself, a volume integral, a flux-surface average, or an aggregation over multiple surfaces.

It is the time-transformed counterpart of the [volume derivative with respect to toroidal flux coordinate](name:flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_major_radius): the linked quantity is the inner derivative $\partial V/\partial \rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$, while this quantity applies the outer partial-time-derivative operator to it.

worked.name: time_derivative_of_diamagnetic_energy
worked.description_before: Time derivative of the global diamagnetic stored energy, representing the rate of change of diamagnetic plasma energy content inferred from diamagnetic measurements.
worked.description_after: Diamagnetic energy accumulation rate for the whole plasma, based on total perpendicular pressure including thermal and fast-particle contributions.
worked.documentation_after:
The diamagnetic energy accumulation rate describes changes in the global plasma stored-energy measure associated with pressure perpendicular to the local magnetic field.

Applying the [time derivative](concept:time_derivative) to [diamagnetic energy](name:diamagnetic_energy) gives:

$$
\frac{\partial W_{\mathrm{dia}}}{\partial t}
$$

where $W_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the global diamagnetic plasma stored energy and $t$ is time.

The differentiated energy is three-halves of the volume integral of total perpendicular pressure over the plasma, including both thermal and fast-particle contributions. Consequently, this derivative is not restricted to thermal energy evolution. It is a global accumulation term, not a local power density or a power attributed to an individual heating or loss mechanism.

Sign convention: Positive when the global diamagnetic plasma stored energy increases with time.

The time derivative is the rate of change of a quantity with time at a fixed point or label.

worked.name: time_derivative_of_electron_density
worked.description_before: Rate of change of free-electron number density, with spatial aggregation determined by the specialization and positive values indicating increasing electron content.
worked.description_after: Rate of change of free-electron number density, with spatial aggregation determined by the specialization and positive values indicating increasing electron content.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the temporal rate of change of free-electron number density. It describes how the electron content per physical volume changes, whether the density is evaluated locally or after a defined spatial aggregation.

The transformed quantity is defined by

$$
\dot{n}_{e,\mathcal{A}}(t) = \frac{d}{dt}\,\mathcal{A}[n_e(\mathbf{r},t)]
$$

where $\dot{n}_{e,\mathcal{A}}$ is the rate of change, $n_e(\mathbf{r},t)$ is the local [electron density](name:electron_density), $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $t$ is time, and $\mathcal{A}$ is the applicable spatial aggregation operation.

The quantity applies to the free-electron population and retains the density aggregation of its specialization. The parent does not itself prescribe a local value, line average, volume average, region, or other spatial weighting; these are supplied by the more specific standard name. It denotes a density rate rather than a total electron-particle rate obtained by integrating over volume.

The [volume-averaged time derivative of electron density](name:volume_averaged_time_derivative_of_electron_density) is a specialization in which $\mathcal{A}$ is the confined-plasma volume average. Positive values indicate increasing aggregated electron density, while negative values indicate decreasing aggregated electron density.

worked.name: time_derivative_of_total_thermal_plasma_internal_energy
worked.description_before: Temporal rate of change of the plasma’s total thermal internal energy, representing net thermal power deposited into or removed from the plasma.
worked.description_after: Net rate of change of stored random kinetic energy in thermal plasma populations, integrated over the plasma volume and summed over those populations.
worked.documentation_before:
The time derivative of total thermal plasma internal energy is the net temporal rate at which the aggregate thermal energy of the plasma changes. Positive accumulation denotes increasing thermal energy, while negative accumulation denotes net thermal-energy loss.

$$
P_{\mathrm{net,th}}(t) = \frac{dU_{\mathrm{th,pl}}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{net,th}}$ is the total thermal-energy change rate, $U_{\mathrm{th,pl}}$ is the total thermal internal energy of the plasma, and $t$ is time.

The underlying energy is integrated over the plasma volume and aggregated over the included thermal plasma populations. It excludes nonthermal-particle energy, bulk-flow kinetic energy, and electromagnetic-field energy; it is not restricted to a single species or energy-transfer channel.

This quantity is the time derivative of [total thermal plasma internal energy](name:total_thermal_plasma_internal_energy). It is a global thermal-energy balance quantity, distinct from [volume-integrated electron power density](name:volume_integrated_electron_power_density), which is restricted to the electron population, and from [power at inside flux surface](name:power_at_inside_flux_surface), which is associated with a specified enclosed region.

Sign convention: Positive when the total thermal plasma internal energy increases with time.
worked.documentation_after:
The [time derivative](concept:time_derivative) of total thermal plasma internal energy is the signed thermal-energy accumulation term in the global plasma energy balance.

The defining expression is:

$$
\frac{\partial W_{\mathrm{th}}}{\partial t}
$$

where $W_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the [total thermal plasma internal energy](name:total_thermal_plasma_internal_energy) and $t$ is time.

The differentiated energy is integrated over the plasma volume and summed over thermal plasma populations. It excludes ordered-flow, magnetic-field, radiation-field, neutral-particle, and fast-particle energy. The derivative reflects the net balance of heating, transport, and radiative losses; it is neither a local power density nor deposited heating power alone.

Sign convention: Positive when the total thermal plasma internal energy increases with time.

The time derivative is the rate of change of a quantity with time at a fixed point or label.

worked.name: toroidal_current_density_flux_surface_averaged_at_constraint_position
worked.description_before: Signed toroidal current-density constraint obtained by geometrically normalized averaging over the magnetic surface that passes through a specified constraint position.
worked.description_after: Signed toroidal current-density constraint obtained by geometrically normalized averaging over the magnetic surface that passes through a specified constraint position.
worked.documentation_before:
The quantity is the toroidal component of plasma current density represented by a flux-surface average, with the magnetic surface selected by a specified constraint position. It is a signed current-density quantity, not the local toroidal current density at the position itself.

The flux-surface-averaged value is defined by

$$
J_{\\phi,\\mathrm{FS}}(\\chi_c)=\\frac{\\left\\langle j_\\phi/R\\right\\rangle_{\\chi_c}}{\\left\\langle 1/R\\right\\rangle_{\\chi_c}}
$$

where $J_{\\phi,\\mathrm{FS}}$ is the resulting flux-surface-averaged toroidal current density, $j_\\phi$ is the local toroidal component of plasma current density, $R$ is major radius, and $\\langle\\cdot\\rangle_{\\chi_c}$ denotes a flux-surface average over the magnetic surface selected by the constraint-position label $\\chi_c$. The quantities $R$, $\\phi$, and $Z$ refer to the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\\phi,Z)$ frame, with $\\phi$ the toroidal angle and $Z$ the vertical coordinate.

The scope is the plasma current density on the complete magnetic surface through the specified constraint position, aggregated by the normalized geometric weighting in the defining relation rather than by a local point value. It does not select a particle species, orbit class, or current-drive mechanism, and it is distinct from a local or component-restricted current-density contribution.

This quantity is the constraint-position, flux-surface-averaged form of [toroidal total current density](name:toroidal_total_current_density). It differs from [parallel flux-surface-averaged current density at constraint position](name:parallel_flux_surface_averaged_current_density_at_constraint_position), which uses the magnetic-field-parallel projection instead of the geometric toroidal projection.

Sign convention: Positive when the toroidal current-density component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\\phi$.

worked.name: total_hydrogenic_density
worked.description_before: Hydrogen-isotope abundance measure derived from included charge states and isotopes, either averaged along a line or over a volume or used to normalize neutral-state density.
worked.description_after: Hydrogen-isotope abundance measure derived from included charge states and isotopes, either averaged along a line or over a volume or used to normalize neutral-state density.
worked.documentation_before:
Hydrogenic-density-derived quantities quantify the abundance of hydrogen-isotope particles with the included isotopic species and charge states. Depending on the derivative, the total density is averaged along a line, averaged over a volume, or used as the reference denominator for a neutral-state composition fraction.

The underlying [hydrogenic density](name:hydrogenic_density) is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{H}} = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{H}} \sum_q n_{s,q}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the total hydrogenic number density, $\mathcal{H}$ is the set of included hydrogen-isotope species, $q$ is charge state, and $n_{s,q}$ is the number density of species $s$ in state $q$.

The line-averaged total hydrogenic density and volume-averaged total hydrogenic density retain density character under their respective averaging operations. The [neutral-state density ratio](name:ratio_of_neutral_state_density_to_total_hydrogenic_density) is instead a composition fraction formed by dividing a neutral charge-state density by $n_{\mathrm{H}}$, and is therefore not itself a density.
worked.documentation_after:
