worked.name: tritium_density
worked.description_before: Local number density of tritium ions in the plasma, the foundational fuel-ion parameter underlying chord-averaged, volume-averaged, and isotopic ratio child quantities.
worked.description_after: Number density of tritium ions is the number of positively charged tritium nuclei per physical volume of plasma. The ions of the species are counted over all charge states, with neutral atoms excluded.
worked.documentation_before:
Tritium ion number density $n_T$ quantifies the local concentration of hydrogen-3 fuel ions in the plasma. It serves as the common physical basis for a family of derived quantities: the chord-integrated mean [line_averaged_tritium_density](name:line_averaged_tritium_density), the confined-volume mean [volume_averaged_tritium_density](name:volume_averaged_tritium_density), and dimensionless isotopic ratios such as ratio_of_tritium_density_to_electron_density and [ratio_of_tritium_density_to_deuterium_density](name:ratio_of_tritium_density_to_deuterium_density).

In deuterium-tritium (DT) fusion plasmas the local volumetric reaction rate is:

$$
R_{DT} = n_T \, n_D \langle \sigma v \rangle_{DT}
$$

where $n_D$ is the deuterium ion number density and $\langle \sigma v \rangle_{DT}$ is the Maxwellian-averaged DT fusion reactivity. The combined DT fuel-ion purity relative to the electron population is tracked by ratio_of_deuterium_tritium_density_to_electron_density.

Tritium density is inferred from active charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy, neutron emission measurements in DT plasmas, or pellet injection and fueling diagnostics.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of tritium. The local density is the zeroth velocity-space moment:

$$
n_{\mathrm{T}} = \int f_{\mathrm{T}}(\mathbf{v})\,\mathrm{d}^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the tritium-ion number density, $f_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the tritium-ion velocity distribution at the point under consideration, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $\mathrm{d}^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The integral covers the complete tritium-ion velocity distribution.

This species-specific density is not restricted to a particular plasma region and is distinct from the total number density of all ion species. No spatial averaging is implicit.

The [line-averaged tritium density](name:line_averaged_tritium_density) and [volume-averaged tritium density](name:volume_averaged_tritium_density) are respectively chord and confined-plasma-volume averages of this local density. It is also the numerator of the [tritium-to-deuterium density ratio](name:ratio_of_tritium_density_to_deuterium_density), whose denominator is [deuterium density](name:deuterium_density); that ratio describes isotope composition rather than absolute concentration.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: tungsten_density
worked.description_before: Number density of tungsten ions summed over all positive ionization states, excluding neutral tungsten, at a specified location or spatial average.
worked.description_after: Number density of tungsten ions summed over all positive ionization states, excluding neutral tungsten, at a specified location or spatial average.
worked.documentation_before:
Tungsten-ion number density is the particle count per unit volume for all positively charged tungsten ions, with neutral tungsten excluded. It may denote a local value or a spatially averaged value over a defined domain.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{W}} = \sum_{Z=1}^{74} n_{\mathrm{W}}^{Z+}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{W}}$ and $n_{\mathrm{W}}^{Z+}$ are number densities in m$^{-3}$, and $Z$ is the positive tungsten charge state. Specific instances include [volume-averaged tungsten density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density), [tungsten density at magnetic axis](name:tungsten_density_at_magnetic_axis), and [tungsten density at divertor target](name:tungsten_density_at_divertor_target); these differ by evaluation locus or averaging domain. Neutral tungsten is not included.
worked.documentation_after:
Tungsten-ion number density is the particle count per unit volume for all positively charged tungsten ions, with neutral tungsten excluded. It may denote a local value or a spatially averaged value over a defined domain.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{W}} = \sum_{Z=1}^{74} n_{\mathrm{W}}^{Z+}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{W}}$ and $n_{\mathrm{W}}^{Z+}$ are number densities in m$^{-3}$, and $Z$ is the positive tungsten charge state. Specific instances include [volume-averaged tungsten density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density), [tungsten density at magnetic axis](name:tungsten_density_at_magnetic_axis), and [tungsten density at divertor target](name:tungsten_density_at_divertor_target); these differ by evaluation locus or averaging domain. Neutral tungsten is not included.

worked.name: volume_averaged_argon_density
worked.description_before: Volume-averaged number density of argon ions over the confined plasma volume, summed over all ionization stages.
worked.description_after: Number density of argon ions summed over positive charge states and averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface, excluding neutral argon.
worked.documentation_before:
The volume-averaged argon ion number density is the spatial mean of the local [argon ion density](name:argon_density) throughout the confined plasma volume, including contributions from every argon ionization stage. It is distinct from a local or charge-state-resolved density.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle n_\mathrm{Ar}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{p}}\int_{V_\mathrm{p}} n_\mathrm{Ar}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $V_\mathrm{p}$ is the confined plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $\mathrm{d}V$ is a volume element, and $n_\mathrm{Ar}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local argon ion density. The local density is charge-state summed, $n_\mathrm{Ar}(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{q=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar},q}(\mathbf{r})$, where $q$ is the argon ionization stage. This quantity provides the argon-density numerator for the impurity concentration ratio [ratio of volume-averaged argon density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_argon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of argon. Its relation to the local [argon density](name:argon_density) is

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\,dV
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the local argon-ion number density, $\langle n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged value, $V$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is a volume element.

The contributing argon charge numbers range from one through eighteen, and both thermal and nonthermal ions contribute. Each ion contributes one particle, without weighting by electric charge or mass.

This is the argon-specific instance of [volume-averaged ion density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density), not the all-species [volume-averaged total ion density](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_density). It differs from [line-averaged argon density](name:line_averaged_argon_density), which averages along a specified plasma chord. Multiplying this volume average by the confined plasma volume gives the total number of argon ions within that volume.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: volume_averaged_beryllium_density
worked.description_before: Volume-averaged number density of beryllium impurity ions over the confined plasma volume, summed over all ionization states and excluding neutral beryllium atoms.
worked.description_after: Number density of beryllium ions summed over positive charge states and averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface, excluding neutral beryllium.
worked.documentation_before:
The volume-averaged beryllium ion number density quantifies the mean beryllium impurity content throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the volume average of the local [beryllium ion number density](name:beryllium_density), rather than a value at a particular position or along a diagnostic chord.

$$
\overline{n}_\mathrm{Be} = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{p}} \int_{V_\mathrm{p}} n_\mathrm{Be}(\mathbf{r})\,dV = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{p}} \int_{V_\mathrm{p}} \sum_{z=1}^{4} n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $V_\mathrm{p}$ is the confined plasma volume, $dV$ is a volume element, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}$ is the local number density of beryllium ions with charge state $z+$, with $z=1$ through $4$. Neutral beryllium is excluded. The resulting global quantity is distinct from the [line-averaged beryllium density](name:line_averaged_beryllium_density) and provides the numerator for the [ratio of volume-averaged beryllium density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_beryllium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of beryllium. Its relation to the local [beryllium density](name:beryllium_density) is

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Be}}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_{\mathrm{Be}}\,dV
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the local beryllium-ion number density, $\langle n_{\mathrm{Be}}\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged value, $V$ is the confined plasma volume, and $dV$ is a volume element.

The contributing beryllium charge numbers range from one through four, and both thermal and nonthermal ions contribute. Each ion counts once, without electric-charge or mass weighting. This is a single-species number density, not an all-species total, charge density, or mass density; the spatial mean is distinct from a local value or a chord mean.

This is the beryllium-specific member of the [volume-averaged ion density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density) family. Multiplying it by the averaging volume gives the number of beryllium ions within that volume. Dividing it by the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density) over the same volume gives the [beryllium-to-electron abundance ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_beryllium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density); this ratio of averages is not generally the volume average of the local density ratio.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: volume_averaged_deuterium_density
worked.description_before: Deuterium ion density averaged over the plasma volume is the mean local number density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion population.
worked.description_after: Number density of deuterium ions summed over positive charge states and averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface, excluding neutral deuterium.
worked.documentation_before:
Deuterium ion density averaged over the plasma volume is the mean local number density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion population. It is the charge-state-summed spatial average of the local [deuterium density](name:deuterium_density).

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_D = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_D(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_D$ is the volume-averaged deuterium density, $V$ is the specified plasma-volume domain, and $n_D(\mathbf{r})$ is the local deuterium density at position $\mathbf{r}$. The local density is summed over positive ionization states and excludes neutral atoms, molecular deuterium, and non-deuterium species.

This quantity averages over the specified plasma volume rather than along a chord; the latter is represented by [line-averaged deuterium density](name:line_averaged_deuterium_density).
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of deuterium. Its relation to the local [deuterium density](name:deuterium_density) is

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm D}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_{\mathrm D}\,dV
$$

where $n_{\mathrm D}$ is the local deuterium-ion number density, $\langle n_{\mathrm D}\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged value, $V$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is a volume element.

Each deuteron contributes one particle, without charge or mass weighting. This quantity is a volume mean rather than a local concentration or chord mean. Multiplying it by the enclosed volume gives the deuteron inventory within that volume.

Unlike the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density), this quantity includes deuterium alone, not the combined fuel-ion population. It supplies the numerator of the [ratio of volume-averaged deuterium density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), whose numerator and denominator refer to the same plasma volume.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density
worked.description_before: Deuterium-tritium density is the volume-averaged ion number density of the combined deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species, treating deuterium and tritium as one effective species.
worked.description_after: Number density of deuterium–tritium fuel ions treated as one effective species, including all ionic charge states but no neutral atoms, averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface.
worked.documentation_before:
Deuterium-tritium density is the volume-averaged ion number density of the combined deuterium-tritium fuel-ion pseudo-species, treating deuterium and tritium ions as one effective species. It is obtained from the local [deuterium-tritium density](name:deuterium_tritium_density), which is summed over all ion charge states.

The defining volume average is

$$
\bar n_{DT} = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_{DT}\,dV
$$

where $\bar n_{DT}$ and $n_{DT}$ are number densities in m$^{-3}$, $V$ is the specified averaging volume in m$^{3}$, and $dV$ is its volume element. The local density satisfies $n_{DT}=n_D+n_T$, with $n_D$ and $n_T$ the corresponding charge-state-summed deuterium and tritium ion densities.

The quantity includes only deuterium and tritium fuel ions represented by the effective pseudo-species; neutral atoms and molecules, reaction products, and impurity ions are excluded. Unlike the [line-averaged deuterium-tritium density](name:line_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density), it uses a volume measure rather than a line-of-sight average, and it supplies the numerator of the [ratio of volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of deuterium tritium. Its relation to the local [deuterium–tritium density](name:deuterium_tritium_density) is

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_{\mathrm{DT}}\,dV
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the local effective fuel-ion number density, $\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}}\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged value, $V$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is a volume element.

The local effective-species density satisfies $n_{\mathrm{DT}}=n_{\mathrm D}+n_{\mathrm T}$, where $n_{\mathrm D}$ is the [deuterium-ion density](name:deuterium_density) and $n_{\mathrm T}$ is the tritium-ion density. Consequently, this average equals the sum of the [volume-averaged deuterium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density) and the corresponding tritium density when both use the same averaging volume. The effective species denotes the combined fuel population, not the deuterium–tritium fusion reaction channel.

Multiplying this average by the confined plasma volume gives the combined fuel-ion inventory. Unlike [line-averaged deuterium–tritium density](name:line_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density), it describes a volume mean rather than a chord mean. It supplies the numerator of the [ratio of volume-averaged deuterium–tritium density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density); that ratio compares two volume means rather than averaging a local density ratio.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: volume_averaged_effective_charge
worked.description_before: Dimensionless volume-averaged effective ionic charge of a plasma mixture, formed by averaging the local second ionic charge moment normalized by free-electron density over the confined plasma volume.
worked.description_after: Volume-averaged effective charge expresses the plasma ion mixture's mean composition factor for electron–ion Coulomb scattering over the plasma volume.
worked.documentation_before:
Volume-averaged effective ionic charge is the effective charge of the complete ion mixture after spatially averaging the local charge-weighted ionic charge moment over the confined plasma volume.

The defining relation is

$$
Z_{\mathrm{eff},V} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} Z_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{eff},V}$ is the volume-averaged effective charge, $Z_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local [effective charge](name:effective_charge), $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, and $dV$ is the volume element.

The average applies to the complete included ion mixture at every position, with ionic contributions summed over all represented species and charge states. It covers the confined plasma volume and is not restricted to one species, one charge state, one region, or one flux surface; it is distinct from an ordinary ion charge average.

This quantity is the volume-averaged counterpart of [effective charge](name:effective_charge). It differs from flux-surface-averaged effective charge at the plasma boundary, which averages the local effective charge over a boundary surface, and from [volume-averaged ion charge](name:volume_averaged_ion_charge), which represents an ordinary ion charge number rather than the second charge moment normalized by free-electron density.
worked.documentation_after:
Volume-averaged effective charge characterizes the composition-dependent contribution of the full plasma ion mixture to electron–ion Coulomb scattering. It applies the volume average to the local [effective charge](name:effective_charge) throughout the plasma volume.

The local quantity entering the average is defined by:

$$
Z_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{\sum_a n_a Z_a^2}{n_e}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the local effective charge, $a$ indexes each ion species and positive charge state, $n_a$ is its local number density, $Z_a$ is its ionic charge number, and $n_e$ is the local free-electron number density.

The sum includes all positive charge states of all ion species, including impurities. Neutral atoms do not contribute to the charge-number moment, and bound electrons are excluded from the free-electron density. The spatial average acts on the local ratio; it is not generally the ratio of the separately volume-averaged numerator and denominator, and no additional electron-density weighting is applied.

This is a mixture-level composition quantity, distinct from the species-specific [volume-averaged ion charge](name:volume_averaged_ion_charge).

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_effective_hydrogenic_mass
worked.description_before: Volume-averaged effective hydrogenic mass is the plasma-volume mean of the local density-weighted mass per hydrogen, deuterium, or tritium ion.
worked.description_after: Volume-averaged effective hydrogenic mass is the plasma-volume average of the local density-weighted atomic mass of hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium ions.
worked.documentation_before:
Volume-averaged effective hydrogenic mass is the volume mean of the local [effective hydrogenic mass](name:effective_hydrogenic_mass) of the hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium ion mixture. Density weighting determines the local mixture mass, while volume weighting determines its spatial average.

The volume average is defined by:

$$
\langle m_{\mathrm{eff,H}}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V m_{\mathrm{eff,H}}\,dV
$$

where $\langle m_{\mathrm{eff,H}}\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged effective hydrogenic mass, $m_{\mathrm{eff,H}}$ is the local effective hydrogenic mass, $V$ is the plasma volume over which the average is taken, and $dV$ is an infinitesimal volume element. The local mass is $m_{\mathrm{eff,H}}=(m_H n_H+m_D n_D+m_T n_T)/(n_H+n_D+n_T)$, where $m_H$, $m_D$, and $m_T$ are the masses of hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium ions, respectively, and $n_H$, $n_D$, and $n_T$ are their respective ion number densities.

Only hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium ions contribute to the local mixture; neutral particles, electrons, and other ion species are excluded. This volume average of the local density-weighted mass is not generally equal to the ratio of volume-integrated hydrogenic mass density to volume-integrated hydrogenic number density. Unlike the [line-averaged effective hydrogenic mass](name:line_averaged_effective_hydrogenic_mass), it averages over the plasma volume rather than along a path.
worked.documentation_after:
Volume-averaged effective hydrogenic mass describes the hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium ion mixture through the volume average of its local [effective hydrogenic mass](name:effective_hydrogenic_mass) over the plasma volume. It characterizes isotope composition rather than the mass of one specified isotope.

The local mass entering this average is

$$
m_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{m_{\mathrm H}n_{\mathrm H} + m_{\mathrm D}n_{\mathrm D} + m_{\mathrm T}n_{\mathrm T}}{n_{\mathrm H} + n_{\mathrm D} + n_{\mathrm T}}
$$

where $m_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the local effective hydrogenic mass; $m_{\mathrm H}$, $m_{\mathrm D}$, and $m_{\mathrm T}$ are the atomic masses of hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium, respectively; and $n_{\mathrm H}$, $n_{\mathrm D}$, and $n_{\mathrm T}$ are their corresponding ion number densities. Each isotope density is summed over all ionic charge states and excludes neutral atoms. Nonhydrogenic species do not contribute, and the local definition requires a nonzero total hydrogenic ion density.

Volume averaging acts on the local density-weighted mass ratio. It does not instead form that ratio from volume-averaged isotope densities; the two operations need not agree when isotope composition and total hydrogenic ion density vary across the plasma.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_electron_decay_time_due_to_disruption
worked.description_before: E-folding time of the plasma-volume-averaged electron temperature during the thermal quench of a disruption.
worked.description_after: Time over which the plasma-volume-averaged electron temperature falls by a factor of e during exponential cooling in a disruption thermal quench.
worked.documentation_before:
This decay time describes the exponential collapse of electron temperature averaged over the entire plasma volume during a disruption thermal quench.

Within the exponential decay interval, it is defined by:

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $\tau$ is the exponential decay time, $t$ is time, $t_0$ is a reference time within that interval, and $\langle T_e\rangle_V(t_0)$ is the volume-averaged electron temperature at that reference time. The volume average is $\langle T_e\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V T_e\,dV$, where $T_e$ is the local [electron temperature](name:electron_temperature), $V$ is the plasma volume, and $dV$ is a volume element.

The average is weighted by volume, not by electron density. Its exponential decay time is distinct from the [electron-temperature decay time at the magnetic axis](name:electron_decay_time_at_magnetic_axis_due_to_disruption), which describes a local temperature decrease. Unlike the [linear 20–80% decay time of volume-averaged thermal electron temperature](name:linear_thermal_electron_decay_time_volume_averaged_due_to_disruption), this quantity is defined by an exponential law rather than a linear decline between specified temperature fractions.
worked.documentation_after:
The exponential decay time describes the collapse of the plasma-volume-averaged electron temperature during the thermal quench of a disruption.

It is defined by the exponential decay law:

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $T_e$ is the [electron temperature](name:electron_temperature), $V$ is the plasma volume, $\langle T_e\rangle_V$ denotes its volume average, $t$ is time, $t_0$ is a reference time within the thermal quench, and $\tau$ is the exponential decay time. The value $\langle T_e\rangle_V(t_0)$ is the averaged temperature at that reference time.

The decay time applies to the plasma-volume-averaged temperature, not to a volume average of local decay times. It is distinct from the [magnetic-axis electron-temperature decay time](name:electron_decay_time_at_magnetic_axis_due_to_disruption), which describes cooling at a single locus. It also differs from the [linear-extrapolated decay time](name:linear_thermal_electron_decay_time_volume_averaged_due_to_disruption), which uses fractional-threshold linear extrapolation rather than an exponential decay law.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_electron_density
worked.description_before: Number density of free electrons averaged over the plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface, including thermal and nonthermal populations.
worked.description_after: Number density of electrons averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface, counting both thermal and nonthermal free electrons.
worked.documentation_before:
Number density of electron

The volume average of the local [electron density](name:electron_density) is defined by

$$
\langle n_e\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_e\,dV
$$

where $n_e$ is the local free-electron number density, $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is its volume average, $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface and specifies the integration region, and $dV$ is a physical volume element. Multiplying the average by that volume gives the total number of free electrons inside the boundary.

All free-electron populations, including thermal and nonthermal electrons, are included; electrons bound in atoms, molecules, or ions are excluded. Plasma outside the last closed flux surface is excluded from the average. Unlike [line-averaged electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density), this quantity is a physical-volume mean rather than a chord mean.

The same spatial averaging applies to [volume-averaged ion density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density), but that quantity counts the specified ion population rather than electrons. This electron mean supplies the denominator of abundance ratios such as the [ratio of volume-averaged carbon density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_carbon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density); such a ratio uses separately averaged densities over the same volume, not a volume average of their local ratio.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of electron. The averaged quantity is the local [electron density](name:electron_density). Its relationship to the electron inventory in the confined plasma is

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $N_e$ is the total number of free electrons within the confined plasma, $V$ is the volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, $n_e$ is the local electron number density, and $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is its volume average.

Bound electrons and electrons outside this volume are excluded. Each free electron contributes one particle, without charge or mass weighting. This is a volume mean, not a local value, a chord mean, or the [electron density at the plasma boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary).

The [volume-averaged ion density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density) uses the same averaging region but counts ions of a specified species rather than electrons. The electron mean supplies the denominator in ion-to-electron abundance ratios, including the [ratio of volume-averaged argon density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_argon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), with both populations averaged over the same volume.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_electron_number_density_over_scrape_off_layer
worked.description_before: Volume-averaged electron number density in the scrape-off layer, equal to the total number of free electrons in the averaging region divided by its volume.
worked.description_after: Volume-averaged electron number density in the scrape-off layer, counting free electrons and excluding electrons bound in atoms or ions.
worked.documentation_before:
Volume-averaged electron number density over the scrape-off layer expresses the free-electron population per total averaging volume. The average weights each volume element by its physical volume.

The defining volume average is

$$
\langle n_e\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_e\,dV
$$

where $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged electron number density, $n_e$ is the [local electron number density](name:electron_number_density_over_scrape_off_layer), $V$ is the volume of the specified scrape-off-layer averaging region, and $dV$ is a physical volume element.

The averaging domain is restricted to the specified scrape-off-layer region rather than the full plasma volume. Only free electrons are counted; electrons bound in atoms or ions are excluded. This quantity is a regional volume mean, not a local density, line average, or line integral. Multiplying it by the averaging volume gives the total free-electron count within that same region.
worked.documentation_after:
Volume-averaged electron number density in the scrape-off layer describes the regional abundance of free electrons, with each electron counted once. Electrons bound in atoms or ions are excluded; particles are not weighted by charge, mass, or energy.

The averaged field is the local [electron number density in the scrape-off layer](name:electron_number_density_over_scrape_off_layer), and the averaging volume is restricted to that region.

This regional mean is neither a pointwise value nor a line-integrated density. It differs from the [confined-plasma volume average](name:volume_averaged_electron_density) by its averaging region.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_electron_temperature
worked.description_before: Temperature of bulk electrons from random translational motion, volume-averaged inside the last closed magnetic flux surface, including during plasma initiation.
worked.description_after: Temperature of bulk electrons from random translational motion, arithmetically averaged over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface.
worked.documentation_before:
Temperature of bulk electrons averaged over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface is the spatial mean of their local energy-equivalent kinetic temperature. For nonrelativistic electrons, the local temperature equals two-thirds of the mean random kinetic energy per particle, excluding directed mean-flow energy.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle T_e\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V T_e\,dV
$$

where $\langle T_e\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged electron temperature, $T_e$ is the local bulk electron temperature, $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface, and $dV$ is the differential physical-volume element.

The quantity applies throughout that enclosed volume, including during plasma initiation. Its aggregation convention is an arithmetic spatial volume average, not a density-weighted particle average or a local value. It differs from [line-averaged electron temperature](name:line_averaged_electron_temperature), which averages along a plasma chord. It is neither total electron thermal energy nor a radiation brightness temperature.

This quantity is obtained by applying volume averaging to [electron temperature](name:electron_temperature); [volume-averaged ion temperature](name:volume_averaged_ion_temperature) applies the corresponding spatial average to a specified ion species. It supplies the denominator of the [ratio of magnetic-axis to volume-averaged electron temperature](name:ratio_of_electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_electron_temperature), which expresses central electron-temperature peaking relative to the plasma-wide mean.
worked.documentation_after:
Temperature of bulk electrons averaged over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface is the spatial mean of their local kinetic temperature. The local temperature represents the isotropic part of random translational energy and excludes directed bulk-flow energy.

For the local [electron temperature](name:electron_temperature) $T_e$, the corresponding volume-averaged temperature $\langle T_e\rangle_V$ satisfies

$$
\langle T_e\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V T_e\,dV
$$

where $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface and $dV$ is the differential physical-volume element.

The spatial average is arithmetic, not weighted by electron number density, and is distinct from volume-integrated electron thermal energy. Its domain excludes plasma outside the last closed magnetic flux surface. Unlike [line-averaged electron temperature](name:line_averaged_electron_temperature), it averages throughout the enclosed volume rather than along a specified chord. The definition also applies during plasma initiation whenever the enclosing surface exists; it is not restricted to that phase.

This quantity includes only the bulk electron population; [volume-averaged ion temperature](name:volume_averaged_ion_temperature) is the corresponding quantity for a specified ion species. It supplies the denominator in the [ratio of magnetic-axis electron temperature to volume-averaged electron temperature](name:ratio_of_electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_electron_temperature), which expresses central electron-temperature peaking.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_helium_3_density
worked.description_before: Volume-averaged helium-3 ion number density is the mean charged-ion population over the confined plasma volume, summed over singly ionized and fully stripped states and excluding neutral atoms.
worked.description_after: Number density of helium-3 ions in all positive charge states, excluding neutral atoms, averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface.
worked.documentation_before:
Volume-averaged helium-3 ion number density is the spatial mean of the charged helium-3 ion population throughout the confined plasma volume. It is derived from the local [helium-3 density](name:helium_3_density), rather than representing a density at one location.

$$
\overline{n}_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}} = \frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x})\,d^3\mathbf{x}
$$

where $V_c$ is the confined plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local helium-3 ion density summed over singly ionized and fully stripped states. Neutral helium-3 atoms are excluded. The [line-averaged helium-3 density](name:line_averaged_helium_3_density) instead averages the same local quantity along a specified path.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of helium 3. Its relation to the local [helium-3 density](name:helium_3_density) is

$$
\langle n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}\,dV
$$

where $n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the local helium-3 ion number density, $\langle n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged number density, $V$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is a volume element.

Both thermal and nonthermal helium-3 ions contribute. Each ion contributes one particle without electric-charge or mass weighting. This is a single-isotope volume mean, not an all-species total, a local value, or a chord mean.

Multiplying this average by the confined plasma volume gives the number of helium-3 ions within that volume. It is a species-specific instance of [volume-averaged ion density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density); the adjacent [volume-averaged helium-4 density](name:volume_averaged_helium_4_density) instead counts helium-4 ions.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: volume_averaged_helium_4_density
worked.description_before: Volume-averaged number density of helium-4 ions over the confined plasma volume, providing a global measure of fusion-ash concentration in deuterium-tritium plasmas.
worked.description_after: Number density of helium-4 ions in all positive charge states, excluding neutral atoms, averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface.
worked.documentation_before:
The volume-averaged helium-4 ion number density quantifies the mean concentration of fusion-ash ions throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the global counterpart of the local [helium-4 ion density](name:helium_4_density) and is distinct from the chord mean [line-averaged helium-4 density](name:line_averaged_helium_4_density).

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_{{}^4\mathrm{He}} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{r})\,d^3\mathbf{r}
$$

where $n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local helium-4 ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume in m$^3$, and $\mathbf{r}$ denotes position.

The helium-4 ion population is summed over all ionic charge states, while neutral helium is excluded. Its ratio to the volume-averaged electron density is defined by [ratio of volume-averaged helium-4 density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of helium 4. Its relation to the local [helium-4 density](name:helium_4_density) is

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{He4}}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_{\mathrm{He4}}\,dV
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the local helium-4 ion number density, $\langle n_{\mathrm{He4}}\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged number density, $V$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is a volume element.

Each counted ion contributes one particle without weighting by electric charge or mass. This is a single-isotope particle-number mean, not an all-species total, electric charge density, mass density, local value, or chord mean.

This quantity is the helium-4-specific instance of [volume-averaged ion density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density). The [volume-averaged helium-3 density](name:volume_averaged_helium_3_density) describes the other helium isotope separately; helium-3 ions do not contribute here.

Multiplying this mean by the confined plasma volume gives the total number of counted helium-4 ions within that volume. Dividing it by the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density) over the same volume gives the [helium-4-to-electron mean-density ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), rather than a volume average of the local density ratio.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: volume_averaged_hydrogen_density
worked.description_before: Volume-averaged number density of hydrogen (protium) ions in the plasma, giving the mean H+ concentration across the confined plasma volume.
worked.description_after: Number density of hydrogen (protium) ions in all ionic charge states, excluding neutral atoms, averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface.
worked.documentation_before:
The volume-averaged hydrogen density quantifies the mean concentration of ionized protium throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the spatial average of the local [hydrogen density](name:hydrogen_density), rather than its value at a particular position.

$$
\overline{n}_H = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_H(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_H$ is the volume-averaged hydrogen density, $n_H(\mathbf{r})$ is the local ionized-protium density at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume, and $dV$ is a volume element. The average includes ionized protium throughout $V_p$ and excludes neutral atomic hydrogen and other isotopes. Unlike [line-averaged hydrogen density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density), it averages over the full plasma volume. Its isotope fraction relative to all hydrogenic fuel is represented by [the volume-averaged hydrogen-density fraction](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density).
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of hydrogen. Its relation to the local [hydrogen density](name:hydrogen_density) is

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{H}}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_{\mathrm{H}}\,dV
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the local protium-ion number density, $\langle n_{\mathrm{H}}\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged value, $V$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is a volume element.

Hydrogen here denotes protium, not the combined hydrogen-isotope population. Each proton contributes one particle without electric-charge or mass weighting. This quantity is a volume mean rather than a local density or a chord mean; multiplying it by the averaging volume gives the number of protium ions within that volume.

This is the protium-specific instance of [volume-averaged ion density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density), whereas [volume-averaged deuterium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density) describes the separate deuterium population. Dividing this quantity by the volume-averaged total hydrogenic-ion density over the same volume gives the protium-ion number fraction.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: volume_averaged_ion_charge_state_average_charge_number
worked.description_before: Mean ionization state of a specified charge-state bundle of one ion species, weighted locally by charge-state concentration and then averaged over the plasma volume.
worked.description_after: Mean ionization state of a specified charge-state bundle of one ion species, concentration-weighted locally and volume-averaged over the plasma.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the plasma-volume average of the local concentration-weighted mean ionic charge number within a specified charge-state bundle of one ion species. Charge-state averaging within the bundle precedes spatial volume averaging.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle \overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V \overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}}\,dV
$$

where $V$ is the plasma volume, $dV$ is a volume element, and $\overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}}$ is the local [bundle-averaged ionic charge number](name:ion_charge_state_average_charge_number). Locally, $\overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}} = \sum_{q\in\mathcal{B}} q x_q$, where $\mathcal{B}$ is the specified bundle, $q$ is the ionic charge number, and $x_q$ is the local number-density fraction of charge state $q$ within that bundle, with $\sum_{q\in\mathcal{B}}x_q = 1$.

Only charge states within the specified bundle contribute; different ion species are not combined. The spatial average uses volume weighting without additional ion-density weighting, so it is not generally equal to the ratio of total ionic charge to total ion number over the plasma. For a bundle containing one fixed charge state, the result equals that state's charge number.

This first charge-number moment is distinct from the [bundle mean-square charge number](name:square_of_ion_charge_state_charge_number), which averages the squared ionic charge number rather than the charge number.
worked.documentation_after:
This quantity is the [volume average](concept:volume_averaged) of the local [ion charge-state average charge number](name:ion_charge_state_average_charge_number) for a specified charge-state bundle of one ion species. The averaging region is the plasma volume unless otherwise specified.

The local mean entering this average is

$$
\overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}} = \frac{\sum_{q\in\mathcal{B}} q\,n_q}{\sum_{q\in\mathcal{B}} n_q}
$$

where $\overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}}$ is the local bundle mean ionic charge number, $\mathcal{B}$ is the specified set of charge states, $q$ is the ionic charge number labeling a state, and $n_q$ is its local number density. This local mean is defined where the bundle has nonzero total number density.

The concentration weighting includes only states within the specified bundle, excluding other species and charge states outside that bundle. Spatial averaging is volume-weighted rather than particle-density-weighted, so the result is not generally the mean obtained by pooling all bundle particles across the volume. For a single-state bundle, both the local and volume-averaged means equal that state's charge number.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_ion_density
worked.description_before: Number density of ions of a specified species, summed over all ionic charge states and averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface.
worked.description_after: Number density of ions of a specified species, summed over positive charge states and averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface, excluding neutral particles.
worked.documentation_before:
Number density of ion

The volume average of the local [ion density](name:ion_density) is defined by

$$
\langle n_i\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_i\,dV
$$

where $i$ labels the specified ion species, $n_i$ is its local ion number density, $\langle n_i\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged number density, $V$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is a volume element.

The species density is summed over all ionic charge states and includes thermal and nonthermal ions; neutral particles are excluded. This is a single-species particle number density, not an all-species total, electric charge density, or mass density. It is a volume mean rather than a local value or a chord mean.

Multiplying this average by the confined plasma volume gives the total number of ions of the specified species within that volume. The [volume-averaged argon density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density) is a species-specific instance of the same averaging definition.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of ion. Its relation to the local [ion density](name:ion_density) is

$$
\langle n_i\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_i\,dV
$$

where $n_i$ is the local number density of the selected ion species, $i$ labels that species, $\langle n_i\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged number density, $V$ is the nonzero confined plasma volume, and $dV$ is a volume element.

The density is summed over all positive charge states of the selected species; neutral particles are excluded. Both thermal and nonthermal ions contribute. Each ion counts once, without electric-charge or mass weighting, so this quantity is neither charge density nor mass density. The corresponding [ion charge-state density](name:ion_charge_state_density) instead resolves a specified charge state.

This quantity concerns one selected species, not an all-species total. Summing it over all ion species using the same averaging volume gives the volume-averaged total ion density. Fixed-species members, such as [volume-averaged argon density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density), specialize the species selection. Multiplying this density by the confined plasma volume gives the number of ions of the selected species within that volume.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_ion_temperature
worked.description_before: Temperature of a specified ion species from random translational motion, arithmetically averaged over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface.
worked.description_after: Temperature of a specified ion species from random translational motion, averaged arithmetically throughout the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface.
worked.documentation_before:
Temperature of a specified ion species averaged over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface is the spatial mean of its local kinetic temperature. The local temperature represents the isotropic part of random translational energy and excludes directed bulk-flow energy.

The volume average of the local [ion temperature](name:ion_temperature) is defined by

$$
\langle T_i\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V T_i\,dV
$$

where $\langle T_i\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged temperature of the specified ion species, $T_i$ is its local temperature, $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface, and $dV$ is the differential physical-volume element.

For the specified species, the local temperature is the density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states; [ion charge-state temperature](name:ion_charge_state_temperature) resolves an individual charge state. The subsequent spatial average is an arithmetic volume average, not a density-weighted particle average or a volume-integrated thermal energy. It does not combine different ion species, unlike [ion average temperature](name:ion_average_temperature).

[Volume-averaged electron temperature](name:volume_averaged_electron_temperature) is the corresponding electron-population quantity. This ion-species volume average supplies the denominator in the [ratio of magnetic-axis ion temperature to volume-averaged ion temperature](name:ratio_of_ion_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_ion_temperature), which expresses central temperature peaking.
worked.documentation_after:
Temperature of a specified ion species averaged over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface describes its thermal state across the confined plasma. The local temperature represents the isotropic part of random translational energy and excludes directed bulk-flow energy.

For the local [ion temperature](name:ion_temperature) $T_i$, the corresponding volume-averaged temperature $\langle T_i\rangle_V$ satisfies

$$
\langle T_i\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V T_i\,dV
$$

where $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface and $dV$ is the differential physical-volume element.

At each location, the species temperature is the density-weighted mean over all charge states of that species. The spatial average is arithmetic, not weighted by ion number density. It is distinct from volume-integrated ion thermal energy and from the cross-species averaging represented by [ion average temperature](name:ion_average_temperature). The averaging domain excludes plasma outside the last closed magnetic flux surface. The definition also applies during plasma initiation whenever the enclosing surface exists; it is not restricted to that phase.

This quantity applies to one specified ion species; [volume-averaged electron temperature](name:volume_averaged_electron_temperature) is the corresponding electron quantity. It supplies the denominator in the [ratio of magnetic-axis ion temperature to volume-averaged ion temperature](name:ratio_of_ion_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_ion_temperature), which expresses central ion-temperature peaking.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_iron_density
worked.description_before: Volume-averaged iron density is the total number density of iron ions, summed over Fe1+ through Fe26+ and averaged over the confined plasma volume.
worked.description_after: Number density of iron ions summed over positive charge states and averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface, excluding neutral iron.
worked.documentation_before:
Volume-averaged iron density is the total number density of iron ions, aggregated over all iron charge states from Fe$^{1+}$ through Fe$^{26+}$ and averaged throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the spatially averaged form of [iron_density](name:iron_density), not a charge-state-resolved quantity.

The volume-averaged density is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{p}}} \int_{V_{\mathrm{p}}} \left(\sum_{z=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}(\mathbf{r})\right)\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the volume-averaged iron density in m$^{-3}$, $V_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the confined plasma volume in m$^{3}$, $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local density of iron charge state $z$, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $dV$ is a volume element.

Neutral iron is excluded, and the result does not preserve the distribution among charge states. It differs from [volume_averaged_ion_density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density) through its fixed iron-species scope and from [iron_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:iron_density_at_magnetic_axis) because it represents a volume average rather than a local axis value.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of iron. Its relation to the local [iron density](name:iron_density) is

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Fe}}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_{\mathrm{Fe}}\,dV
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the local iron-ion number density, $\langle n_{\mathrm{Fe}}\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged value, $V$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is a volume element.

Both thermal and nonthermal iron ions contribute. Each ion contributes one count, without weighting by electric charge or mass. This is a single-species number density, not an all-species total, electric charge density, or mass density.

This volume mean differs from a local value and from [line-averaged iron density](name:line_averaged_iron_density), which averages along a specified plasma chord. Multiplying this volume mean by $V$ gives the number of iron ions within the confined plasma volume.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: volume_averaged_lithium_density
worked.description_before: Volume-averaged total number density of lithium ions, summed over all charge states from Li+ through fully stripped Li3+, within the confined plasma volume.
worked.description_after: Number density of lithium ions summed over all ionic charge states, excluding neutral atoms, and averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface.
worked.documentation_before:
This is the volume average of lithium ion number density, summed over all ionization stages from Li+ through fully stripped Li3+, throughout the confined plasma. Neutral lithium is excluded. The quantity provides a global measure of lithium impurity content rather than a local or boundary value.

The volume average is defined as

$$
\overline{n}_{Li} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_{Li}\,dV
$$

where $n_{Li}$ is the local lithium-ion number density, $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is the physical volume element. Unlike the boundary value flux-surface-averaged lithium density at the plasma boundary, this quantity averages over the full confined volume. Its electron-normalized counterpart is the ratio of volume-averaged lithium density to volume-averaged electron density.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of lithium. The species-specific volume average is

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Li}}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_{\mathrm{Li}}\,dV
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the local lithium-ion number density, $\langle n_{\mathrm{Li}}\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged value, $V$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is a volume element.

Each ion contributes one particle without weighting by electric charge or mass. This is the lithium-specific instance of [volume-averaged ion density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density), not the [volume-averaged total ion density](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_density) summed across species. It is a volume mean rather than a local value or a chord mean.

Multiplying this average by the confined plasma volume gives the number of lithium ions within that volume.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: volume_averaged_parallel_electric_field_due_to_dreicer
worked.description_before: Plasma-volume mean of the parallel electric-field magnitude at which electric acceleration competes with collisional drag on bulk thermal electrons.
worked.description_after: Plasma-volume-averaged electric-field scale at which magnetic-field-parallel acceleration competes with Coulomb drag on bulk thermal electrons.
worked.documentation_before:
The volume-averaged Dreicer field is the plasma-volume mean of the positive local field scale for accelerating bulk thermal electrons into runaway motion parallel to the magnetic field.

It is the unweighted volume average of the [local Dreicer field](name:parallel_electric_field_due_to_dreicer):

$$
\langle E_D\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V E_D\,dV
$$

where $\langle E_D\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged Dreicer field, $E_D$ is the local Dreicer field magnitude, $V$ is the plasma volume, and $dV$ is an infinitesimal volume element.

The average covers the plasma volume and is not weighted by electron density. It averages a positive reference magnitude, not the signed applied parallel electric field. The Dreicer scale characterizes electric acceleration competing with collisional drag on thermal electrons; it is not a sharp threshold below which thermal-tail runaway generation vanishes.

This quantity is distinct from the [volume-averaged runaway-electron critical field](name:volume_averaged_runaway_electron_critical_electric_field), which concerns sustained acceleration of relativistic electrons rather than acceleration out of the bulk thermal population.
worked.documentation_after:
The plasma-volume-averaged Dreicer field characterizes primary runaway generation from the thermal electron population. It is the global average of the local [Dreicer-field magnitude](name:parallel_electric_field_due_to_dreicer), rather than the applied parallel electric field.

Its defining relation is

$$
\langle E_{\mathrm D}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V E_{\mathrm D}\,dV
$$

where $E_{\mathrm D}$ is the local Dreicer-field magnitude, $V$ is the plasma volume, $dV$ is a volume element, and $\langle E_{\mathrm D}\rangle_V$ is the plasma-volume-averaged Dreicer field.

The averaging covers the plasma volume with volume weighting only, not electron-density weighting. The result is a nonnegative field scale, not a signed electric-field component.

It differs from the [volume-averaged runaway-electron critical field](name:volume_averaged_runaway_electron_critical_electric_field), which concerns sustained acceleration of already energetic electrons against collisional drag rather than acceleration out of the thermal population.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_parallel_runaway_electron_current_density
worked.description_before: Plasma-volume average of the signed conventional current-density component carried by runaway electrons along the local magnetic-field direction.
worked.description_after: Parallel current density carried by runaway electrons, expressed as a magnetic-field-weighted plasma-volume average in the reference-field convention.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the plasma-volume average of the local field-aligned conventional current density carried only by runaway electrons. It selects the magnetic-field-parallel contribution of the runaway-electron current before applying the same volume averaging represented by volume-averaged runaway-electron current density.

$$
\left\langle j_{\parallel,\mathrm{RE}} \right\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}}(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the local conventional current-density vector of the runaway-electron population, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the local unit vector in the magnetic-field direction, $V_p$ is the selected plasma volume, and $dV$ is its volume element. Contributions from thermal electrons, ions, and non-runaway populations are excluded. Because this is conventional current, its direction is opposite to the motion of negatively charged runaway electrons.

Sign convention: Positive when the local conventional runaway-electron current component points along the local magnetic-field direction.
worked.documentation_after:
Parallel runaway-electron current density averaged over the plasma volume represents the signed conventional-current contribution of the runaway-electron population. It is the plasma-volume aggregate of [parallel runaway-electron current density](name:parallel_runaway_electron_current_density), using the same reference-field convention.

Its defining relation is:

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $\overline{j}_{\parallel,\mathrm{RE}}$ is this volume-averaged parallel current density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the conventional current-density vector carried by runaway electrons, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, and $B_0$ is the nonzero reference magnetic-field value used for normalization. The brackets $\langle\cdot\rangle_V$ denote the volume-average operator over the plasma volume $V$.

The magnetic-field weighting distinguishes this convention from an unweighted average of the local current projection onto the magnetic-field unit vector. The quantity includes only runaway-electron current, excluding thermal-electron and ion contributions. It is a global current density, not a local value, a single-flux-surface average, or a cross-section-integrated runaway current.

Sign convention: Positive when the plasma-volume average of $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}}\cdot\mathbf{B}$ has the same sign as $B_0$.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_ratio_of_hydrogen_density_to_electron_density
worked.description_before: Ratio of hydrogen (protium) ion density to electron density, averaged over the plasma volume at the time of peak electron density.
worked.description_after: Ratio of volume-averaged protium-ion number density to volume-averaged free-electron number density in the confined plasma, evaluated at the time of peak electron density.
worked.documentation_before:
Ratio of local hydrogen (protium) ion number density to local electron number density, averaged over the plasma volume and evaluated at the time of peak electron density. It expresses hydrogen-ion abundance relative to free electrons.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle n_\mathrm{H}/n_e\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V \frac{n_\mathrm{H}}{n_e}\,dV
$$

where $n_\mathrm{H}$ is the local hydrogen ion number density, $n_e$ is the local free-electron number density, $V$ is the plasma volume and denotes the integration region, and $dV$ is a volume element. The angle brackets denote the volume average. All densities and the integration volume refer to the time of peak electron density; this is not a time average.

The numerator includes all ionic charge states of protium, comprising only singly ionized hydrogen. Neutral hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium are excluded from the numerator. The local ratio requires nonzero electron density wherever it is evaluated.

This quantity is the volume average of the [hydrogen-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_hydrogen_density_to_electron_density), not, in general, the ratio of the two volume-averaged densities. The [lithium counterpart](name:volume_averaged_ratio_of_lithium_density_to_electron_density) applies the same spatial averaging and peak-electron-density evaluation convention to lithium ions.
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of volume-averaged hydrogen (protium) ion number density to volume-averaged free-electron number density, evaluated at the time of peak electron density.

The composition ratio is

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $C_{\mathrm{H}/e}$ is this composition ratio, $n_{\mathrm H}$ is the local [protium-ion number density](name:hydrogen_density), $n_e$ is the local free-electron number density, and $t_*$ is the time of peak electron density. The numerator is the [volume-averaged hydrogen density](name:volume_averaged_hydrogen_density), and the denominator is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density). Both averages use the same nonzero confined plasma volume $V$ inside the last closed flux surface; the denominator must be positive.

The numerator is summed over all positive charge states of protium, counting each ion once without charge or mass weighting. Neutral hydrogen and other hydrogen isotopes are excluded from the numerator. Both thermal and nonthermal particles contribute to their respective densities, while bound electrons are excluded from the denominator.

This quantity uses the separately volume-averaged operands of the local [hydrogen-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_hydrogen_density_to_electron_density); it is not the unweighted volume average of that local ratio. Its electron denominator also distinguishes it from the [protium fraction among hydrogenic ions](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density).

$$a/b$$

The ratio is one quantity divided by another.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_ratio_of_lithium_density_to_electron_density
worked.description_before: Ratio of lithium ion number density to free-electron number density, averaged over the plasma volume at the time of peak electron density.
worked.description_after: Ratio of charge-state-summed lithium-ion density to free-electron density, volume averaged over confined plasma at the time of peak electron density.
worked.documentation_before:
Ratio of lithium ion number density to free-electron number density, averaged over the plasma volume, expresses the mean lithium ion abundance relative to free electrons. It is evaluated at the time of peak electron density.

The local [lithium-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_lithium_density_to_electron_density) is $c_\mathrm{Li}=n_\mathrm{Li}/n_e$, where $n_\mathrm{Li}$ is the local lithium ion number density and $n_e$ is the local free-electron number density. Its volume average is defined by

$$
\langle c_\mathrm{Li}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V c_\mathrm{Li}\,dV
$$

where $\langle c_\mathrm{Li}\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged ratio, $V$ denotes the plasma integration region and its volume, and $dV$ is a volume element. All densities and the integration volume refer to the same evaluation time.

Lithium density is summed over all ionic charge states, from singly ionized through fully stripped lithium; neutral lithium is excluded. The electron density must be nonzero wherever the local ratio is evaluated. This quantity is the volume average of the local ratio, not the ratio of separately volume-averaged densities, and it is not a time average.

The [hydrogen counterpart](name:volume_averaged_ratio_of_hydrogen_density_to_electron_density) applies the same volume averaging and peak-electron-density evaluation convention with hydrogen ion density in the numerator.

$$a/b$$
worked.documentation_after:
Ratio of lithium-ion number density to free-electron number density, formed locally and then volume averaged over the confined plasma inside the last closed flux surface. The quantity is evaluated at the time of peak electron density, rather than averaged over time.

Its defining relation is

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Li}}/n_e\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V \frac{n_{\mathrm{Li}}}{n_e}\,dV
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the local lithium-ion number density, $n_e$ is the local free-electron number density, $V$ is the nonzero confined plasma volume at the evaluation time, $dV$ is a volume element, and the angle-bracketed expression is the volume-averaged lithium abundance relative to electrons. The electron density must be nonzero wherever the local ratio is evaluated.

The lithium density is summed over all positive charge states, excluding neutral lithium. Both thermal and nonthermal particles contribute. Each lithium ion counts once without electric-charge or mass weighting, so the ratio expresses particle abundance rather than lithium's contribution to charge density.

This quantity averages the local [lithium-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_lithium_density_to_electron_density). It is not generally equal to the ratio of [volume-averaged lithium density](name:volume_averaged_lithium_density) to volume-averaged electron density, because averaging and division do not generally commute.

The ratio is one quantity divided by another.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_runaway_electron_critical_electric_field
worked.description_before: Plasma-volume average of the critical parallel electric-field magnitude required for sustained runaway-electron acceleration against collisional drag.
worked.description_after: Plasma-volume-averaged parallel electric-field threshold above which sufficiently energetic electrons can sustain acceleration against relativistic collisional drag.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the unweighted plasma-volume average of the local threshold parallel electric-field magnitude for sustained runaway-electron acceleration against collisional drag.

The volume average of the [runaway-electron critical electric field](name:critical_electric_field) is defined by

$$
\langle E_c\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V E_c\,dV
$$

where $E_c$ is the local critical parallel electric-field magnitude, $V$ is the plasma volume, $dV$ is a spatial volume element, and $\langle E_c\rangle_V$ is the resulting volume average.

The average is weighted by spatial volume, not by electron density. It averages the threshold magnitude rather than the actual electric field and does not replace the local criterion for sustained runaway acceleration.

This threshold concerns sustained acceleration of sufficiently energetic electrons. It is distinct from the [volume-averaged Dreicer field](name:volume_averaged_parallel_electric_field_due_to_dreicer), which characterizes electric acceleration relative to collisional drag on thermal electrons.
worked.documentation_after:
The plasma-volume-averaged critical electric field characterizes the threshold for electric acceleration to overcome relativistic collisional drag on sufficiently energetic electrons. The averaging applies to the local [critical electric-field magnitude](name:critical_electric_field) throughout the plasma volume, not to the actual accelerating electric field.

The local classical Connor–Hastie threshold in a fully ionized plasma is

$$
E_c = \frac{n_e e^3 \ln\Lambda}{4\pi\varepsilon_0^2 m_e c^2}
$$

where $E_c$ is the local critical electric-field magnitude, $n_e$ is the electron number density, $e$ is the elementary-charge magnitude, $\ln\Lambda$ is the Coulomb logarithm, $\varepsilon_0$ is the vacuum permittivity, $m_e$ is the electron rest mass, and $c$ is the speed of light.

This classical threshold concerns collisional drag and does not include additional radiation-reaction losses. Its plasma-volume average is a global summary of local thresholds, not a criterion that guarantees runaway acceleration everywhere in the plasma.

It differs from the [volume-averaged Dreicer field](name:volume_averaged_parallel_electric_field_due_to_dreicer), which characterizes electric acceleration competing with Coulomb drag on bulk thermal electrons rather than the relativistic drag limit.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_runaway_electron_density
worked.description_before: Mean number density of runaway electrons over the confined plasma volume, obtained by averaging the local suprathermal population that remains in the accelerating tail.
worked.description_after: Number density of runaway electrons averaged over the plasma volume, counting the suprathermal population for which electric-field acceleration can overcome collisional drag.
worked.documentation_before:
Volume-averaged runaway electron density is the spatial mean of the local runaway-electron population over the confined plasma volume. Runaway electrons are suprathermal electrons whose momentum makes collisional slowing-down ineffective compared with continued electromagnetic acceleration, as described by [runaway_electron_density](name:runaway_electron_density).

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_\mathrm{RE} = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{p}} \int_{V_\mathrm{p}} n_\mathrm{RE}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $\overline{n}_\mathrm{RE}$ is the volume-averaged runaway electron density, $n_\mathrm{RE}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local runaway electron density at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V_\mathrm{p}$ is the confined plasma volume, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is the physical volume element.

This quantity averages the local density rather than reporting the total runaway-electron count; the latter is obtained by multiplying the average by $V_\mathrm{p}$. It includes the full confined plasma volume and excludes regions outside that volume.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of runaway electron. The runaway-electron inventory in the averaging volume satisfies

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{RE}}$ is the total number of runaway electrons within the averaging volume, $V$ is that nonzero plasma volume, $n_{e,\mathrm{RE}}$ is the local [runaway-electron density](name:runaway_electron_density), and $\langle n_{e,\mathrm{RE}}\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged value.

The averaging domain is the stated plasma volume, not only the region occupied by runaway electrons. All runaway electrons within that volume contribute, regardless of their generation mechanism; nonrunaway electrons are excluded. Each particle counts once, without electric-charge, kinetic-energy, or velocity weighting.

For the same averaging volume, this quantity is the runaway-population contribution to the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), which also includes nonrunaway free electrons. It differs from the [volume-averaged runaway-electron kinetic-energy density](name:volume_averaged_runaway_electron_kinetic_energy_density), which weights the runaway population by particle kinetic energy rather than counting particles.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_runaway_electron_kinetic_energy_density
worked.description_before: Mean relativistic kinetic energy per unit volume of the runaway electron population, obtained by averaging the local kinetic energy density over the confined plasma volume.
worked.description_after: Relativistic kinetic energy density of runaway electrons averaged over the full plasma volume, excluding rest-mass energy.
worked.documentation_before:
The volume-averaged runaway electron kinetic energy density is a global scalar characterizing the mean suprathermal energy stored per unit volume in the runaway electron (RE) population. It is obtained by integrating the local relativistic kinetic energy density over the total confined plasma volume $V$ and dividing by $V$.

The underlying local quantity is the relativistic kinetic energy moment of the RE distribution function:

$$
u_\mathrm{RE}(\mathbf{r}) = \int f_\mathrm{RE}(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{p})\,(\gamma - 1)\,m_e c^2 \, d^3p
$$

where $f_\mathrm{RE}$ is the runaway electron phase-space distribution function, $\gamma = (1 + p^2 / m_e^2 c^2)^{1/2}$ is the Lorentz factor, $m_e$ is the electron rest mass, $c$ is the speed of light, and $\mathbf{p}$ is the relativistic momentum. The volume average is then $\langle u_\mathrm{RE} \rangle = V^{-1} \int_V u_\mathrm{RE}\,dV$.

This quantity is evaluated from kinetic or reduced-fluid runaway electron models, particularly in disruption current-quench simulations where RE populations can reach energies of several to tens of MeV per particle. Multiplying by the plasma volume $V$ recovers the total stored relativistic energy given by [runaway_electron_kinetic_energy](name:runaway_electron_kinetic_energy). The local non-averaged counterpart is runaway_electron_kinetic_energy_density, and the corresponding global particle number density is [volume_averaged_runaway_electron_density](name:volume_averaged_runaway_electron_density).
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of runaway electron. The corresponding total [runaway-electron kinetic energy](name:runaway_electron_kinetic_energy) satisfies:

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $W_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the total runaway-electron kinetic energy within the plasma volume, $V$ is that volume, $w_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the local [runaway-electron kinetic energy density](name:runaway_electron_kinetic_energy_density), and $\langle w_{\mathrm{RE}}\rangle_V$ is its plasma-volume average.

The averaging domain is the entire plasma volume, including regions without runaway electrons, rather than only the volume occupied by the runaway-electron population.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.
