worked.name: volume_averaged_runaway_electron_source_rate
worked.description_before: Volume-averaged production rate of runaway-electron number density over the confined plasma, including all active generation mechanisms and excluding runaway-electron losses.
worked.description_after: Volume-averaged production rate of runaway-electron number density over the confined plasma, including all active generation mechanisms and excluding runaway-electron losses.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the confined-plasma volume average of the local runaway-electron number-density production rate. It represents a production contribution to the runaway-electron balance, not a loss rate.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle S_{\rm RE} \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_c} \int_{V_c} S_{\rm RE}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $S_{\rm RE}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local volumetric source rate, $V_c$ is the confined-plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $dV$ is the volume element. The integrand is the total [runaway electron source rate](name:runaway_electron_source_rate), including all active generation mechanisms. Sink and loss terms are excluded. This quantity is distinct from the volume-averaged runaway-electron density, which describes the population rather than its production rate.
worked.documentation_after:
This quantity is the confined-plasma volume average of the local runaway-electron number-density production rate. It represents a production contribution to the runaway-electron balance, not a loss rate.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle S_{\rm RE} \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_c} \int_{V_c} S_{\rm RE}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $S_{\rm RE}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local volumetric source rate, $V_c$ is the confined-plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $dV$ is the volume element. The integrand is the total [runaway electron source rate](name:runaway_electron_source_rate), including all active generation mechanisms. Sink and loss terms are excluded. This quantity is distinct from the volume-averaged runaway-electron density, which describes the population rather than its production rate.

worked.name: volume_averaged_runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_compton_scattering
worked.description_before: Plasma-volume-averaged source rate of electrons entering the runaway population after receiving energy from gamma-ray photons through Compton scattering.
worked.description_after: Plasma-volume-averaged Compton source rate counts electrons entering the runaway population through energy transfer from gamma-ray photons, averaged over the plasma volume.
worked.documentation_before:
Plasma-volume-averaged runaway-electron source rate due to Compton scattering is the mean volumetric production rate associated with energy transfer from gamma-ray photons to plasma electrons. It counts energetic recoil electrons that enter the runaway regime, where electric-field acceleration overcomes collisional drag.

The volume average is defined by:

$$
\langle S_{\mathrm C}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V S_{\mathrm C}\,dV
$$

where $S_{\mathrm C}$ is the [local runaway-electron source rate due to Compton scattering](name:runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_compton_scattering), $\langle S_{\mathrm C}\rangle_V$ is its plasma-volume average, $V$ is the plasma volume and integration domain, and $dV$ is an infinitesimal volume element.

The average covers the entire plasma and uses volume weighting only, not electron-density weighting. It remains a production rate per unit volume, distinct from the volume-integrated electron production rate.

This contribution forms part of the [volume-averaged total runaway-electron source rate](name:volume_averaged_total_runaway_electron_source_rate), but excludes contributions assigned to other generation mechanisms. It is a generation term, not the net rate of change of runaway-electron density after transport and losses.
worked.documentation_after:
Plasma-volume-averaged Compton source rate describes runaway-electron generation initiated when gamma-ray photons transfer sufficient energy to plasma electrons through Compton scattering.

Applying the [volume average](concept:volume_averaged) over the plasma volume to the [local Compton source rate](name:runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_compton_scattering) gives

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $S_{\mathrm C}$ is the local Compton contribution to runaway-electron production, $n_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the runaway-electron number density, $t$ is time, and $V$ is the plasma volume. Angle brackets denote the volume average, and the restriction $\mathrm C$ selects only the Compton generation contribution.

Only electrons entering the runaway population are counted, not all Compton recoil electrons. The quantity remains a volumetric source rate, rather than a volume-integrated production rate or a net density-change rate including transport and losses.

This contribution enters the [plasma-volume-averaged total runaway-electron source rate](name:volume_averaged_total_runaway_electron_source_rate) alongside the separately attributed generation mechanisms.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_dreicer
worked.description_before: Plasma-volume-averaged source rate of runaway electrons generated from the thermal tail by magnetic-field-parallel electric acceleration below the Dreicer field.
worked.description_after: Plasma-volume-averaged Dreicer source rate counts runaway electrons produced from the thermal distribution's suprathermal tail by parallel electric acceleration below the Dreicer field.
worked.documentation_before:
Plasma-volume-averaged runaway-electron source rate due to Dreicer generation is the mean volumetric production rate from thermal-tail electrons accelerated into the runaway population by the magnetic-field-parallel electric field. The sub-critical electric fields considered here are below the [Dreicer field](name:parallel_electric_field_due_to_dreicer), which characterizes competition between electric acceleration and collisional drag on thermal electrons.

The plasma-volume average is defined by

$$
\langle S_{\mathrm D}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V S_{\mathrm D}\,dV
$$

where $S_{\mathrm D}$ is the local [runaway-electron source rate due to Dreicer generation](name:runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_dreicer), $V$ is the plasma volume, $dV$ is a differential volume element, and $\langle S_{\mathrm D}\rangle_V$ is the resulting volume average.

The average covers the full plasma volume with no additional density weighting. It remains a volumetric source rate; multiplication by the plasma volume gives the total number of runaway electrons produced per unit time through Dreicer generation.

This quantity is the Dreicer contribution to the [volume-averaged total runaway-electron source rate](name:volume_averaged_total_runaway_electron_source_rate). It excludes avalanche, hot-tail, Compton, and other generation mechanisms, and it is not the net density-change rate after transport and losses.
worked.documentation_after:
Plasma-volume-averaged Dreicer source rate counts electrons entering the runaway population through primary electric acceleration from the thermal distribution's suprathermal tail. The accelerating electric field is parallel to the magnetic field and has magnitude below the [Dreicer field](name:parallel_electric_field_due_to_dreicer).

The local source entering this average is defined by:

$$
S_{\mathrm D}=\left.\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{RE}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm D}
$$

where $S_{\mathrm D}$ is the local [runaway-electron source rate due to Dreicer generation](name:runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_dreicer), $n_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is runaway-electron number density, $t$ is time, and the subscript $\mathrm D$ restricts the derivative to Dreicer production.

The averaging region is the plasma volume, without density or current weighting. The result remains a volumetric production rate, not a volume-integrated particle production rate or a net density derivative including transport and losses.

This source contributes to the [volume-averaged total runaway-electron source rate](name:volume_averaged_total_runaway_electron_source_rate), but excludes avalanche multiplication, hot-tail generation, Compton scattering, and tritium-decay generation.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_hot_tail
worked.description_before: Plasma-volume-averaged hot-tail source rate of runaway electrons produced from a suprathermal tail that survives rapid cooling of the thermal electron population.
worked.description_after: Plasma-volume-averaged hot-tail source rate describes runaway-electron production from a suprathermal electron tail surviving rapid bulk-electron cooling.
worked.documentation_before:
Plasma-volume-averaged hot-tail runaway-electron source rate is the volumetric production rate averaged over the plasma volume. It describes runaway generation from a suprathermal electron tail whose collisional relaxation is slower than the cooling of the thermal population.

The unweighted volume average is defined by

$$
\langle S_{\mathrm{ht}}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V S_{\mathrm{ht}}\,dV
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{ht}}$ is the local [hot-tail runaway-electron source rate](name:runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_hot_tail), $V$ is the plasma volume over which the integral is taken, $dV$ is the differential volume element, and $\langle S_{\mathrm{ht}}\rangle_V$ is the resulting plasma-volume average.

Only hot-tail production is included; Dreicer generation, avalanche multiplication, and other generation mechanisms are excluded. This quantity is an average production rate per unit volume, not a volume-integrated electron production rate or a net density-change rate including losses. It is the hot-tail contribution to the [plasma-volume-averaged total runaway-electron source rate](name:volume_averaged_total_runaway_electron_source_rate).
worked.documentation_after:
Plasma-volume-averaged hot-tail runaway-electron source rate quantifies generation from a high-energy electron tail that persists during rapid cooling of the bulk electrons. These tail electrons relax collisionally more slowly than the bulk cools, allowing some to enter the runaway population through electric-field acceleration.

The local source entering this average is defined by:

$$
S_{\mathrm{ht}} = \left.\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{RE}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{ht}}
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{ht}}$ is the local [hot-tail runaway-electron source rate](name:runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_hot_tail), $n_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the [runaway-electron number density](name:runaway_electron_density), $t$ is time, and the subscript $\mathrm{ht}$ selects production by the hot-tail mechanism rather than the complete density evolution.

The quantity applies to the entire plasma volume without density weighting. It is an averaged volumetric source, not the volume-integrated electron production rate. It supplies the hot-tail contribution to the [volume-averaged total runaway-electron source rate](name:volume_averaged_total_runaway_electron_source_rate); other generation mechanisms, transport, and loss terms are excluded.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_time_derivative_of_electron_density
worked.description_before: Rate of change of the electron number density averaged over the confined plasma volume, with positive values indicating increasing mean density.
worked.description_after: Volume-averaged rate of local free-electron density change inside the last closed flux surface, including thermal and nonthermal electrons.
worked.documentation_before:
This quantity is the temporal rate of change of the electron number density after volume averaging over the confined plasma volume. Positive values indicate increasing mean electron density, while negative values indicate decreasing mean electron density.

For a fixed averaging volume, the defining relation is

$$
\frac{d\langle n_e\rangle_V}{dt} = \frac{1}{V}\int_V \frac{\partial n_e}{\partial t}\,dV
$$

where $n_e$ is the local electron number density, $V$ is the confined plasma volume, and $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density).

The volume-average operation is applied to the electron density before time differentiation. This distinguishes the quantity from the more general [time derivative of electron density](name:time_derivative_of_electron_density), which does not specify volume averaging.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of electron. For a fixed averaging volume, the relation between this quantity and the local [electron density](name:electron_density) is:

$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial t}$$

Here, $n_e$ is the local free-electron number density, $t$ is time, $V$ is the nonzero confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface, $dV$ is a volume element, and $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density). The local time derivative is evaluated at each fixed spatial position before the [volume average](concept:volume_averaged). Each electron contributes one particle, without charge or mass weighting.

When the averaging volume changes with time, differentiating its mean also includes changes to the integration region and to $V$; in that case, the time derivative of the mean is not in general equal to the volume average of the local time derivative. This quantity is volume-averaged, unlike the line-averaged [time derivative of electron density](name:time_derivative_of_electron_density).

Sign convention: Positive when the volume-averaged free-electron number density increases with time.

The time derivative is the rate of change of a quantity with time at a fixed point or label.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_total_ion_density
worked.description_before: Volume-averaged total ion number density over the confined plasma volume, summing all ion species and charge states and including thermal and non-thermal ion populations.
worked.description_after: Number density of ions summed over all species and positive charge states, including thermal and nonthermal ions but excluding neutrals, averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface.
worked.documentation_before:
Volume-averaged total ion density is the aggregate ion number density averaged over the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface. It includes all ion species, resolved charge states, and thermal and non-thermal ion populations; it excludes electrons and neutral particles.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_{i,\mathrm{total}} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_{i,\mathrm{total}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_{i,\mathrm{total}}$ is the volume-averaged density, $n_{i,\mathrm{total}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local [total ion density](name:total_ion_number_density) in m$^{-3}$, $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume in m$^3$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $dV$ is the volume element. This is a density average, not the total ion inventory. Unlike [volume-averaged ion density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density), it aggregates all ion species rather than one selected species.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of ion. Its relationship to the [volume-averaged density of a selected ion species](name:volume_averaged_ion_density) is

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $\langle n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged total ion number density, $s$ labels an ion species, $n_s$ is that species' local number density summed over positive charge states, and $\langle n_s\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged number density. The subscript $i$ denotes ions, and $V$ is the same nonzero confined plasma volume for every term.

All positive charge states contribute; the [ion charge-state density](name:ion_charge_state_density) instead resolves one species and charge state. Neutral particles and electrons are excluded. Both thermal and nonthermal ions contribute, unlike the thermal-only population counted by [total thermal ion density](name:total_thermal_ion_density). Each ion counts once without electric-charge or mass weighting, so this quantity is neither charge density nor mass density.

Multiplying this density by the averaging volume gives the total number of ions within that volume.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature
worked.description_before: Density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion population, with all included species and charge states contributing by number density and averaged over the confined plasma volume.
worked.description_after: Temperature of thermal ions from random motion, density-weighted locally over all species and charge states and volume-averaged inside the last closed magnetic flux surface.
worked.documentation_before:
The volume-averaged total ion temperature is the volume average of the local density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion population, including all included thermal ion species and charge states. It represents random thermal motion and excludes directed bulk-flow energy.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{T}_{i,\mathrm{tot}} = \frac{\int_V T_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV}{\int_V dV}
$$

where $V$ is the confined plasma volume, $dV$ is its differential volume element, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $T_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local quantity defined by [total_ion_temperature](name:total_ion_temperature). Species and charge-state density weighting is performed locally before the volume averaging. Unlike [line_averaged_total_ion_temperature](name:line_averaged_total_ion_temperature), this quantity averages over volume rather than along a plasma chord.
worked.documentation_after:
Temperature of the combined thermal ion population averaged over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface describes its thermal state across the confined plasma. The local temperature represents random translational motion and excludes directed bulk-flow energy.

The local quantity being averaged is the [total ion temperature](name:total_ion_temperature), defined by

$$
T_{i,\mathrm{tot}} = \frac{\sum_{s,q} n_{s,q}T_{s,q}}{\sum_{s,q} n_{s,q}}
$$

where $T_{i,\mathrm{tot}}$ is the local effective temperature of the combined thermal ion population, $s$ labels ion species, $q$ labels ionic charge states, $n_{s,q}$ is the corresponding number density, and $T_{s,q}$ is the corresponding local temperature. Both sums include all thermal ion species and charge states in the population.

The number-density weighting combines populations locally; it is not an additional spatial weight. Unlike [volume-averaged ion temperature](name:volume_averaged_ion_temperature), which applies to one specified ion species, this quantity combines all included ion species. It is a temperature rather than a volume-integrated thermal energy, and its averaging domain excludes plasma outside the last closed magnetic flux surface.

The [line-averaged total ion temperature](name:line_averaged_total_ion_temperature) uses the same local population aggregate but averages along a specified plasma chord rather than throughout the enclosed plasma volume.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_total_runaway_electron_source_rate
worked.description_before: Plasma-volume-averaged volumetric production rate of runaway electrons, summed over Dreicer, avalanche, hot-tail, Compton, and tritium-decay generation mechanisms.
worked.description_after: Plasma-volume-averaged total runaway-electron source rate counts electrons entering the runaway population through all active generation mechanisms.
worked.documentation_before:
Plasma-volume-averaged volumetric production rate of runaway electrons is the spatial average, over the plasma volume, of the local total rate at which electrons enter the runaway population. The total rate includes generation by Dreicer, avalanche, hot-tail, Compton, and tritium-decay mechanisms.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\left\langle S_{\mathrm{RE,total}}\right\rangle_V = \frac{1}{|\Omega_p|}\int_{\Omega_p} S_{\mathrm{RE,total}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $\left\langle S_{\mathrm{RE,total}}\right\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged total runaway electron source rate, $S_{\mathrm{RE,total}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the total runaway electron source rate at position $\mathbf{x}$, $\Omega_p$ is the plasma-volume domain, $|\Omega_p|$ is the volume measure of that domain, and $dV$ is the volume element.

This quantity applies to the runaway-electron population within the plasma volume and uses an unweighted volume average of the total local volumetric production rate. The mechanism sum is part of the quantity definition; the total includes component production rates such as the [Dreicer runaway electron source rate](name:runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_dreicer) and the [hot-tail runaway electron source rate](name:runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_hot_tail), but is not restricted to either component.

It is the plasma-volume-averaged counterpart of the total runaway electron source rate. It is a production-rate density averaged over volume, not the absolute number of runaway electrons and not a current-density measure; in particular it is distinct from the [volume-averaged parallel runaway electron current density](name:volume_averaged_parallel_runaway_electron_current_density), which describes charge transport by the runaway population.
worked.documentation_after:
Plasma-volume-averaged total runaway-electron source rate quantifies the generation contribution to the change in runaway-electron number density. The averaging region is the plasma volume, and the total includes all active runaway-generation mechanisms.

The quantity being averaged is the [total runaway-electron source rate](name:total_runaway_electron_source_rate), with mechanism aggregation defined by

$$
S_{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_k S_k
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the local total volumetric runaway-electron source rate, $S_k$ is the local volumetric contribution from generation mechanism $k$, and $k$ ranges over all active mechanisms. These include Dreicer generation, avalanche multiplication, hot-tail generation, Compton scattering, and tritium decay.

The result remains a volumetric production rate, distinct from the volume-integrated particle production rate. It describes generation rather than the full density evolution when transport or runaway-electron losses are present. The [volume-averaged hot-tail source rate](name:volume_averaged_runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_hot_tail) is one mechanism-specific contribution to this total.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: volume_averaged_total_xenon_fraction
worked.description_before: Volume-averaged density of xenon summed over all charge states divided by volume-averaged electron density.
worked.description_after: Volume-averaged density of xenon summed over all charge states divided by volume-averaged electron density.

worked.name: volume_averaged_tritium_density
worked.description_before: Volume-averaged number density of tritium ions over the confined plasma volume, obtained from the local charge-state-summed fuel-ion density.
worked.description_after: Number density of tritium ions summed over positive charge states, excluding neutral atoms, averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface.
worked.documentation_before:
Volume-averaged tritium ion number density quantifies the mean concentration of hydrogen-3 fuel ions throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the spatial average of the local [tritium_density](name:tritium_density), rather than a chord average such as [line_averaged_tritium_density](name:line_averaged_tritium_density).

$$
\overline{n}_T = \frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_T\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_T$ is the volume-averaged tritium ion number density, $n_T$ is the local tritium ion number density, $V_c$ is the confined plasma volume bounded by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is the volume element. The tritium ion density is summed over all ionic charge states and excludes neutral tritium. This quantity provides the tritium-density basis for volume-averaged isotopic ratios and is distinct from the local boundary value [tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary).
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of tritium. The average determines the tritium-ion inventory through

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the total number of tritium ions within the averaging volume, $V$ is the confined plasma volume, $n_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the local [tritium density](name:tritium_density), and $\langle n_{\mathrm{T}}\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged value.

This is a single-species particle number density, not an all-species total, electric charge density, or mass density. It is a volume mean rather than a local value or a chord mean. It is the tritium-specific instance of [volume-averaged ion density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density).

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: volume_averaged_tungsten_density
worked.description_before: Volume-averaged number density of positively charged tungsten ions within the plasma enclosed by the last closed flux surface, summed over all ionization states.
worked.description_after: Number density of tungsten ions in all positive charge states, excluding neutral atoms, averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface.
worked.documentation_before:
Volume-averaged tungsten-ion density is the spatial mean of the local charge-state-summed density tungsten-ion density over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface. It includes all positive tungsten ionization states and excludes neutral tungsten.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{W}} \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}}\int_{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}} n_{\mathrm{W}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{W}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local tungsten-ion density, $V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is the enclosed plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ denotes position, and $dV$ is the volume element. The local density is the sum of the densities of all tungsten charge states from W$^{1+}$ through W$^{74+}$.

This quantity is distinct from the boundary flux-surface-averaged tungsten density and from the impurity-abundance [ratio of volume-averaged tungsten density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_tungsten_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), which is normalized to electron density.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of tungsten. Its relation to the local [tungsten density](name:tungsten_density) is

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{W}}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_{\mathrm{W}}\,dV
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{W}}$ is the local tungsten-ion number density, $\langle n_{\mathrm{W}}\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged number density, $V$ is the nonzero confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is a volume element.

Both thermal and nonthermal tungsten ions contribute. Each ion contributes one particle, without electric-charge or mass weighting. This is a single-species number density, not an all-species total, charge density, or mass density. Its volume weighting distinguishes it from [line-averaged tungsten density](name:line_averaged_tungsten_density), which averages along a specified chord.

This quantity is the tungsten-specific instance of [volume-averaged ion density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density). Multiplying it by the confined plasma volume gives the number of tungsten ions within that volume. It is also the numerator of the [ratio of volume-averaged tungsten density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_tungsten_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

worked.name: volume_averaged_xenon_density
worked.description_before: Number density of xenon ions averaged over the full plasma volume, including all charged xenon ionization states and excluding neutral xenon.
worked.description_after: Number density of xenon ions summed over all charge states, excluding neutral atoms, and averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface.
worked.documentation_before:
The volume-averaged xenon ion number density is the plasma-wide mean of the local [xenon_density](name:xenon_density), which sums xenon ions from singly ionized through fully stripped xenon and excludes neutral atoms.

$$
\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Xe}} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_{\mathrm{Xe}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the volume-averaged xenon ion density, $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local xenon ion density at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V_p$ is the full plasma volume, and $dV$ is the physical volume element. The averaging is over the plasma volume rather than along a measurement chord or at a single locus. The resulting global impurity-content measure can be compared with electron content through the ratio of volume-averaged xenon density to volume-averaged electron density.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of xenon. Its relation to the local [xenon density](name:xenon_density) is

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Xe}}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_{\mathrm{Xe}}\,dV
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the local xenon-ion number density, $\langle n_{\mathrm{Xe}}\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged value, $V$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is a volume element.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded. Both thermal and nonthermal xenon ions contribute. Each ion contributes one particle without weighting by electric charge or mass. This is a xenon-only particle number density, not an all-species total, electric charge density, or mass density. It is a volume mean rather than a local value or a chord mean.

Multiplying this average by the confined plasma volume gives the total number of xenon ions within that volume. The [volume-averaged argon density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density) applies the same averaging definition to argon instead of xenon.

The volume average is the integral of a quantity over a stated volume divided by that volume.

worked.name: xenon_density
worked.description_before: Number density of xenon ions at a given point in the plasma, summed over all ionization states from singly ionized through fully stripped xenon, excluding neutral xenon atoms.
worked.description_after: Number density of xenon ions across all positive charge states, excluding neutral xenon, expressing their concentration per physical plasma volume.
worked.documentation_before:
Xenon is a high-$Z$ noble-gas impurity (atomic number $Z_\mathrm{Xe} = 54$) introduced into fusion plasmas for radiative-mantle experiments, impurity-transport studies, and disruption mitigation. The xenon ion number density $n_\mathrm{Xe}$ quantifies the local concentration of all charged xenon species and enters the plasma effective charge through $Z_\mathrm{eff} = \sum_i Z_i^2 n_i / n_e$, where $n_i$ is the partial density of ion species $i$ and $n_e$ is the electron density.

The total xenon ion density is the sum over all ionic charge states:

$$
n_\mathrm{Xe} = \sum_{z=1}^{54} n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{z+}}$ is the partial number density of xenon ions carrying charge $ze$. The charge-state distribution is determined by coronal equilibrium or collisional-radiative modeling at the local electron temperature and density.

The xenon density profile is inferred from vacuum-ultraviolet or soft-X-ray line emission via spectroscopy and tomographic inversion, or from charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy using neutral-beam injection. Spatially resolved forms include [xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis) at the innermost flux surface and xenon_density_at_pedestal in the edge transport barrier, while [volume_averaged_xenon_density](name:volume_averaged_xenon_density) provides the global impurity content figure of merit. The dimensionless impurity fraction relative to electron density is given by xenon_fraction.
worked.documentation_after:
Number density of xenon. The corresponding local density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe}} = \int f_{\mathrm{Xe}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the local xenon-ion number density, $f_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the velocity-space number distribution of the counted xenon-ion population, $\mathbf{v}$ is ion velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The integral covers all velocities.

No particular location or spatial averaging operation is specified. [Xenon density at the plasma boundary](name:xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary) selects a local boundary value. [Line-averaged xenon density](name:line_averaged_xenon_density) averages this concentration along a specified plasma chord, whereas [volume-averaged xenon density](name:volume_averaged_xenon_density) averages it over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface. These averages remain number densities, distinct from line-integrated density or a total ion count.

The density counts ions summed over all charge states; neutral atoms are excluded.

rename_candidates.name: fast_neutral_density
rename_candidates.detail: the name selects a neutral population, which the bare-species sentence would misstate; per the lead ruling the name needs a rename with its source evidence and its text is left alone here
source_texts: Array of values for density fast.

Number density of fast (non-thermal) neutral particles (n_fast) of a given neutral species as a 1D radial profile, summed over charge states. Represents suprathermal neutrals in both the closed field line region and SOL.

rename_candidates.name: fast_neutral_internal_state_number_density

source_texts: Density of fast (non-thermal) neutral particles for a specific neutral species and internal state, resolved along the 1D SOL radial profile. Captures the suprathermal neutral population distinct from the bulk thermal distribution.

Number density of fast (non-thermal) neutral particles (n_fast) for a given neutral species in a specific internal state, as a 1D radial profile. Represents the non-Maxwellian neutral population in a defined energy, excitation, or charge state.

rename_candidates.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_number_density
rename_candidates.detail: the name selects a single-charge-state population, which the bare-species sentence would misstate; per the lead ruling the name needs a rename with its source evidence and its text is left alone here
source_texts: Thermal particle number density (n_thermal) of a given ion charge state, representing the density of ions in thermodynamic equilibrium with the bulk plasma. Radial profile resolved by ion species and charge state.

Thermal particle density (n_thermal) of a given ion charge state in 1D edge/SOL profiles. Represents the number density of the thermalized (non-fast) ion population for the specified ionization state.

rename_candidates.name: thermal_neutral_density
rename_candidates.detail: the name selects a neutral population, which the bare-species sentence would misstate; per the lead ruling the name needs a rename with its source evidence and its text is left alone here
source_texts: Thermal number density (n_thermal) of a neutral species in the core plasma as a 1D radial profile, summed over all charge states. Characterizes the thermal neutral population from recycling, charge exchange, and atomic processes.

Thermal number density (n_thermal) of a neutral species in the edge/SOL region as a 1D radial profile, summed over all charge states. Represents the density of neutrals in thermal equilibrium, excluding fast (non-thermal) components.

rename_candidates.name: thermal_neutral_internal_state_density
rename_candidates.detail: the name selects a neutral population, which the bare-species sentence would misstate; per the lead ruling the name needs a rename with its source evidence and its text is left alone here
source_texts: Number density of thermal (Maxwellian) neutral particles (n_thermal) for a specific neutral species and state as a 1D radial profile in the edge/SOL. Distinguishes the thermal component from the total neutral density and the fast (non-thermal) neutral component.

Number density of thermal neutral particles (n_thermal) as a radial profile in the core plasma. Distinguishes the thermal (Maxwellian) population from fast or suprathermal neutrals within the neutral species state.

rename_candidates.name: total_neutral_number_density
rename_candidates.detail: the name selects a neutral population, which the bare-species sentence would misstate; per the lead ruling the name needs a rename with its source evidence and its text is left alone here
source_texts: Total neutral species number density (thermal plus non-thermal), summed over charge states, as a 1D radial profile in the edge and SOL region. Characterizes the neutral particle population in the scrape-off layer.

Total neutral particle number density (thermal + non-thermal, summed over charge states) as a 2D fluctuating field on the poloidal plane grid. Represents the combined neutral population density for a given neutral species in a turbulence simulation.
